q: בת 86, התקבלה למחלקת סיעוד מורכב עקב פצע לחץ דרגה 4 עמוק ומזוהם באזור הסאקרום. קיבלה טיפול מקומי בפצע באמצעות ניקוי והסרת הרקמות הנימקיות. כעבור שבועיים עדיין הפרשה מרובה עם ריח אופנסיבי, סימני צלוליטיס מסביב, ללא חום סיסטמי. בספירת דם 13,000 לויקוציטים, CRP = 24.5 (תקין עד 0.5). נלקח מטוש לתרבית עם צמיחה של Pseudomonas aeruginosa ו- Providencia. מה הטיפול המתאים במצב זה?
o: טיפול מקומי בפצע בלבד. אין צורך בטיפול אנטיביוטי
אנטיביוטיקה רחבת טווח
טיפול אנטיביוטי סיסטמי מותאם לרגישות החיידקים שצמחו
הטיפול ב VAC (לחץ שלילי) הוא טיפול הבחירה בפצע מזוהם
explanation:
Spreading cellulitis around a deep pressure injury indicates infection beyond the open wound. Leukocytosis, high inflammatory markers and worsening purulent drainage warrant systemic treatment even when an older patient is afebrile.

**Start broad systemic antibiotics and obtain a suitable deep specimen.** A drainage swab can grow colonizing flora as well as invasive pathogens, so use reliable culture findings to narrow the regimen.

**A. Local treatment alone.** Debridement and dressings remain important. They cannot treat cellulitis extending beyond the wound.
**B. Broad-spectrum antibiotics.** Deep pressure wounds may contain gram-positive, gram-negative and anaerobic organisms. Empiric cover is appropriate while clarifying the pathogens and extent of infection.
**C. Treat only the swab isolates.** Pseudomonas and Providencia in a surface sample may omit invasive organisms. Tissue sampling gives a better basis for targeted treatment.
**D. Negative pressure alone.** Negative pressure can help manage selected wounds after debridement. It cannot replace systemic therapy for spreading cellulitis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 695, 697. WHS pressure ulcer guidelines, 2023 update, guideline 6.3.

q: בת 75, עצמאית בתפקודה, מעשנת כבדה. אובחנה כסובלת מ- CAROTID ARTERY STENOSIS עקב ממצא מקרי של אוושה בצוואר בבדיקה גופנית. בדופלקס נמצא חסימה של 80%. מה הטיפול במצבה?
o: התחלת טיפול בסטטינים רק במידה ויש לה היפרליפידמיה
ניתוח carotid endarterectomy
שינוי אורחות חיים כולל הפסקת עישון ומעקב לחצי שנה
צנתור וסטנט לעורק הקרוטידי
explanation:
An incidental bruit with 80% carotid stenosis and no reported ipsilateral ischemic symptoms calls for **intensive medical prevention and individualized assessment for revascularization**. Endarterectomy was a historical option for selected high-grade stenosis. The percentage alone does not select it for this 75-year-old.

**A. Statin only for high lipids.** Established carotid atherosclerosis warrants intensive lipid lowering regardless of a previous hyperlipidemia label.
**B. Endarterectomy.** In the CREST-2 surgical trial, the four-year composite outcome occurred in 3.7% with surgery plus intensive medical therapy and 5.3% with medical therapy alone. The difference was not statistically significant.
**C. Lifestyle and surveillance.** Smoking cessation is essential, but the medical plan also includes lipid lowering, blood-pressure control and appropriate antiplatelet therapy.
**D. Carotid stenting.** In the separate CREST-2 stenting trial, events fell from 6.0% to 2.8%. The trials did not compare stenting directly with surgery. Consider procedural expertise, anatomy and risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1213–1214. CREST-2, N Engl J Med, 2026, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2508800.
Key note: Modern CREST-2 data did not demonstrate a significant four-year advantage for endarterectomy over intensive medical treatment in asymptomatic high-grade stenosis. An 80% incidental lesion does not automatically warrant surgery.

q: בת 92, מאושפזת במחלקת אורתופדיה לאחר ניתוח תיקון שבר צוואר ירך. ברקע: דמנציה, מטופלת ב- DONEPEZIL. במהלך הבתר ניתוחי הצוות שמו לב שהיא ישנונית, אינה מתמצאת בזמן או במקום, מתקשה לבצע הוראות של צוות פיזיותרפיה. יש תנודות במצב ההכרה ובמצב הקוגניטיבי במהלך היום. ביום השני לאחר הניתוח – הוצא צנתר משלפוחית השתן. מעקב שארית שתן- ללא שארית. עקב ניסיון לתלוש את העירוי, ידיה של המטופלת נקשרו. אילו מבין הגורמים הבאים תורם לתסמונת ממנה היא סובלת כעת?
o: פיזיותרפיה בעיתוי מוקדם מדי לאחר הניתוח
הוצאת הצנתר מכיס השתן
קשירה של הידיים
תגובה ממושכת לתרופות אינדוקציה סביב הניתוח
explanation:
Baseline dementia increases vulnerability. Hospital exposures that restrict movement can further precipitate or prolong delirium.
**Tying her wrists is a recognized, modifiable precipitant.**

**A. Early physical therapy.** Appropriate assisted mobility helps prevent functional decline and delirium.
**B. Removing the catheter.** With satisfactory bladder emptying, removing this tether supports mobility.
**C. Tying her hands.** Restraints restrict movement and may increase fear, struggling and injury.
**D. Prolonged induction-drug effect.** Perioperative medication deserves review, but the vignette gives no evidence of ongoing induction-drug effect. It directly describes a validated precipitant.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 888, Tables 58-1 and 58-5

q: בן 78, ימני, התקבל למחלקת שיקום גריאטרי לאחר שבץ בטריטוריה של Rt. Middle cerebral artery. מה הממצאים הצפויים פרט לפלגיה משמאל?
o: aphasia
סטיית מבט לשמאל
neglect
חרשות באוזן ימין
explanation:
The right middle cerebral artery supplies cortex involved in spatial attention. **Left spatial neglect** can accompany left hemiplegia after a right MCA infarction in a right-handed patient.

**A. Aphasia.** Language is usually left-dominant in a right-handed person.
**B. Leftward gaze.** A destructive right frontal eye-field lesion generally favors gaze toward the right.
**C. Neglect.** The patient may ignore people, objects or body parts on the left.
**D. Right-sided deafness.** Unilateral peripheral hearing loss is not a typical right MCA sign.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 958.

q: בת 75, ברקע אי ספיקת לב, סוכרת, יתר לחץ דם, וזיהומים חוזרים בדרכי השתן עם טיפול אנטיביוטי מניעתי. פונה למרפאה בגין קשיי נשימה שהתחילו בצורה הדרגתית. בבדיקתה – סטורציה נמוכה, בהאזנה לריאות – קרפיטציות עדינות דו צדדיות בסוף אינספיריום. לאיזה מהתרופות שמקבלת יכול להיות קשר למחלתה?
o: AMLODIPINE
METFORMIN
SPIRONOLACTONE
NITOFURANTOIN
explanation:
Nitrofurantoin can cause chronic interstitial lung injury during prolonged treatment for recurrent urinary infections. Gradual dyspnea, hypoxemia and fine end-inspiratory crackles make **nitrofurantoin toxicity** a concern in this woman. Heart failure remains another possible cause.

**A. Amlodipine.** Arteriolar dilation commonly causes dependent ankle edema. This effect poorly explains hypoxemia with inspiratory crackles.
**B. Metformin.** Metformin-associated lactic acidosis can cause rapid, deep breathing. Fine crackles point toward disease within the lungs.
**C. Spironolactone.** This drug treats heart failure and can raise potassium. Worsening heart failure itself could account for pulmonary congestion.
**D. Nitrofurantoin.** Long-term urinary prophylaxis supplies the relevant exposure. Suspected lung toxicity warrants stopping nitrofurantoin and assessing other causes of dyspnea.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1708. Macrodantin prescribing information, Pulmonary Reactions.

q: בת 60, סובלת בחודשים האחרונים משינויים קוגניטיביים ושינויים התנהגותיים. מדברת באופן בוטה, לא מתעניינת בדברים שעינינו אותה בעבר, חוזרת פעמים רבות על אותם משפטים. בבדיקה הקוגניטיבית בולטת פגיעה בתפקודים הניהוליים (Executive functions) והזיכרון יחסית שמור. מה הממצא ההדמייתי האופייני במצב זה?
o: MRI מוח יראה ירידה בנפח המוח
CT אנגיוגרפיה יראה אוטמים מרובים ופגיעה ווסקולרית
מיפוי PET FDG יראה ירידה במטבוליזם באונות הפרונטליות
CT יראה נפח חדרים מוגבר עם השטחה של הסולקים
explanation:
Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia affects networks governing inhibition, initiative and executive function. **Frontal hypometabolism on FDG-PET** fits the behavioral change with relatively preserved memory.

**A. Reduced overall volume.** Generalized atrophy is nonspecific.
**B. Multiple infarcts.** These favor vascular injury when they explain the clinical deficits.
**C. Frontal hypometabolism.** Preferential frontal involvement fits disinhibition, apathy and stereotyped speech.
**D. Ventriculomegaly with tight sulci.** This suggests a hydrocephalus pattern and does not explain the characteristic behavioral syndrome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 989.

q: אילו מבין השינויים הבאים של ההזדקנות קשורים להתמודדות אדם זקן עם COPD?
o: עליה ב- cardiac output
ירידה ב- peripheral vascular resistance
ירידה בלחץ בעורקי הריאה
סיכון מוגבר לאוסטאופורוזיס
explanation:
**Osteoporosis** is an important COPD comorbidity, and musculoskeletal impairment adds to age-related functional decline. Systemic inflammation, deconditioning, and other factors contribute; a single unproven mechanism should not be assigned to every patient (pp. 1241–1242).

**A. Increased cardiac output.** Wrong, aging is not described as increasing cardiac output: peak-exercise output declines, and the aging–COPD table describes further reduction with COPD (pp. 1121, 1242).
**B. Decreased peripheral vascular resistance.** Wrong, age-related arterial stiffness accompanies increased peripheral resistance, not the proposed decrease (p. 1242, Table 81-3).
**C. Decreased pulmonary artery pressure.** Wrong, pulmonary vascular loss and hypoxic vasoconstriction in COPD may increase pulmonary pressure; a decrease is not the described effect (p. 1241).
**D. Increased osteoporosis risk.** Correct, age-related bone loss adds to osteoporosis among COPD comorbidities, impairing musculoskeletal capacity and mobility (pp. 1241–1242).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1121, 1241–1242.

q: בת 70, מתלוננת כי מספר שנים סובלת מרעד בשתי הידיים ובראש אשר החמיר לאחרונה. אינה מסוגלת להשתמש בכף כדי לאכול מרק, כיוון הנוזל נשפך מהכף. שתיית אלכוהול מקלה על הרעד ואילו מתח נפשי מחמיר אותו. בבדיקה מדובר ברעד דו צדדי (יד ימין ויד שמאל) סימטרי בחומרתו, רעד בראש ושאר הבדיקה הנוירולוגית תקינה. מה הטיפול המומלץ לרעד?
o: LEVODOPA+CARBIDOPA (DOPICAR)
Beta blockers
Calcium channel blockers
AMANTADINE
explanation:
Essential tremor appears when the hands hold a posture or perform a task, such as carrying a spoon. Bilateral hand tremor, head involvement and temporary improvement after alcohol fit this pattern.

**A beta blocker such as propranolol can reduce the disabling hand tremor.** The treatment target is her ability to eat without spilling.

**A. Levodopa with carbidopa.** This treats parkinsonian slowness and rigidity. Neither accompanies her action tremor.
**B. Beta blockers.** Propranolol is an established initial treatment for limb tremor when essential tremor interferes with daily activities.
**C. Calcium channel blockers.** They are not standard initial therapy for disabling essential tremor. Evidence for individual agents is weaker than for propranolol.
**D. Amantadine.** Its usual role here would be in Parkinson disease, particularly levodopa-induced dyskinesia. Her difficulty is a rhythmic action tremor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 146, 940, 944. American Academy of Neurology, Treatment of Essential Tremor guideline update, 2011.
explanationReviewNote: The source supports identifying essential tremor from this presentation; reaching beta-blocker treatment also requires an essential-tremor treatment recommendation, which it does not state.

q: בת 84, עצמאית בתפקודה וללא ירידה קוגניטיבית ידועה. ברקע סוכרת ויתר לחץ דם. מה צריך לכלול הטיפול בסוכרת על פי המאמר Older Adults: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes 2020?
o: איזון סוכרת עם המוגלובין A1C מתחת ל- 7.5% והערכה קוגניטיבית אחת לשנה
איזון סוכרת עם המוגלובין A1C מתחת ל-7% ואיזון לחץ דם מתחת ל- 130/80
איזון סוכרת עם ערכי גלוקוז בצום 100-200 ומתן טיפול בסטטינים
איזון סוכרת עם ערכי גלוקוז בצום 70-100 ובדיקת גילוי מוקדם לכף רגל סוכרתית
explanation:
Cognition affects a person's ability to take medicines, monitor glucose and respond to a low. Independence in daily life does not rule out early difficulty with those tasks.

**An A1C goal below 7.5% and annual cognitive assessment fit this independent patient.** The 2020 recommendation calls for screening at the initial visit from age 65 and annually as appropriate.

**A. A1C below 7.5% with yearly cognitive assessment.** This combination addresses both healthy-category glycemic goals and the safety of self-management.
**B. A1C below 7% with BP below 130/80.** Both values are more intensive than the healthy-category defaults in ADA 2020.
**C. Fasting 100–200 with a statin.** A statin may be appropriate, but the healthy-category fasting range is 90–130 mg/dL.
**D. Fasting 70–100 with foot screening.** Foot examination helps prevent ulcers. The proposed fasting range is unnecessarily low and narrow.

Reference · ADA, Older Adults, 2020, recommendation 12.3 and Table 12.1 (S153–S155).
ref: Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes—2020

q: בת 96, סובלת מדמנציה. גרה בבית עם מטפלת 24 שעות. החולה הולכת עם הליכון בהשגחה. לפני שנתיים חוותה שבץ מוחי ומאז סובלת מחולשת פלג גוף ימין קלה. החולה נפלה שלוש פעמים בשנה החולפת. בבדיקה גופנית לחץ הדם בשכיבה הוא 145/80 ממ"כ, ולאחר שלוש דקות עמידה הוא 110/65 ממ"כ. לחולה מספר גורמי סיכון לנפילות. לאיזה גורם סיכון הקשר החלש ביותר לנפילות?
o: גיל מבוגר
אורתוסטטיזם
שבץ בעבר
ירידה קוגניטיבית
explanation:
Official answer: ב

Table 43-1 ranks the **strength of evidence** associating factors with falls. Orthostatic hypotension has weak evidence, whereas advanced age, stroke and dementia have strong evidence; this does not quantify the individual patient’s risk (p. 635).
"weak evidence (occasionally but not usually found)" (Table 43-1 footnote, p. 635).

**A. Advanced age.** Wrong, the table assigns strong, consistent evidence, rather than the weakest category among these factors (p. 635).
**B. Orthostatic hypotension.** Correct, it has the weakest evidence category among these four. This does not make the measured blood-pressure fall clinically unimportant in this patient (p. 635).
**C. Previous stroke.** Wrong, stroke has strong evidence, unlike orthostatic hypotension (p. 635).
**D. Cognitive impairment.** Wrong, dementia and impaired cognition have strong evidence, so they are not the weakest category requested (p. 635).

Orthostatic hypotension is the official answer to the wording “weakest association.” Read this as strength and consistency of evidence, not a comparative risk ratio.
Source versus explanation: "Strong evidence (consistently found in high-quality studies)" (Table 43-1 footnote, p. 635).
Note: The question does not specify whether “weakest” means consistency of evidence or effect size. The table supports the former interpretation.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 635.

q: בת 85, הסובלת מסרטן גרורתי ודמנציה מתקדמת הוכרזה כחולה נוטה למות שאינה כשירה. בברור רצונה נמצא כי תוקף ייפוי הכוח עליו חתמה ובו מינתה את שכנתה, פג לפני שנתיים, אך לאחרונה מונה לה אפוטרופוס מטעם המדינה. מי צריך להיות מקבל ההחלטה בעניין הטיפול בסוף החיים?
o: האפוטרופוס
אחייניתה שהינה קרובת המשפחה היחידה שלה
הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם השכנה
הרופא האחראי בהתייעצות עם האפוטרופוס
explanation:
ייפוי כוח לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות מאפשר לאדם לקבוע מי יבטא את רצונו כשיאבד את כשירותו. **הרופא האחראי מברר את רצון המטופלת, מעיין בייפוי הכוח שפג ויכול להיעזר בשכנה אם היא מכירה את רצונה**.

**א. האפוטרופוס לבדו.** עצם המינוי אינו מעניק לאפוטרופוס סמכות בלעדית להכריע בטיפול בסוף החיים.
**ב. האחיינית.** קרבת משפחה כשלעצמה אינה מוכיחה שהאחיינית יודעת מה רצתה המטופלת.
**ג. הרופא האחראי והשכנה.** המסמך שפג אינו מחייב. יש לעיין בו, ועדות השכנה כאדם קרוב יכולה לסייע אם מתקיימים תנאי החוק.
**ד. הרופא האחראי והאפוטרופוס.** יש לבחון את תפקידו ואת קרבתו למטופלת לפי החוק. עצם המינוי מטעם המדינה אינו מקנה לעמדתו עדיפות אוטומטית.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, התשס״ו–2005, סעיפים 5(ג), 29 ו־39(ב).

q: מה הייחוד של טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה מטיפול פליאטיבי בחולים אונקולוגים?
o: בחולי דמנציה אין צורך בטיפול בכאב היות והשכיחות של כאב היא נמוכה
טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה יכול התבצע בצורה טובה על ידי הצוות המטפל ואין חשיבות להכנסה של מומחים בטיפול פליאטיבי
חולי דמנציה מתקדמת סובלים מנטל סימפטומים גופניים משמעותי ובזה אינם שונים מחולים אונקולוגים
שילוב של טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה חשוב רק בשלבים המתקדמים של המחלה
explanation:
Palliative care addresses symptoms and stress regardless of diagnosis. **Advanced dementia can produce substantial physical symptom burden, as can cancer**, including pain, swallowing problems, infections and weight loss.

**A. Pain treatment unnecessary.** Impaired communication can conceal pain. Observe behavior and offer appropriate analgesia.
**B. Specialist input unimportant.** Primary teams provide palliative care, and complex symptoms may benefit from specialist help.
**C. Substantial symptoms in both.** Comparable burden does not require identical symptom patterns.
**D. Only advanced dementia.** Earlier conversations can clarify goals before communication declines.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1047–1048, 1071.

q: הוזמן ייעוץ שיקומי לבן 79 המאושפז במחלקה כירורגית לאחר כריתת כיס מרה דחופה. החולה מוזן כעת בזונדה, משתף פעולה חלקית בפיזיותרפיה ובבדיקה נמצא פצע לחץ דרגה 3 בעכוז. במעבדה- לויקוציטים 11,400, CRP-13. מה ההמלצה להמשך שיקום לחולה זה?
o: בשל פצע לחץ דרגה 3 מתאים למחלקה לסיעוד מורכב בלבד
לצורך קבלתו למחלקת שיקום יש לגמול אותו קודם מזונדה
יש להמתין עד להתנרמלות מדדי דלקת ואז לקבלו לשיקום
ניתן לקבלו למחלקה שיקומית בתנאי שמסכים ומשתף פעולה בטיפול
explanation:
לאחר ניתוח בודקים אם קיימת מחלה חריפה שמונעת מאמץ ואם המטופל מסוגל להשתתף בשיקום. רמת CRP וספירת לויקוציטים הן חלק מההערכה לצד התסמינים, הבדיקה ומגמת השינוי.

**אפשר לקבלו אם הוא יציב, מסכים ומשתף פעולה. אם יש זיהום פעיל שמונע מאמץ, ממתינים להתייצבות ומעריכים מחדש.**

**A. סיעוד מורכב בלבד בגלל פצע לחץ.** פצע דרגה 3 דורש טיפול והפחתת לחץ. הוא אינו מחייב לשלול שיקום אם ניתן להתאמן בלי לפגוע בריפויו.
**B. גמילה מזונדה כתנאי לקבלה.** אפשר לשקם אדם המוזן בזונדה אם מצבו יציב וההזנה אינה מפריעה לתוכנית הטיפול.
**C. המתנה להתנרמלות מדדי דלקת.** דחייה מתאימה כאשר זיהום חריף מונע השתתפות. CRP ולויקוציטים יכולים להישאר מוגברים גם אחרי שיפור קליני, ולכן חזרה לערכי תקין אינה תנאי סף.
**D. קבלה בהסכמה ובשיתוף פעולה.** בהנחה של יציבות רפואית, בודקים אם שיתוף הפעולה החלקי מספיק למטרות מעשיות ומתאימים את התוכנית ליכולתו.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר מינהל רפואה 4/2009, סעיפים 5.2–5.4, עמ׳ 4.

Key note: לצד קבלה בשיתוף פעולה התקבלה גם האפשרות להמתין להתנרמלות מדדי הדלקת. סעיף 5.2 קובע הערכה חוזרת לאחר חלוף מחלה חריפה שמונעת מאמץ שיקומי ואינו דורש נרמול מעבדתי.
ref: משרד הבריאות — אמות מידה למתן טיפול שיקומי לקשישים
keySource: IMA 2021-Dec Subspecialty official answer key, Q97

explanationSource.status: Official accepted answer first; separately attributed book and secondary sources.

explanationReviewNote: The source supports rehabilitation when medical stability and participation permit it despite tube feeding or a pressure injury; reaching mandatory normalization of inflammatory markers also requires that laboratory threshold, which it does not state.

q: בת 88 פנתה למיון עקב שקיעה במצב ההכרה. לפני שבוע נפלה ונחבלה וסבלה מכאבים קשים. המשפחה יודעת שהחולה לקחה תכשירים שונים לשיכוך כאב, ולאחר מכן הפכה להיות שקועה. המשפחה מביאה שקית עם תרופות אנלגטיות שונות אותן החולה לקחה בבית בשבוע האחרון. מי מבין התרופות האנלגטיות הבאות יכולה לגרום בסבירות גבוהה לשקיעה הכרתית?
o: ACAMOL FOCUS (PARACETAMOL, ASPIRIN, CAFFEINE)
COMBODEX (PARACETAMOL, IBUPROFEN)
MUSCOL (PARACETAMOL, ORPHENADRINE)
DIPYRONE (OPTALGIN)
explanation:
An over-the-counter analgesic may contain another drug with central effects. Check every ingredient when consciousness changes after several new products.
**Muscol contains orphenadrine, a strongly anticholinergic muscle relaxant that can impair cognition and cause sedation.**

**A. Paracetamol, aspirin and caffeine.** None supplies the strong anticholinergic muscle relaxant found in Muscol.
**B. Paracetamol and ibuprofen.** Assess dose and NSAID toxicity, but this combination lacks the centrally anticholinergic ingredient.
**C. Paracetamol and orphenadrine.** Orphenadrine makes depressed alertness particularly plausible. The recent fall also warrants assessment for head injury.
**D. Dipyrone.** This analgesic lacks orphenadrine. Its other adverse effects follow a different mechanism.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–883, Table 58-2. AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Table 7, p. 2074

q: מה מאפיין את הזקנים בארץ מבחינה פסיכו-סוציאלית לפי לקט הנתונים האינפוגרפי של השנתון הסטטיסטי?
o: אחוז בני 65+ בקרב הרוגים ופצועים קשה בתאונות דרכים גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה
קופת חולים מכבי היא בעלת אחוז הזקנים הגבוה ביותר
כ- 8% מבני 75 ומעלה שוהים במוסד
רוב הנשים בנות 70 ומעלה מקבלות "גמלת סיעוד"
explanation:
יש להשוות **אותה אוכלוסייה ואותו מכנה**: חלקם של מבוגרים בכלל האוכלוסייה מול חלקם בנפגעי תאונות קשות, ושיעור מקבלות גמלת סיעוד מתוך כלל הנשים בקבוצת הגיל. כאן הבדיקה נשענת על שנתון 2024 שברשימת הקריאה; אין זו בדיקה ישירה של המהדורה ההיסטורית שנבחנה (עמ׳ 34, 36–37, 41–42, 63).

**א. אחוז בני 65+ בקרב הרוגים ופצועים קשה בתאונות דרכים גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה.** נכונה, האינפוגרפיקה קובעת במפורש כי חלקם של בני 65 ומעלה בהרוגים ובפצועים קשה גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה; זהו ייצוג־יתר, בלי צורך להמציא סיבות שלא נבדקו בעמוד (עמ׳ 36).
**ב. קופת חולים מכבי היא בעלת אחוז הזקנים הגבוה ביותר.** שגויה, בתרשים שיעור המבוגרים מבין מבוטחי כל קופה גבוה יותר בכללית מאשר במכבי; יש להבחין בין שיעור בתוך קופה לבין חלוקת כלל המבוגרים בין הקופות (עמ׳ 37).
**ג. כ- 8% מבני 75 ומעלה שוהים במוסד.** שגויה, שיעור השוהים במוסד בשתי קבוצות הגיל המרכיבות את בני 75 ומעלה נמוך מן השיעור שבאפשרות; גם ממוצע משוקלל שלהן אינו מגיע אליו (עמ׳ 42).
**ד. רוב הנשים בנות 70 ומעלה מקבלות "גמלת סיעוד".** שגויה, השיעור עולה עם הגיל, אך אין להחיל את שיעור הקבוצה המבוגרת ביותר על כל הנשים בנות 70 ומעלה. כהסקה חישובית, שקלול השיעורים לפי קבוצות הגיל בתרשים באמצעות מבנה אוכלוסיית הנשים אינו מצביע על רוב; החישוב משתמש בנתונים מעוגלים ולכן אינו מוצג כשיעור מדויק (עמ׳ 41, 63).

א׳ נתמכת במהדורה המקומית המאוחרת: בני 65 ומעלה מהווים 21% מההרוגים ו־19% מהפצועים קשה בתאונות דרכים, ושיעורם בקבוצות אלה גדול מחלקם באוכלוסייה. זהו אימות לפי שנתון 2024, ולא אימות המספרים בשנתון ההיסטורי שנבחן (בני 65+ בישראל, שנתון 2024, עמ׳ מודפס 36).

אפשרות ב שגויה: בשנתון 2024, עמ׳ מודפס 37, שיעור בני 65+ מכלל מבוטחי הקופה גבוה ביותר בכללית (14%), לעומת מכבי (13%); אלו נתוני מהדורת 2024, ולא אימות של המספרים במהדורת הבחינה הישנה.

מקור: שנור י, דוידוביץ נ (עורכים). בני 65+ בישראל, שנתון סטטיסטי 2024, מס׳ 26. מכון מאיירס־ג׳וינט־ברוקדייל, עמ׳ 34, 36–37, 41–42, 63 (לוח 1.2).
referenceNote: Brookdale yearbook: לקט נתונים אינפוגרפי. Examined on an earlier edition; figures may differ from the required 2024 edition.

explanationSource.status: Page-backed supplemental explanation; original IMA bibliography retained.

q: בת 75, אושפזה בשל חשד לדלקת ריאות במחלקה הפנימית, בשל שיעול של כשבועיים. במהלך אשפוזה בוצע CT ריאות, ללא לתסנין, אולם הודגמו ממצאים בבלוטת התריס. תפקודי תריס נלקחו, אשר תקינים. באיזה ממצא בתירואיד יש להמשיך בברור על ידי FNA?
o: יש לדגום כל Multinodular Goiter (MNG) בשל סיכון לממאירות
נודול סולידי (Solid) בגודל של 2 ס"מ, עם מיקרוקלציפיקציות
יש לדגום כל נודול ציסטי (Purely cystic nodules), לשלילת Cystic Carcinoma
גוש "חם" במיפוי תירואיד
explanation:
Thyroid nodule aspiration is based on ultrasound appearance and size. With normal thyroid function, **a 2-cm solid nodule with microcalcifications** warrants FNA because it has suspicious sonographic features.

**A. Sample every multinodular goiter.** Evaluate individual nodules by risk features and size.
**B. Solid nodule with microcalcifications.** Normal thyroid tests do not exclude structural malignancy.
**C. Sample every pure cyst.** A purely cystic nodule lacks a suspicious solid component and generally does not need diagnostic FNA.
**D. Hot nodule.** Hyperfunctioning nodules rarely harbor malignancy and usually do not require cytology.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1555.

q: A 78-year-old man is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three, he becomes agitated, pulls at IV lines, and is disoriented after being oriented that morning. In addition to the acute change, which finding is central to delirium assessment?
o: Disorganized thinking
Inattention
Altered level of consciousness
Hallucinations
explanation:
CAM is a bedside algorithm for recognizing an acute change in cognition. Inattention means losing track of a task or conversation despite efforts to engage.
**Test attention. An acute change plus inattention is required by CAM, with disorganized thinking or altered arousal completing the pattern.**

**A. Disorganized thinking.** Disorganized thinking can complete the algorithm after its two required features are present.
**B. Inattention.** Difficulty sustaining or shifting focus is the required feature to assess here.
**C. Altered level of consciousness.** Altered consciousness can substitute for disorganized thinking, but neither substitutes for inattention.
**D. Hallucinations.** Perceptual disturbances may occur. Many delirious patients have no hallucinations.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 880, 883

q: A 72-year-old woman takes diphenhydramine every night for sleep and reports morning drowsiness. Which explanation is consistent with Hazzard?
o: A short half-life confines the sedating effect to the evening
Tolerance to the sedating effect develops slowly over years
A long half-life contributes to sedation on the following day
Antihistaminergic activity increases alertness after taking the drug
explanation:
Diphenhydramine is a sedating, anticholinergic first-generation antihistamine. **Its prolonged half-life can leave residual sedation the following morning**, especially in older adults.

**A. Short half-life, evening effect only.** Next-day exposure can persist beyond the night.
**B. Tolerance develops over years.** Tolerance to the sedating effect can develop rapidly.
**C. Long half-life, next-day sedation.** This explains morning drowsiness despite taking the drug at bedtime.
**D. Antihistaminergic alertness.** Central H1 blockade promotes sedation, not alertness.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 661.

q: A 68-year-old man is referred for comprehensive geriatric assessment after a recent hospitalization. He is independent in basic activities of daily living but needs help managing medications, paying bills, and shopping. How should his functional status be characterized?
o: Dependent in basic ADLs but independent in IADLs; needs help with self-care
Independent in basic ADLs, dependent in IADLs; needs household assistance
Independent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with recreational activities
Dependent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with feeding and transfers
explanation:
**Basic ADLs** concern self-care, whereas **IADLs** concern maintaining an independent household (p. 123). The latter include shopping, taking medications, and handling finances; needing help with these tasks indicates IADL dependence while the stem explicitly preserves basic self-care independence (p. 123; application to the case). "BADLs refer to self-care tasks such as bathing, dressing, toileting, continence, grooming, feeding, and transferring." (p. 123).

**A. Dependent in basic ADLs but independent in IADLs; needs help with self-care.** Wrong, the deficits described involve household tasks, and the stem states that basic self-care is independent (p. 123; application).
**B. Independent in basic ADLs, dependent in IADLs; needs household assistance.** Correct, medications, finances, and shopping are instrumental tasks, so the distinction matches the reported abilities (p. 123).
**C. Independent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with recreational activities.** Wrong, he already needs help with IADLs; this is not a limitation confined to recreational activities (p. 123).
**D. Dependent in basic ADLs and IADLs; needs help with feeding and transfers.** Wrong, the stem does not describe dependence in feeding or transfers, which are basic ADLs (p. 123).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 123.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A woman is eating little and losing weight because her sense of taste has changed. Which evaluation appears in the dysgeusia branch of the Hazzard weight-loss algorithm?
o: Assess oral health, medications, and zinc deficiency
Assess thyroid disease, diabetes, and a catabolic condition
Assess food access and the need for meal-delivery assistance
Assess depressive symptoms and the need for counseling
explanation:
The weight-loss algorithm links **dysgeusia** to potentially relevant oral, medication, and nutritional factors. Its dysgeusia branch reads, "Poor oral health, drugs? Zinc deficiency?" (p. 427, Figure 30-8). The other evaluations occupy different branches of the algorithm, so they are not the branch requested here.

**A. Assess oral health, medications, and zinc deficiency.** Correct, these are the factors specifically linked to dysgeusia in the figure (p. 427).
**B. Assess thyroid disease, diabetes, and a catabolic condition.** Wrong, thyroid disease and diabetes appear under altered metabolism or catabolism, not under the taste-disturbance branch (p. 427).
**C. Assess food access and the need for meal-delivery assistance.** Wrong, meal delivery and assistance address inadequate access to food in the figure, not the dysgeusia branch (p. 427).
**D. Assess depressive symptoms and the need for counseling.** Wrong, counseling belongs to the depression branch, whereas the stated question asks for the taste-disturbance evaluation (p. 427).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 427.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A 76-year-old woman with dementia has agitation. In which circumstance should antipsychotic treatment be considered according to the approach in Hazzard?
o: Mild symptoms after environmental interventions have been tried
Severe, dangerous symptoms after a nonpharmacologic treatment trial
Mild symptoms before environmental triggers have been investigated
Stable symptoms to prevent a future behavioral deterioration
explanation:
Antipsychotics can reduce some behavioral symptoms in dementia but carry vascular and mortality risks. **Consider treatment for severe, dangerous symptoms after a trial of nonpharmacologic care**.

**A. Mild symptoms after environmental changes.** Mild residual symptoms rarely justify the harms of antipsychotic exposure.
**B. Severe dangerous symptoms.** When practical measures fail, define a target behavior and reassess benefit and harm.
**C. Mild symptoms before assessment.** Pain, fear, overstimulation or other triggers may be readily treatable.
**D. Prevent future deterioration.** Antipsychotic prophylaxis exposes a stable patient without a current treatment target.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 927.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: Which principle describes the weekly high-dose treatment option for severe vitamin D deficiency in Hazzard?
o: Continue high-dose replacement long term instead of changing to maintenance
Use a replacement course followed by a daily maintenance dose
Continue replacement until hypercalciuria appears, then change to maintenance
Start maintenance dosing and increase it when serum calcium rises
explanation:
**Replacement followed by maintenance** is the sequence described for the weekly high-dose option. Hazzard separately identifies hypercalciuria as an early sign of overtreatment, with hypercalcemia occurring subsequently; these are toxicity signals rather than treatment targets. (p. 1540)
"vitamin D2 50,000 IU weekly for 8 to 12 weeks, then vitamin D3 800 to1000 IU daily." (p. 1540)
"The first indication of over-treatment with vitamin D is hypercalciuria which predisposes individuals to nephrolithiasis, and subsequently, hypercalcemia." (p. 1540)

**A. Continue high-dose replacement long term instead of changing to maintenance.** Wrong, the described weekly course is followed by daily vitamin D, rather than continued as the long-term replacement regimen. (p. 1540)
**B. Use a replacement course followed by a daily maintenance dose.** Correct, this preserves the sequence of correcting deficiency and then using a daily maintenance regimen. (p. 1540)
**C. Continue replacement until hypercalciuria appears, then change to maintenance.** Wrong, hypercalciuria is a sign of overtreatment, not the target for ending the replacement course. (p. 1540)
**D. Start maintenance dosing and increase it when serum calcium rises.** Wrong, a rise in calcium is described in the toxicity sequence and is not a reason to escalate treatment. (p. 1540)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1540.
ref: Hazzard Ch 97 — AGING OF THE ENDOCRINE SYSTEM AND NON-THYROID ENDOCRINE DISORDERS
chapterTitle: Aging of the Endocrine System and Non-Thyroid Endocrine Disorders

q: In the Fried frailty phenotype, meeting at least three of five criteria identifies frailty. What underlying process does this model propose?
o: Preserved adaptation to stress despite slower performance of daily activities
Reduced risk of losing independence in the absence of an acute precipitating event
Dysregulated stress responses with loss of capacity to maintain homeostasis
Increased physiologic reserve in response to reduced activity and weight loss
explanation:
The **frailty phenotype** is linked to dysregulation of stress-response systems and loss of homeostatic capacity. Its clinical features represent a cycle of declining energy and reserve, and the severity of frailty predicts disability and loss of independence even without an acute precipitant (p. 619).
"frailty is the result of dysregulation of the stress response systems responsible for organismal resilience, leading to loss of homeostatic capabilities, increased susceptibility to stress," (p. 619).
"the severity of frailty is associated with risk for disability and loss of independence, even in the absence of an acute precipitant." (p. 619).

**A. Preserved adaptation to stress despite slower performance of daily activities.** Wrong, preserved stress adaptation conflicts with the model's dysregulated response systems and increased susceptibility to stress (p. 619).
**B. Reduced risk of losing independence in the absence of an acute precipitating event.** Wrong, frailty is associated with disability and loss of independence even without an acute precipitating event, rather than reduced risk in its absence (p. 619).
**C. Dysregulated stress responses with loss of capacity to maintain homeostasis.** Correct, it matches the proposed dysregulation and loss of homeostatic capability underlying the phenotype (p. 619).
**D. Increased physiologic reserve in response to reduced activity and weight loss.** Wrong, reserve declines in the described pathologic cycle; reduced activity and weight loss do not represent an increase in reserve (p. 619).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 619.

q: A 79-year-old woman taking sertraline reports improvement in mood but continues to lose weight unintentionally. What is the appropriate approach to investigating the weight loss?
o: Attribute the loss to the medication and wait for spontaneous change
Assess dietary intake, underlying disease and remediable factors
Attribute the loss to depression and increase the antidepressant dose
Attribute the loss to age and continue monitoring mood alone
explanation:
Persistent involuntary weight loss can reflect inadequate intake, illness, medication effects or difficulty obtaining and eating food. **Assess diet, underlying disease and reversible barriers** even though mood has improved.

**A. Wait for a drug effect to resolve.** Sertraline deserves review, but attributing the loss to it without assessing other causes delays evaluation.
**B. Evaluate intake and reversible factors.** Establish the weight trajectory and what she actually eats, then investigate potentially treatable causes.
**C. Increase the antidepressant.** Improved mood with continuing weight loss is a reason to broaden the assessment before escalating medication.
**D. Attribute it to age.** Unintentional weight loss is a clinical finding that merits evaluation at any age.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 425.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A 75-year-old man with COPD develops confusion and fatigue over 12 hours. His family says he is unlike his usual self. He is inattentive, lethargic, and less active than usual. Heart rate is 88/min, blood pressure 140/85 mm Hg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 92% on home oxygen. Which interpretation and initial approach fit this presentation?
o: Chronic dementia; assess gradual cognitive progression at follow-up
Hypoactive delirium; investigate and treat acute contributors
Primary depression; prioritize mood treatment before medical evaluation
Hyperactive delirium; prioritize sedation before precipitant evaluation
explanation:
Hypoactive delirium presents with slowing, drowsiness and reduced engagement and is easily missed because the patient is quiet.
**Treat this as hypoactive delirium and look for acute contributors, including respiratory illness, hypoxemia and medication exposure in this patient with COPD.**

**A. Chronic dementia; assess gradual cognitive progression at follow-up.** The change occurred in twelve hours and differs sharply from his usual cognition.
**B. Hypoactive delirium; investigate and treat acute contributors.** Lethargy with abrupt inattention is the quiet motor presentation of delirium.
**C. Primary depression; prioritize mood treatment before medical evaluation.** Fatigue or low mood alone does not explain this abrupt change in attention and arousal.
**D. Hyperactive delirium; prioritize sedation before precipitant evaluation.** His activity is reduced. Sedation could obscure worsening respiratory or mental status.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–885

q: A woman taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation starts ibuprofen for pain. Which medication approach addresses a modifiable bleeding risk?
o: Continue ibuprofen and rely on INR monitoring to address the risk
Avoid the NSAID and assess another approach to pain relief
Increase ibuprofen to permit a reduction in anticoagulant treatment
Replace ibuprofen with regular aspirin for continuing pain relief
explanation:
NSAIDs can increase bleeding risk in patients taking warfarin through gastrointestinal injury and platelet effects. **Avoid ibuprofen when possible and select a safer pain strategy**.

**A. Continue with INR checks.** INR does not measure NSAID-induced mucosal injury or platelet dysfunction.
**B. Avoid the NSAID.** Removing a modifiable interaction reduces bleeding risk without sacrificing indicated anticoagulation.
**C. Increase ibuprofen and lower anticoagulation.** This increases bleeding hazards while reducing stroke protection.
**D. Substitute regular aspirin.** Aspirin also inhibits platelets and can increase bleeding.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1202.

q: על פי הנתונים האפידמיולוגיים הנוכחיים, מהי הסיבה המובילה לתמותה במבוגרים מעל גיל 65?
o: זיהום או אלח דם
דמנציה או מחלת אלצהיימר
מחלת לב
פציעות הקשורות ל-falls
explanation:
התשובה היא **מחלת לב**: בטבלה 2-3 היא הסיבה המובילה לתמותה בקרב בני 65 ומעלה בשנת 2017, עם 25% מכלל מקרי המוות בקבוצה זו (עמ׳ 29).
"Heart disease" — 25% (עמ׳ 29, טבלה 2-3).

**א. זיהום או אלח דם.** שגויה, הטבלה מציבה מחלת לב בראש הרשימה. שפעת ודלקת ריאות מופיעות עם 2.3% מהתמותה; אין בטבלה דירוג של זיהום או אלח דם כסיבה המובילה (עמ׳ 29, טבלה 2-3).
**ב. דמנציה או מחלת אלצהיימר.** שגויה, מחלת אלצהיימר מופיעה בטבלה עם 5.8% מהתמותה, פחות ממחלת לב; אין להסיק שזה שיעור התמותה מכל סוגי הדמנציה (עמ׳ 29, טבלה 2-3).
**ג. מחלת לב.** נכונה, מחלת לב מופיעה עם 519,052 מקרי מוות ועם 25% מכלל מקרי המוות בבני 65 ומעלה, השיעור הגבוה מבין הסיבות הנקובות בטבלה (עמ׳ 29, טבלה 2-3).
**ד. פציעות הקשורות ל-falls.** שגויה, פציעות לא מכוונות מהוות 2.7% מהתמותה בטבלה. הטקסט מציין נפילות כסוג התאונה השכיח ביותר במבוגרים ביותר, אך הן אינן הסיבה המובילה בכלל מקרי המוות (עמ׳ 29).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 29, טבלה 2-3.

q: A 74-year-old woman with a previous hip fracture takes a long-acting benzodiazepine. Which rationale in Beers 2023 supports reducing exposure?
o: Increased sensitivity and slower metabolism of long-acting agents contribute to harm
Reduced sensitivity with age supports increasing the subsequent medication dose
Switching to a short-acting agent provides a demonstrated reduction in falls risk
Faster metabolism of long-acting agents explains the need for prolonged treatment
explanation:
Benzodiazepines sedate and can impair balance. Older adults may respond more strongly to the same exposure and metabolize long-acting agents more slowly.

**Greater sensitivity and slower metabolism increase harm.** Both matter in a woman who has already fractured her hip.

**A. Greater sensitivity and slower metabolism.** A stronger response can coexist with prolonged exposure, increasing the chance of sedation and another fall.
**B. Reduced sensitivity.** Older adults tend to be more sensitive. Increasing the dose could worsen impaired balance.
**C. Switch to a short-acting drug.** Short-acting benzodiazepines also increase fall risk. Duration alone offers no reliable protection.
**D. Faster metabolism.** Metabolism of long-acting agents tends to slow, allowing drug effects to persist.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2060, 2066.

q: Which nutritional approach to sarcopenia is consistent with the evidence described in Hazzard?
o: Consider vitamin D on the basis of demonstrated improvement in muscle function in sarcopenia
Review food intake and consider high-protein supplements when usual food does not meet requirements
Consider isolated leucine on the basis of demonstrated effects independent of complete nutritional supplements
Spread additional protein throughout the day in preference to timing a protein boost near exercise
explanation:
Nutrition can support muscle maintenance when combined with physical activity. **Review usual food intake and add a high-protein supplement if dietary intake is insufficient**.

**A. Vitamin D for proven functional gain.** Correct severe deficiency if present, but routine vitamin D has not demonstrated a general muscle-function benefit in sarcopenia.
**B. Intake review and targeted supplementation.** Identify the protein and energy gap, then choose a practical way to close it.
**C. Isolated leucine for proven independent benefit.** Many studies used complete nutritional mixtures, so their effects cannot be assigned to leucine alone.
**D. Prefer distributing a boost over timing near exercise.** Muscle uptake is stimulated after exercise, making a protein serving near training a reasonable strategy.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 737.

q: An 84-year-old woman with progressive Alzheimer dementia and an MMSE score of 18/30 takes donepezil. Which cardiovascular adverse-effect pattern is identified in Hazzard as potentially serious enough to trigger deprescribing a cholinesterase inhibitor?
o: Hypertension with an increase in heart rate
Bradycardia with an episode of syncope
Tachycardia with accelerated AV conduction
Hypertension with accelerated AV conduction
explanation:
Cholinesterase inhibitors can increase vagal activity at the sinus and atrioventricular nodes. When the resulting slow heart rate causes loss of consciousness, the medication itself belongs in the syncope evaluation.

**Bradycardia with syncope** is a potentially serious adverse effect and warrants reassessing continued treatment.

**A. Hypertension and a faster pulse.** Neither finding represents the conduction slowing associated with this class.
**B. Bradycardia and syncope.** A slow pulse can reduce cerebral perfusion enough to cause fainting. Check the rhythm and review the drug.
**C. Tachycardia and faster AV conduction.** Both changes run in the opposite direction from the expected vagal effect.
**D. Hypertension and faster AV conduction.** Blood pressure can vary, but accelerated nodal conduction does not explain this adverse-effect pattern.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 911.

q: A comprehensive geriatric assessment identifies depression as a contributor to functional decline in a 77-year-old patient. Why is this finding clinically useful?
o: It identifies disability for which management centers on compensatory assistance
It identifies a treatable affective disorder associated with increased disability
It identifies preserved function despite the reported difficulties in daily activities
It identifies dementia as the established explanation for the functional decline
explanation:
Comprehensive geriatric assessment seeks treatable contributors to loss of independence. **Depression is a treatable affective disorder associated with disability** and can influence daily function.

**A. Compensatory help only.** Practical support may be needed, but depression itself can be treated.
**B. Treatable contributor.** Addressing mood may improve engagement and function while other causes are evaluated.
**C. Preserved function.** Depression does not negate the reported difficulties in daily tasks.
**D. Dementia established.** A mood disorder alone cannot diagnose dementia.

q: According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which effect supports avoiding concomitant opioid and benzodiazepine use in an older adult?
o: The combination may decrease sedation while depressing respiration
The combination may cause profound sedation and respiratory depression
The combination may cause profound sedation while stimulating respiration
The combination may decrease sedation while stimulating respiration
explanation:
Opioids depress breathing, and benzodiazepines depress alertness. Together their effects on the central nervous system can be dangerous.

**Expect a risk of profound sedation and respiratory depression.** Excessive drowsiness can accompany inadequate ventilation.

**A. Less sedation with slower breathing.** Depressed breathing is a concern, but adding a benzodiazepine can deepen sedation.
**B. Profound sedation with slower breathing.** The patient may become difficult to arouse while breathing becomes inadequate.
**C. Profound sedation with stimulated breathing.** Sedation can deepen, and opioid-related respiratory depression can worsen.
**D. Less sedation with stimulated breathing.** Both predictions reverse the combined depressant effects.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2060.

q: A 71-year-old man presents with cognitive decline, visual hallucinations, slow shuffling gait, and frequent falls. He also acts out dreams during REM sleep. Which dementia syndrome is most consistent with this combination?
o: Alzheimer disease with a predominantly episodic-memory syndrome
Nonfluent primary progressive aphasia with an agrammatic syndrome
Dementia with Lewy bodies and associated parkinsonian features
Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia with personality change
explanation:
Dementia with Lewy bodies combines cognitive decline with characteristic perceptual, motor and sleep findings. **Visual hallucinations, a parkinsonian gait and REM dream enactment strongly favor DLB**.

**A. Alzheimer disease.** Prominent episodic-memory loss is more typical at presentation.
**B. Nonfluent PPA.** Speech apraxia and agrammatism would dominate.
**C. Lewy body dementia.** The combination of formed hallucinations, parkinsonism and REM sleep behavior disorder is particularly informative.
**D. Behavioral FTD.** Early disinhibition, altered eating or loss of empathy would better support this diagnosis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 993.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 983

q: מה הצפי הדמוגרפי ל-10 שנים קדימה לגבי אנשים בני 65+ בארצות הברית?
o: יישאר על 16% הנוכחיים מהאוכלוסייה
יעלה לכ-20-23% מהאוכלוסייה
יירד עקב ירידה בתוחלת החיים
מבנה הגיל ישקף את הפצ'ות הנוכחית
explanation:
התשובה היא **עלייה לכ־20–23 אחוזים מהאוכלוסייה**: בספר מופיעה תחזית של 21 אחוזים וכ־73 מיליון בני 65 ומעלה בשנת 2030. זו תחזית המעוגנת בזמן כתיבת המקור, ולא תחזית מתגלגלת לעשר שנים ממועד הקריאה (עמ׳ 1078).

**א. יישאר על 16% הנוכחיים מהאוכלוסייה.** שגויה, הספר מתאר גידול בשיעור המבוגרים, ולא קיפאון בשיעור של 16 אחוזים (עמ׳ 24, 1078).
**ב. יעלה לכ-20-23% מהאוכלוסייה.** נכונה, תחזית 2030 נמצאת בטווח האפשרות. הזדקנות דור הבייבי בום, שהראשונים בו הגיעו לגיל 65 בשנת 2011, תורמת לגידול; עלייה בתוחלת החיים וירידה בפריון מגדילות את חלקם היחסי של מבוגרים. למגמה השלכות על משפחות, כוח העבודה, רפואה וטיפול ממושך ועל היחס בין גילי העבודה לגילים התלויים בהם (עמ׳ 24–25, 27).
**ג. יירד עקב ירידה בתוחלת החיים.** שגויה, התחזית המצוטטת היא לעלייה בשיעור בני 65 ומעלה. המקור מכיר באיומים על תוחלת החיים, ובהם מגפת הקורונה, אך אינו מחליף בשל כך את תחזית השיעור בירידה (עמ׳ 23–25).
**ד. מבנה הגיל ישקף את הפצ'ות הנוכחית.** שגויה, מבנה הגיל אינו נשמר: חלקם של המבוגרים גדל, והירידה בפריון מקטינה יחסית את חלקם של ילדים. גם עקומות ההישרדות השתנו לכיוון מלבני יותר, אך זו עקומת הישרדות ולא פירמידת גיל (עמ׳ 24–25).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 23–25, 27, 1078; תחזית לשנת 2030.

q: A 78-year-old woman reports urine loss when running or coughing and denies sudden urgency or nocturia. Which brief interview instrument was developed to distinguish stress from urge incontinence in women in primary care?
o: Postvoid residual measurement
The 3IQ questionnaire
Multichannel urodynamic testing
Filling cystometrography
explanation:
The Three Incontinence Questions, or 3IQ, distinguish stress and urge leakage in women by asking about typical situations. **Use the 3IQ questionnaire**. Leakage with coughing or running points to stress incontinence.

**A. Postvoid residual.** It measures incomplete bladder emptying.
**B. 3IQ.** The brief interview distinguishes leakage with exertion from loss associated with sudden urgency.
**C. Multichannel urodynamics.** This is specialized physiologic testing, not a brief interview.
**D. Filling cystometry.** It evaluates bladder pressure and function during filling.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 120, 562, 705.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A 72-year-old man hospitalized with COPD develops a stage 2 sacral pressure injury on the third hospital day. Which intervention directly addresses continuing pressure exposure and belongs in the treatment plan for an existing pressure injury?
o: Apply topical antibiotic ointment to the sacral wound
Provide pressure relief and repositioning adapted to the patient
Provide supplemental vitamin C to support intake during wound treatment
Apply an enzymatic debridement agent to the sacral wound
explanation:
An existing pressure injury continues to receive mechanical stress every time the person lies on it. Pressure relief is part of treatment throughout healing.

**Provide individualized repositioning and pressure relief.** Help the patient move off the sacrum, confirm the wound is clear of the support surface and adapt the plan to mobility and tolerance.

**A. Topical antibiotic.** This addresses selected local infections. It cannot relieve the load on the sacrum.
**B. Repositioning and offloading.** Changing position reduces ongoing deformation and gives the tissue an opportunity to reperfuse.
**C. Vitamin C.** Nutrition assessment may uncover deficiencies. Supplementation alone leaves the local mechanical injury in place.
**D. Enzymatic debridement.** Enzymes act on devitalized tissue. A stage 2 wound has viable exposed dermis, and enzyme application would not remove pressure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 683–684, 689–690.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 683

q: A 76-year-old woman has a DXA T-score of -2.8 and no previous fragility fracture. Which classification in Hazzard’s WHO criteria table fits these findings?
o: Bone density is classified as normal
Bone density is classified as osteopenia
Bone density is classified as severe osteoporosis
Bone density is classified as osteoporosis
explanation:
**Osteoporosis** in the table is defined by a T-score of -2.5 or lower; severe osteoporosis additionally includes a fragility fracture (p. 760). The table lists "Osteoporosis ≤ −2.5" and "Severe osteoporosis ≤ −2.5 + fragility fracture" (p. 760). Thus, this is a classification question using both bone density and fracture history.

**A. Bone density is classified as normal.** Wrong, the normal category requires a T-score above -1, whereas the stated value is below the osteoporosis threshold (p. 760).
**B. Bone density is classified as osteopenia.** Wrong, the osteopenia row requires a value above -2.5; the stated value falls on the osteoporosis side of that boundary (p. 760).
**C. Bone density is classified as severe osteoporosis.** Wrong, the severe category adds a fragility fracture to the low T-score; that fracture history is absent in the stem (p. 760).
**D. Bone density is classified as osteoporosis.** Correct, the value meets the osteoporosis threshold, and the stem does not supply the additional fragility fracture required for the severe category (p. 760).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 760.

q: An 82-year-old man with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is starting spironolactone. Which laboratory measurements require close monitoring during initiation and dose titration?
o: Liver enzyme levels and platelet count
Renal function and serum potassium levels
Vitamin B12 and folate levels
Thyroid hormone and serum ferritin levels
explanation:
Spironolactone blocks aldosterone and can retain potassium, particularly when kidney function declines. **Monitor renal function and serum potassium closely** at initiation and after dose changes.

**A. Liver enzymes and platelets.** These miss the principal risk of hyperkalemia.
**B. Renal function and potassium.** Reduced filtration increases vulnerability to dangerous potassium elevation.
**C. B12 and folate.** These investigate selected anemias and do not monitor spironolactone toxicity.
**D. Thyroid hormones and ferritin.** Neither assesses the relevant electrolyte or renal effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1181.

q: An overweight woman with knee osteoarthritis asks for a treatment plan that includes weight loss. Which approach matches the chapter recommendations?
o: Rapid weight loss through a crash diet with reduced physical activity
Gradual weight loss combined with aerobic and strengthening exercise
Maintenance of current weight combined with aerobic and strengthening exercise
Gradual weight loss combined with avoidance of strengthening exercise
explanation:
Excess weight increases knee loading, while exercise maintains strength and walking capacity. **Combine gradual weight loss with aerobic and strengthening exercise** for overweight patients with knee osteoarthritis.

**A. Crash diet with less activity.** Rapid restrictive dieting and inactivity risk loss of muscle and conditioning.
**B. Gradual loss and exercise.** This addresses joint load and supports the muscles needed for mobility.
**C. Maintain current weight and exercise.** Exercise is beneficial, but this omits her weight-loss goal and its potential symptom benefit.
**D. Lose weight without strengthening.** Muscle strengthening is a useful component of pain and function management.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 784, 786.

q: An 80-year-old patient taking chronic morphine for cancer pain develops fecal impaction. Which effect of enteric mu-opioid receptor activation explains the constipation?
o: Increased bowel contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption
Decreased bowel contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption
Decreased bowel contractility with decreased colonic fluid absorption
Increased bowel contractility with decreased colonic fluid absorption
explanation:
Morphine activates enteric mu-opioid receptors, weakening propulsion and allowing greater water reabsorption. **Reduced contractility with increased colonic fluid absorption** produces hard, difficult-to-pass stool.

**A. More contractility, more absorption.** Water reabsorption increases, but propulsive contractions weaken.
**B. Less contractility, more absorption.** Slow, dry stool is more likely to accumulate and impact.
**C. Less contractility, less absorption.** Weak propulsion is correct, but opioid-associated stool becomes drier as absorption increases.
**D. More contractility, less absorption.** Both proposed changes would favor passage of looser stool.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1377, 1378.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 1377–1378

q: A 74-year-old man requests treatment for insomnia and asks about lorazepam. Which statement explains the Beers 2023 warning about benzodiazepines in older adults?
o: Choosing a short-acting agent reduces the risk of subsequent falls
Older adults have increased sensitivity and an increased risk of falls
Continued benzodiazepine use reduces the risk of physical dependence
Combining a benzodiazepine with an opioid reduces the risk of sedation
explanation:
Lorazepam is a benzodiazepine. Increased sensitivity to sedatives in older adults can impair balance even with a shorter-acting drug.

**Greater benzodiazepine sensitivity raises fall risk.** For insomnia, that risk matters when deciding whether to prescribe lorazepam.

**A. Short-acting means fewer falls.** Shorter-acting benzodiazepines also impair coordination and are not reliably safer for falls.
**B. Greater sensitivity and more falls.** Sedation and impaired balance can occur at ordinary doses in older adults.
**C. Continued use reduces dependence.** Regular exposure can lead to physical dependence, complicating withdrawal.
**D. Opioid coadministration reduces sedation.** The combination can deepen sedation and depress respiration.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2060, 2066.

q: An older woman with long-standing hypertension develops dizziness when her blood pressure falls abruptly after a treatment change. Why can cerebral ischemic symptoms occur even within a blood pressure range considered normal?
o: The cerebral autoregulatory threshold shifts toward lower pressures
The cerebral autoregulatory threshold shifts toward higher pressures
The abrupt pressure fall increases cerebral blood flow
Acute antihypertensive administration protects against postural hypotension
explanation:
Cerebral autoregulation maintains blood flow across a range of pressures. Chronic hypertension can **shift the lower autoregulatory threshold toward higher pressures**, making an abrupt reduction symptomatic even at a conventionally normal reading.

**A. Shift to lower pressures.** This would permit better tolerance of a pressure decrease.
**B. Shift to higher pressures.** A sudden drop can cross her individual lower limit and reduce cerebral perfusion.
**C. Increased cerebral flow after the drop.** Dizziness from ischemia reflects inadequate perfusion, not increased flow.
**D. Acute treatment protects against orthostasis.** Rapid pressure lowering can aggravate postural symptoms when regulation is impaired.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 668.

q: An 84-year-old patient has exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, preserved ejection fraction, and echocardiographic evidence of elevated filling pressures. Which treatment principle agrees with the discussion of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in Hazzard?
o: Prioritize beta-blockade to improve the ability to increase heart rate during exercise
Prioritize symptom relief and blood-pressure control with diuretics titrated to congestion
Prioritize rapid diuresis to reduce filling volume despite emerging relative hypotension
Prioritize avoiding diuretics because preserved ejection fraction makes congestion unresponsive
explanation:
HFpEF can produce congestion because a stiff ventricle fills at high pressure despite preserved ejection fraction. **Relieve congestion with carefully titrated diuretics and control blood pressure**.

**A. Beta blocker to increase exercise heart rate.** Beta blockade can blunt the chronotropic response.
**B. Titrate to congestion.** Reduce pulmonary or systemic fluid overload while monitoring pressure and renal function.
**C. Rapid diuresis through hypotension.** Excessive preload reduction can further lower output.
**D. Avoid diuretics for preserved EF.** They can relieve congestion regardless of ejection fraction.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1186.

q: A 75-year-old man has diabetic neuropathic pain, normal renal function, and no concurrent opioid treatment. Gabapentin is started at 100 mg at bedtime as listed in Table 68-8. Which titration approach follows that table?
o: Advance to the maintenance dose immediately after the first bedtime dose
Increase the dose gradually, guided by response and tolerability
Introduce concurrent oxycodone as the gabapentin dose is increased
Replace low-dose initiation with immediate maintenance-dose treatment
explanation:
**Low-dose initiation and gradual titration** are the table’s principles for gabapentinoids (p. 1063). It states "Initiate at lowest dose and gradually titrate" and cautions against concurrent opioid use; central nervous system adverse effects also require attention (pp. 1063–1064).

**A. Advance to the maintenance dose immediately after the first bedtime dose.** Wrong, an immediate increase to maintenance dosing conflicts with the table’s gradual titration instruction (p. 1063).
**B. Increase the dose gradually, guided by response and tolerability.** Correct, gradual adjustment follows the stated approach, with response and adverse effects informing the clinical application (pp. 1063–1064).
**C. Introduce concurrent oxycodone as the gabapentin dose is increased.** Wrong, the table advises avoiding gabapentinoids in patients with concurrent opioid use, so introducing oxycodone conflicts with that instruction (p. 1063).
**D. Replace low-dose initiation with immediate maintenance-dose treatment.** Wrong, immediate maintenance-dose treatment abandons both low-dose initiation and gradual titration (p. 1063).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063, 1064.

q: A 79-year-old woman with coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction takes a high-intensity statin. She tolerates it well and has good functional status. Which approach is appropriate according to Hazzard?
o: Consider stopping the statin because secondary prevention lacks benefit at her age
Consider continuing the tolerated statin for secondary prevention of recurrent cardiovascular events
Consider stopping the statin because primary prevention has uncertain benefit at her age
Consider replacing the statin with fish oil as proven therapy for secondary prevention
explanation:
Secondary prevention reduces recurrent vascular events after established coronary disease. **Continue a well-tolerated high-intensity statin after myocardial infarction** when consistent with the patient's goals.

**A. Stop because of age.** Older adults with established disease can benefit from secondary prevention.
**B. Continue statin.** Prior infarction, good function and tolerability support continuation.
**C. Primary prevention uncertainty.** A previous infarction places her in secondary prevention.
**D. Replace with fish oil.** Fish oil alone does not provide the established secondary-prevention benefit of statin therapy.

q: A 73-year-old woman who has taken alendronate for several years reports new atraumatic thigh and groin pain. Which investigation is directed at a suspected atypical femoral fracture associated with prolonged treatment?
o: Bone-density measurement to assess bone mass
Plain radiography of the painful femoral region
Serum calcium measurement to assess mineral balance
Bone-turnover markers to assess skeletal response
explanation:
Prolonged bisphosphonate use can be associated with an atypical femoral stress fracture. New atraumatic thigh or groin pain is a warning symptom. **Obtain a plain radiograph of the painful femur** to look for a developing fracture.

**A. Bone-density test.** DXA estimates fracture risk over time. It cannot localize a painful cortical fracture.
**B. Femoral radiograph.** Targeted imaging can show a fracture line or focal cortical thickening at the symptomatic site.
**C. Serum calcium.** A calcium level assesses mineral balance and can be normal despite a femoral fracture.
**D. Bone-turnover markers.** They reflect skeletal metabolism but cannot show whether or where the femur has fractured.

q: An 81-year-old man with obstructive sleep apnea has hypertension despite several medications. Which statement correctly distinguishes the blood-pressure finding from cardiovascular-event trial results reported by Hazzard?
o: Modest blood-pressure improvement; cardiovascular-event reduction not demonstrated in large CPAP trials
Modest blood-pressure worsening; cardiovascular-event reduction demonstrated in large CPAP trials
Unchanged blood pressure; cardiovascular-event reduction demonstrated in large CPAP trials
Unchanged blood pressure; cardiovascular-event reduction not demonstrated in the large randomized CPAP trials
explanation:
Continuous positive airway pressure prevents upper-airway collapse during sleep. **CPAP can modestly improve blood pressure, but large randomized trials did not demonstrate fewer cardiovascular events**.

**A. Modest pressure improvement, no proven event reduction.** A change in blood pressure and a reduction in clinical events are separate outcomes.
**B. Worse pressure, fewer events.** Both directions conflict with the observed trial findings.
**C. Unchanged pressure, fewer events.** Hypertensive patients can see modest blood pressure improvement, while event benefit was not demonstrated.
**D. Unchanged pressure, no proven event reduction.** The event interpretation fits, but it omits the modest blood pressure benefit.

q: A 70-year-old man with an eGFR of 25 develops severe constipation while taking opioid analgesics. He has not yet tried a laxative regimen. Which initial approach follows Hazzard’s stepwise treatment principles?
o: Start senna and reassess the bowel response
Start methylnaltrexone before a trial of conventional laxatives
Start docusate monotherapy for its substantial laxative effect
Start regular long-term magnesium hydroxide for rapid catharsis
explanation:
Opioid-related constipation usually begins with conventional laxatives. With an eGFR of 25 and no previous laxative trial, **start senna and reassess the response**.

**A. Senna.** A stimulant laxative improves colonic propulsion without the magnesium load of saline cathartics.
**B. Methylnaltrexone first.** Peripheral opioid antagonists are generally reserved for inadequate response to conventional treatment.
**C. Docusate alone.** Its stool-softening action offers little effective laxation in established opioid constipation.
**D. Long-term magnesium hydroxide.** Poor renal clearance creates a risk of magnesium accumulation.

q: An 85-year-old man with ischemic stroke and a disabling neurologic deficit arrives within the intravenous treatment window. CT shows no hemorrhage. Which principle should guide the decision about thrombolysis?
o: Favor withholding thrombolysis because of the patient’s advanced age
Assess benefit and risk and review inclusion and exclusion criteria
Use the absence of CT hemorrhage in place of reviewing exclusion criteria
Delay treatment in an eligible patient toward the end of the treatment window
explanation:
Intravenous thrombolysis treats eligible disabling ischemic stroke within a defined time window. **Assess the individual benefit, bleeding risks and all eligibility criteria promptly**.

**A. Withhold for age.** Advanced age alone is not an exclusion.
**B. Review eligibility.** The disabling deficit, timing, imaging and contraindications determine suitability together.
**C. Negative CT alone.** Absence of hemorrhage is necessary but other exclusions still matter.
**D. Delay when eligible.** Earlier reperfusion offers greater opportunity to preserve threatened tissue.

q: A patient undergoing rehabilitation after stroke has no mood disorder. The family asks about fluoxetine to improve functional recovery. What did the later trials described in Hazzard find?
o: Improved functional outcomes supporting routine use during rehabilitation
No functional improvement and an increased risk of bone fractures
Improved functional outcomes and a reduced risk of bone fractures
No functional improvement but fracture protection supporting routine use
explanation:
Fluoxetine treats mood disorders and was studied as an aid to stroke recovery. **Later trials found no functional benefit and increased fractures**, arguing against routine use solely for rehabilitation.

**A. Improved function.** Later larger trials did not reproduce a clinically meaningful functional gain.
**B. No gain and more fractures.** This unfavorable combination matters in a patient without a mood indication.
**C. Better function and fewer fractures.** Both proposed effects are reversed.
**D. No gain but fracture protection.** Fractures increased rather than decreased.
