q: אישה בת 70 עם מספר מחלות כרוניות שואלת את הגריאטר שלה לגבי תכנון לנכות עתידית אפשרית. בעלה נפטר לפני 5 שנים והיא גרה לבד. היא חוששת מהמשמעויות הכלכליות של צורך אפשרי בטיפול ארוך-טווח. איזה היבט של דפוסי אריכות החיים בנשים משפיע באופן הישיר ביותר על צרכי תכנון הטיפול שלה?
o: לנשים יש עלויות בריאות נמוכות יותר לאורך החיים בשל תחזוקת בריאות טובה יותר
תוחלת החיים הארוכה יותר של נשים כוללת לעיתים קרובות תקופות ממושכות של ירידה תפקודית ואלמנות
נשים מסתגלות טוב יותר לסביבות של assisted living
לנשים יש רשתות תמיכה משפחתיות חזקות יותר
explanation:
התשובה היא **אפשרות לשנים ממושכות של מוגבלות ואלמנות**. נשים נוטות לשרוד אחרי בני זוגן, ובמקביל נושאות יותר מגבלות תפקודיות; לכן תכנון טיפול ותמיכה עשוי להידרש לאורך זמן (עמ׳ 27, 92).

**א. לנשים יש עלויות בריאות נמוכות יותר לאורך החיים בשל תחזוקת בריאות טובה יותר.** שגויה, אין להסיק עלויות נמוכות מיתרון ההישרדות. הספר מתאר יותר ביקורי רופא, ימי אשפוז, תרופות ומגבלות אצל נשים, המצדיקים תכנון משאבים אישי (עמ׳ 92; יישום לתכנון).
**ב. תוחלת החיים הארוכה יותר של נשים כוללת לעיתים קרובות תקופות ממושכות של ירידה תפקודית ואלמנות.** נכונה, נשים נוטות יותר להתאלמן עקב תוחלת חיים ארוכה יותר. מוגבלות, מחלות כרוניות וחיים ללא בן זוג עלולים להאריך את הצורך בעזרה; נשים גם מיוצגות ביתר במסגרות מגורים טיפוליות. יש לתכנן תמיכה זמינה, יכולת מימון, רצונות עתידיים ושמירת עצמאות, במיוחד לאלמנה עם מחלות כרוניות (עמ׳ 27, 92; יישום לתרחיש).
**ג. נשים מסתגלות טוב יותר לסביבות של assisted living.** שגויה, הסתגלות לדיור מוגן אינה מסבירה את הצורך לתכנן שנות תמיכה ממושכות, ואין במקור בסיס להניח הסתגלות טובה יותר למטופלת זו (עמ׳ 27, 92).
**ד. לנשים יש רשתות תמיכה משפחתיות חזקות יותר.** שגויה, אי אפשר להניח שרשת משפחתית מספיקה תישאר זמינה. המקור מציג אלמנות ומצב כלכלי ובריאותי כגורמים בצורת המגורים, ומדגיש התייחסות למטפל ולמשפחה בתכנון (עמ׳ 27).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 27, 92.

q: גבר בן 67 מגיע להערכת סיכון קרדיווסקולרי. הוא הפסיק לעשן לפני 5 שנים לאחר הרגל של 45 שנה, ושואל מה הסיכון שלו כיום בהשוואה לגברים שמעולם לא עישנו. בהתחשב במגמות האפידמיולוגיות לגבי ההשפעות המושהות של עישון על הבריאות, מה הייעוץ המתאים ביותר?
o: הסיכון שלו חזר מיד לבסיס עם הפסקת העישון
הסיכון שלו ימשיך לרדת אך יישאר מוגבר במשך שנים רבות
הסיכון שלו שווה כעת לזה של אנשים שמעולם לא עישנו באותו גיל
היסטוריית העישון שלו אינה רלוונטית לאחר 5 שנות גמילה
explanation:
**התשובה הנכונה היא שהסיכון שלו ימשיך לרדת אך יישאר מוגבר במשך שנים רבות**.

**א. הסיכון שלו חזר מיד לבסיס עם הפסקת העישון.** שגויה, אפשרות של חזרה מיידית לסיכון הבסיסי עם הפסקת העישון שגויה כי ירידת הסיכון הינה הדרגתית ולא מיידית.
**ב. הסיכון שלו ימשיך לרדת אך יישאר מוגבר במשך שנים רבות.** נכונה, הספרות האפידמיולוגית דנה בהרחבה ב'השפעה המושהית של הרגלי העישון ההיסטוריים' על דפוסי התמותה, ומדגימה כי ההשפעות הבריאותיות של עישון נמשכות זמן רב לאחר הגמילה. הנתונים האפידמיולוגיים המראים כי מוות הקשור לעישון בקרב גברים יורד, אך לאט, מדגישים שמעשנים לשעבר ממשיכים להיות בסיכון מוגבר שנים רבות לאחר הגמילה. סרטן ריאה ומחלות נשימה משמשים כ'אינדיקטורים נוחים להשפעת העישון על הבריאות הכללית', תוך הדגשה שעישון 'משפיע לרעה על היבטים מרובים של הבריאות מעבר להשפעתו על הריאות' — כלומר, סיכון קרדיווסקולרי, סיכון לסרטן וסיכונים נוספים נשארים מוגברים. היסטוריית העישון של 45 שנה של המטופל מייצגת חשיפה מצטברת משמעותית. אמנם הגמילה לפני 5 שנים הייתה מיטיבה וירידת הסיכון החלה מיד, אך הדפוסים האפידמיולוגיים מראים שהשיפורים ברמת אוכלוסייה מתרחשים בהדרגה לאורך עשורים ולא שנים. בעת ייעוץ למטופלים מבוגרים על יתרונות הגמילה מעישון, יש להדגיש כי למרות שהגמילה תמיד מיטיבה וירידת הסיכון מתחילה מיד, מעשנים כבדים לשעבר צריכים לצפות לסיכון מוגבר מתמשך הדורש ערנות רציפה למחלות הקשורות לעישון — כולל cardiovascular disease, סרטן ומחלות נשימה — שנים רבות לאחר הגמילה.
**ג. הסיכון שלו שווה כעת לזה של אנשים שמעולם לא עישנו באותו גיל.** שגויה, אפשרות של סיכון שווה כעת לזה של מי שלא עישנו שגויה מכיוון ששוויון לאנשים שמעולם לא עישנו דורש בדרך כלל 15–20 שנה עבור חלק מהסיכונים, ועבור חלק מהסיכונים לאחר חשיפה כה ממושכת ייתכן שלא יושג כלל.
**ד. היסטוריית העישון שלו אינה רלוונטית לאחר 5 שנות גמילה.** שגויה, אפשרות של חוסר רלוונטיות של העישון לאחר חמש שנים ממעטת בצורה מסוכנת בהשלכות הבריאותיות המתמשכות של עישון ממושך.

מקור: Hazzard Ch 2 — DEMOGRAPHY AND EPIDEMIOLOGY

q: אישה בת 84 עם דמנציה מובאת על ידי בתה להערכה. הבת מציינת שלמרות שאמה סבלה מיותר בעיות בריאותיות לאורך החיים מאביה המנוח, אמה חיה 8 שנים יותר ממנו. היא שואלת מה המשמעות של דפוס זה לתכנון הטיפול. איזה עיקרון מרכזי צריך להנחות את הדיון?
o: לנשים עם דמנציה יש פרוגנוזה טובה יותר מאשר לגברים
הישרדות ממושכת עם מחלות כרוניות מחייבת care planning מורחב
אריכות חיים בנשים מפחיתה את הצורך בהתערבויות אגרסיביות
נשים זקוקות לתרופות שונות עבור אותן מחלות
explanation:
התשובה היא **תכנון טיפול רחב לאורך הישרדות עם מחלות כרוניות**. יתרון ההישרדות הנשי יכול להתקיים לצד יותר מחלה ומוגבלות, ולכן אינו מבטל צורך בתכנון טיפול, תמיכה ומימון (עמ׳ 27, 92).

**א. לנשים עם דמנציה יש פרוגנוזה טובה יותר מאשר לגברים.** שגויה, יתרון הישרדות ברמת האוכלוסייה אינו קביעה של פרוגנוזה טובה יותר לכל אישה עם דמנציה. השאלה המעשית היא הצרכים לאורך זמן, ולא הסקת פרוגנוזה אישית מהמגדר (עמ׳ 92; יישום לתרחיש).
**ב. הישרדות ממושכת עם מחלות כרוניות מחייבת care planning מורחב.** נכונה, הדפוס של יותר תחלואה אך פחות תמותה תואם את פרדוקס הבריאות וההישרדות. מחלות כרוניות, דמנציה וירידה תפקודית עלולות ליצור מסלול ממושך ותנודות בצרכים. אלמנות עשויה לצמצם תמיכת בן זוג; יש לברר מטרות ורצונות כשהדבר אפשרי, להכין את המשפחה ולתכנן תמיכה, מעברים בין מסגרות וצרכים כספיים (עמ׳ 27, 92).
**ג. אריכות חיים בנשים מפחיתה את הצורך בהתערבויות אגרסיביות.** שגויה, אריכות חיים אינה כשלעצמה הוראה להפחית או להגביר טיפול אגרסיבי. המקור מדגיש התאמת טיפול למטרות, לערכים ולהעדפות המטופלת לאורך רצף הטיפול (עמ׳ 1078).
**ד. נשים זקוקות לתרופות שונות עבור אותן מחלות.** שגויה, האפשרות עוסקת בבחירת תרופות לפי מין, ואינה עונה לצורך בתכנון טיפול ממושך בשל מחלה ומוגבלות. תכנון כולל גם תמיכה במטפלים ותפקוד בבית ובמסגרות אחרות (עמ׳ 1078).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 27, 92, 1078.

q: A 78-year-old woman is admitted to a geriatric evaluation and management unit after a fall at home. She has diabetes, hypertension, and mild cognitive impairment. CGA identifies 12 problems. How should the team prioritize its recommendations?
o: By how quickly the investigations for each problem can be completed
By which major recommendations are most likely to achieve desired outcomes
By the sequence in which the problems were identified during assessment
By the lead physician's specialty before addressing the remaining problems
explanation:
Comprehensive geriatric assessment identifies interacting medical, functional and social problems. **Prioritize recommendations by urgency and likelihood of achieving the patient's desired outcomes**.

**A. Fastest tests first.** Speed does not identify which problem poses the greatest risk or offers the greatest benefit.
**B. Desired outcomes.** Agree on priorities with the patient, family where appropriate and the interdisciplinary team.
**C. Order of discovery.** An issue found late may need immediate action.
**D. Lead clinician's specialty.** The most consequential problem may lie outside that specialty.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A comprehensive geriatric assessment team has implemented a care plan and is following the patient. Progress toward the agreed goals is inadequate. Which response is part of the CGA process described in Hazzard?
o: Maintain the plan and judge success by the number of documented problems
Complete follow-up and judge success by the number of recommendations delivered
Reassess the plan with the patient and monitor the effects of revisions
Expand the plan and judge success by the number of specialist referrals
explanation:
Follow-up after geriatric assessment checks both implementation and progress toward agreed goals. **Reassess the patient and plan together, revise it and monitor the effect** when progress is inadequate.

**A. Count documented problems.** More documentation does not improve function or explain the lack of progress.
**B. Count delivered recommendations.** Delivery does not mean a plan was implemented or helped.
**C. Reassess and revise.** Identify barriers, changed goals or missed contributors, then observe the response.
**D. Increase referrals.** Referral count cannot measure whether the patient's priorities are being met.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.130

q: A 75-year-old woman with polypharmacy and recurrent falls undergoes comprehensive geriatric assessment. The team identifies a medication as a possible cause of delirium. She also needs physical therapy for fall prevention and nutritional advice for diabetes. How should the interventions be timed?
o: Begin physical therapy and dietary changes, then review the medication after those interventions
Stop the suspected medication promptly, and implement the other measures after she stabilizes
Continue the suspected medication and add a sedative while starting the other interventions
Defer the medication change and functional interventions to a common follow-up appointment
explanation:
Geriatric assessment orders interventions by clinical urgency as well as likely benefit. **Promptly remove or adjust a suspected deliriogenic medication**, taking withdrawal risk into account, and introduce other recommendations as she stabilizes.

**A. Physical therapy and diet first.** These longer-term goals should not delay addressing a possible acute drug effect.
**B. Prompt medication action.** Reducing the offending exposure can improve attention and immediate safety.
**C. Continue and sedate.** Adding sedation can mask symptoms and worsen fall risk.
**D. Wait for a common review.** Delaying all measures leaves the acute concern untreated.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A 79-year-old man with a hip fracture receives joint orthopedic and geriatric care incorporating CGA. His family asks about the evidence for this model. Which finding is reported in the meta-analysis of eight randomized trials summarized in Hazzard?
o: More discharges to a higher level of care than before hospitalization
Fewer discharges to a higher level of care than before hospitalization
A significant increase in mortality during the hospital admission
A significant reduction in mortality during the hospital admission
explanation:
**Geriatric comanagement** was associated with fewer discharges to a higher level of care in the cited eight-trial meta-analysis. Its inpatient mortality result was a nonsignificant trend toward reduction, rather than a demonstrated mortality benefit or increase (p. 130).
"geriatric comanagement programs for older patients with hip fractures have shown reduced discharges to an increased level of care compared to their pre-hospitalization living situation." (p. 130).

**A. More discharges to a higher level of care than before hospitalization.** Wrong, the reported direction was fewer discharges to an increased level of care (p. 130).
**B. Fewer discharges to a higher level of care than before hospitalization.** Correct, this is the discharge outcome reported for the eight randomized trials (p. 130).
**C. A significant increase in mortality during the hospital admission.** Wrong, mortality trended toward reduction, not a significant increase (p. 130).
**D. A significant reduction in mortality during the hospital admission.** Wrong, the mortality reduction was a nonsignificant trend, not a statistically established effect (p. 130).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 130.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 130, 796

q: An 84-year-old woman receives several recommendations after comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA). After six weeks of monitoring, progress toward the agreed goals is below expectations. Her daughter reports reduced motivation. Which next step follows the CGA process?
o: Continue the existing plan with a longer observation period
Return care to the primary physician with the existing plan
Reassess the patient and revise the plan through team discussion
Increase the frequency of interventions within the existing plan
explanation:
Comprehensive geriatric assessment is a continuing process of setting goals, implementing a plan and assessing outcomes. **Reassess with the patient and team when progress falls short**.

**A. Observe longer unchanged.** This may overlook new illness, implementation barriers or changed motivation.
**B. Return unchanged plan.** Transferring care does not explain why goals were not met.
**C. Reassess and revise.** Ask what changed for the patient and agree on realistic next steps.
**D. Intensify everything.** More frequent interventions can add burden without addressing the actual barrier.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
ref: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 130, Revising the treatment plan
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 130, Revising the treatment plan

q: A 73-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment lives with his supportive wife and is being considered for comprehensive geriatric assessment after hospitalization for pneumonia. In the posthospital randomized trial summarized by Hazzard, which outcome improved with CGA rather than usual care?
o: Less functional decline at the 24-week assessment
Fewer acute-care visits during the postdischarge period
Fewer hospital readmissions during the follow-up period
Less depression at the 24-week assessment
explanation:
**Posthospital CGA outcomes depend on the program and outcome measured**. Hazzard describes inconsistent benefits and reports one trial in which readmissions decreased without a corresponding difference in the other listed outcomes (p. 130). "However, patients assigned to the intervention group were less likely to be readmitted to the hospital." (p. 130)

**A. Less functional decline at the 24-week assessment.** Wrong, the trial did not find a difference in functional decline after 24 weeks, so this was not its demonstrated benefit (p. 130).
**B. Fewer acute-care visits during the postdischarge period.** Wrong, postdischarge acute-care visits did not differ in this trial, despite the difference in readmissions (p. 130).
**C. Fewer hospital readmissions during the follow-up period.** Correct, readmission was less likely in the intervention group in the trial specified by the question (p. 130).
**D. Less depression at the 24-week assessment.** Wrong, depression did not differ after 24 weeks in the trial; it was not the outcome that improved (p. 130).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 130.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A hospital uses a Mobile Acute Care of the Elderly (MACE) team for older medical and surgical inpatients. Which description matches this service?
o: A dedicated rehabilitation ward providing prolonged inpatient recovery
An interdisciplinary ward team reducing the hazards of hospitalization
A home-visiting team providing acute care instead of hospitalization
A scheduled day-clinic team providing outpatient geriatric assessment
explanation:
Mobile Acute Care of the Elderly (MACE) brings geriatric care to older patients on their existing medical or surgical wards. The team works with ward staff to reduce hazards such as immobility, educate families, and prepare for discharge.

**A. Dedicated rehabilitation ward.** Transfer to a rehabilitation unit serves patients who need ongoing recovery after an acute illness.
**B. Interdisciplinary ward team.** A geriatrician, clinical nurse specialists, and social workers can address risks at the bedside while the patient stays on the admitting ward.
**C. Acute care at home.** Hospital-at-home teams deliver acute treatment in the patient's residence.
**D. Day clinic.** Scheduled geriatric assessments serve outpatients and take place outside the inpatient ward.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 194.
ref: Hazzard Ch 14 — MODELS OF HOSPITAL AND OUTPATIENT CARE
chapterTitle: Models of Hospital and Outpatient Care

q: A 76-year-old woman with dementia, diabetes, and hypertension undergoes comprehensive geriatric assessment. Her adult son is her principal caregiver. Which approach best incorporates patient-centered care into the treatment plan?
o: Use motivational interviewing to secure agreement with goals already chosen by the team
Use motivational interviewing to identify her priorities and willingness to make changes
Use the diagnosis list to set disease-based goals before discussing the plan with her son
Use her son's preferences to set goals and judge success by adherence to instructions
explanation:
Motivational interviewing explores a person's priorities and readiness to change. **Use it to identify what this woman wants to achieve**, including her son in planning as appropriate.

**A. Secure agreement with preset goals.** Persuasion to accept a predetermined plan misses her priorities.
**B. Identify priorities and readiness.** Adapt communication to dementia and use her responses to shape achievable goals.
**C. Start from diagnoses alone.** Disease-specific goals may neglect function, preferences and caregiving realities.
**D. Adopt the son's goals.** His information and support matter, but his preferences do not automatically replace hers.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: An 81-year-old man is admitted to a geriatric evaluation and management unit after repeated falls and medication-related confusion. Physicians, nurses, clinical pharmacists, social workers, and therapists present their findings. What task belongs to the team-discussion phase of comprehensive geriatric assessment?
o: Determining who should assume responsibility for implementing each recommendation
Determining which problems need action and might respond to treatment
Determining whether the patient's progress might require further team review
Determining how recommendations might change after progress falls below expectations
explanation:
**Team discussion** links assessment findings to problems that warrant intervention. The subsequent treatment plan defines goals and how recommendations will be implemented and monitored (pp. 129–130). "The team then identifies problems that need action and might be responsive to treatment." (p. 130)

**A. Determining who should assume responsibility for implementing each recommendation.** Wrong, assigning responsibility concerns implementation of recommendations; it follows identification of actionable problems (p. 130).
**B. Determining which problems need action and might respond to treatment.** Correct, this is the task explicitly assigned to team discussion after the initial discipline-specific presentations (pp. 129–130).
**C. Determining whether the patient's progress might require further team review.** Wrong, monitoring follows delivery of the treatment plan and checks progress and implementation (p. 130).
**D. Determining how recommendations might change after progress falls below expectations.** Wrong, revision is prompted by monitoring that shows progress is not proceeding as expected (p. 130).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 130.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 129–130, Discussion among team

q: A 77-year-old woman receives CGA recommendations for medication changes, physical therapy, and home safety. Which account of the purpose and resource implications of monitoring matches Hazzard?
o: Monitoring tracks implementation; longer, more intensive follow-up reduces consultation resource use
Monitoring tracks assessment completion; longer, more intensive follow-up leaves resource use unchanged
Monitoring tracks implementation and progress; longer, more intensive follow-up increases resource use
Monitoring tracks the final diagnosis; shorter, less intensive follow-up increases consultation resource use
explanation:
Monitoring after comprehensive geriatric assessment checks implementation and measures patient progress. **Longer, more intensive monitoring requires more team resources**.

**A. More monitoring reduces resource use.** More visits and communication generally require additional staff time.
**B. Assessment completion only.** Monitoring continues beyond the initial evaluation and uses resources.
**C. Implementation, outcomes and greater resources.** The team or primary clinician checks what was done and whether it helped.
**D. Final diagnosis only.** Follow-up addresses function and agreed goals, not just diagnostic closure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A healthy 72-year-old man takes lisinopril for hypertension and exercises regularly. He asks whether supplements advertised as targeting aging pathways will help him live longer. What should guide your advice?
o: Recommend the supplement on the strength of its proposed biological mechanism
Defer supplement use pending rigorous clinical data and FDA review
Recommend the supplement on the strength of its over-the-counter availability
Recommend the supplement on the strength of claims from an unregulated clinic
explanation:
An aging-pathway effect in a laboratory cannot show whether a person lives longer or experiences harm. **Defer using this supplement for longevity until rigorous human evidence shows meaningful benefit and acceptable risk.** In the United States, dietary supplements generally are sold without FDA premarket approval for efficacy.

**A. Recommend from the mechanism.** A plausible pathway does not quantify survival benefit, adverse effects or interactions with lisinopril.
**B. Wait for clinical data and FDA review.** Waiting for outcome evidence is appropriate. A new drug seeking authorization for a therapeutic indication faces an approval process distinct from the rules for ordinary dietary supplements.
**C. Recommend because it is over the counter.** Availability establishes neither lifespan benefit nor safety in this patient.
**D. Rely on clinic claims.** Testimonials and marketing do not compare clinical outcomes or harms against an appropriate control.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 602–603. FDA, Information for Consumers on Using Dietary Supplements.
Key note: FDA does not approve ordinary dietary supplements for safety and efficacy before sale. The relevant reason to defer is lack of demonstrated clinical benefit, not an expected premarket supplement approval.

q: A 68-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and osteoarthritis wishes to join a trial of an intervention intended to slow biological aging. Which biomarker property is needed to detect a response to the intervention?
o: Association with chronological age despite unchanged biomarker values
Sensitivity of biomarker values to change with intervention
Association with one age-related disease despite unchanged values
Stability of biomarker values despite an effective intervention
explanation:
A biomarker intended to monitor treatment must move detectably when the biological process changes. **Sensitivity to intervention-related change** is necessary before it can measure response.

**A. Correlation with chronological age.** It may distinguish younger from older people without changing during treatment.
**B. Responsive values.** A measurable change permits comparison over the course of an intervention. Clinical significance still requires validation.
**C. Association with a single disease.** Disease association is different from responsiveness and is narrow for a general aging marker.
**D. Unchanged despite benefit.** A marker insensitive to effective treatment cannot track the response.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.

q: A clinician is considering a biomarker of aging that is associated with mortality in an observational study. What is needed before interpreting a treatment-induced change in this biomarker as evidence of clinical benefit?
o: An observational assessment of its association with mortality
An assessment within an intervention with demonstrated clinical benefit
An analytical assessment of laboratory accuracy and reproducibility
A combined assessment of several biomarkers in one blood sample
explanation:
**Validation of a biomarker** requires more than an association with mortality. Hazzard requires an accepted clinical outcome and an intervention proven to change its risk before mediation can be evaluated (p. 602).
"an accepted outcome for a geroscience trial" (p. 602).

**A. An observational assessment of its association with mortality.** Wrong, an observational association does not evaluate mediation of an effective intervention; that additional requirement remains unmet (p. 602).
**B. An assessment within an intervention with demonstrated clinical benefit.** Correct, this supplies the effective-intervention setting required to evaluate mediation of a change in clinical outcome risk (p. 602).
**C. An analytical assessment of laboratory accuracy and reproducibility.** Wrong, laboratory reproducibility does not supply the required evidence about intervention effects on a clinical outcome (inference from the validation criteria, p. 602).
**D. A combined assessment of several biomarkers in one blood sample.** Wrong, combining markers does not by itself evaluate mediation of benefit from an effective intervention (inference from the validation criteria, p. 602).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 602.

q: A 70-year-old woman receives a result showing peripheral white-cell telomere length below the average for her age. Which limitation is important when interpreting this result in an individual?
o: The telomere measurement is calibrated primarily from DNA methylation patterns
Substantial variability limits the clinical applications of the telomere measurement
Telomeres lengthen with age and provide a measure of reversed aging
Uniformity between individuals permits precise estimation of biological age from telomeres
explanation:
Leukocyte telomeres generally shorten with age, but lengths vary considerably between people. **Substantial variability limits interpretation of an individual below-average result**.

**A. Calibrated from methylation.** Methylation patterns underlie epigenetic clocks, not direct measurement of telomere length.
**B. Substantial variability.** An individual's length overlaps broadly across age groups and cannot precisely assign biological age.
**C. Progressive lengthening.** The usual association with aging is shortening, not reliable lengthening or reversal.
**D. Uniform precise age determination.** The wide distribution prevents the proposed precision.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 602

q: An older patient asks to start caloric restriction after hearing that CALERIE slowed the advancement of physiologic age. What principle should guide interpretation before an individual recommendation?
o: Treat the biomarker change as evidence that dementia is prevented
Assess effectiveness and safety beyond the change in the aging measure
Treat the biomarker change as evidence of suitability in malnutrition
Use the biomarker change in place of an assessment of treatment risks
explanation:
A change in a physiological aging measure is a surrogate finding. **Assess clinical effectiveness and safety before recommending caloric restriction to an individual**, particularly when nutritional reserve may be limited.

**A. Prevents dementia.** Slower change in an aging measure is not a demonstrated cognitive outcome.
**B. Assess benefit and risk.** Ask whether people function better or avoid disease and whether restriction causes harm in the relevant population.
**C. Suitable in malnutrition.** Further energy restriction could worsen weight and muscle loss. A biomarker result cannot answer that safety question.
**D. Replace risk assessment.** Favorable laboratory changes can coexist with clinical harms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.

q: A 69-year-old woman with coronary disease asks why LDL cholesterol can serve as a treatment-development biomarker whereas developing biomarkers for aging interventions remains difficult. Which explanation matches Hazzard?
o: An established single aging pathway makes the main difference the duration of trials
LDL has a causal atherosclerotic role; no single longevity pathway is identified
Validated aging surrogate endpoints make the main difference the cost of clinical trials
Aging biomarkers need no linkage between treatment-related changes and health outcomes
explanation:
A treatment biomarker is easier to interpret when the biological factor has a causal role in disease. **LDL contributes causally to atherosclerosis, whereas no single pathway explains human longevity**.

**A. One known longevity pathway.** Aging reflects interacting processes and cannot be reduced to one established pathway.
**B. Causal LDL versus complex longevity.** LDL has a defined disease relationship. An aging marker must earn an analogous link to meaningful outcomes.
**C. Validated aging endpoints already exist.** Validation of treatment surrogates is itself a major challenge beyond trial expense.
**D. No outcome link needed.** Treatment-related biomarker change must be linked to altered health risk before substituting for an outcome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 602

q: An aging study uses a DNA methylation clock. According to Hazzard, what relationship underlies the age estimate?
o: Correlation of plasma protein concentrations with chronological age
Correlation of cellular telomere length with chronological age
Correlation of DNA methylation patterns with chronological age
Correlation of organ volumes on imaging with chronological age
explanation:
A DNA methylation clock estimates age from chemical marks on DNA that change over the lifespan. Researchers calibrate the clock against known chronological ages, then use the methylation pattern in a new sample to estimate the donor’s age.

**A. Plasma protein concentrations.** Age-related changes in circulating proteins can inform a proteomic clock, which measures a different set of molecules.
**B. Telomere length.** Shortening at chromosome ends can reflect a cell’s history of division. Length is a separate marker of aging.
**C. DNA methylation patterns.** The clock combines measurements at sites whose methylation varies predictably with chronological age. The biological mechanism behind that association remains uncertain.
**D. Organ volumes.** Imaging measures anatomical changes such as tissue loss. It cannot measure methylation at individual DNA sites.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 41.

q: A 73-year-old woman with age-related diseases is considering a study using a panel of aging biomarkers. Researchers want to establish that an intervention-related biomarker change reflects a health-outcome change. Which finding most directly supports that link under the Hazzard criteria?
o: An association between the biomarker level at baseline and chronological age measured at the same assessment
An association between biomarker change and outcome-risk change, with evidence of mediation during an effective intervention
An association between the biomarker level at baseline and subsequent mortality assessed during the follow-up period
An association between the biomarker level at baseline and the presence of multiple age-related health conditions
explanation:
An intervention surrogate must reflect what treatment changes about health, beyond predicting risk at baseline. **Link biomarker change to change in outcome risk and show mediation of an effective treatment's benefit**.

**A. Baseline age correlation.** It shows a cross-sectional relationship, not response to therapy.
**B. Change and mediation.** Track the marker and a meaningful outcome under treatment, then assess whether the marker accounts for treatment-related benefit.
**C. Baseline mortality prediction.** Prediction identifies risk without proving that modifying the marker changes it.
**D. Baseline multimorbidity association.** Association with several diseases is relevant for aging biology but does not demonstrate mediation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 602

q: An 80-year-old man with several chronic diseases asks whether an aging biomarker could measure the effect of treatment. Which relationship is required for a biomarker used to evaluate outcomes in a geroscience trial?
o: A relationship between the biomarker and laboratory availability.
A relationship between the biomarker and treatment cost.
A relationship between biomarker change and clinical change.
A relationship between the biomarker and clinic-visit frequency.
explanation:
**Trial biomarkers** must be linked to the outcome of interest. After intervention, movement in the biomarker should predict clinical outcomes, connecting biological change with clinical change (p. 601). "Importantly, biomarkers for clinical trials must have a strong statistical link to the desired outcome." (p. 601).

**A. A relationship between the biomarker and laboratory availability.** Wrong, laboratory availability does not demonstrate the required statistical link to the clinical outcome (p. 601).
**B. A relationship between the biomarker and treatment cost.** Wrong, treatment cost does not demonstrate that biomarker changes predict clinical outcomes (p. 601).
**C. A relationship between biomarker change and clinical change.** Correct, this links change in the underlying biology with change in the clinical endpoint, as required (p. 601).
**D. A relationship between the biomarker and clinic-visit frequency.** Wrong, visit frequency does not supply the required relationship with the desired clinical outcome (p. 601).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 601.

q: Researchers develop a blood biomarker associated with future mortality and propose using treatment-related changes in it to assess benefits of interventions targeting aging. Which study design provides the prerequisite setting for evaluating this use?
o: An observational study comparing age groups and correlations with chronological age
An intervention study using an accepted outcome and proven effective treatment
An observational study replicating the association with long-term mortality in another cohort
A laboratory study combining aging-pathway markers and examining their interrelationships
explanation:
To test whether a biomarker can stand in for a clinical outcome, investigators need an intervention with a known outcome benefit. **Study an effective treatment against an accepted clinical outcome** and assess how biomarker change relates to that benefit.

**A. Compare age groups.** Cross-sectional age differences do not test a treatment effect.
**B. Effective treatment and accepted outcome.** This design allows investigators to assess change and potential mediation.
**C. Replicate mortality prediction.** A second observational association still cannot show whether treatment-induced change tracks benefit.
**D. Combine laboratory markers.** Correlations within a panel do not supply a clinical intervention or endpoint.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 602, Biomarkers of aging

q: A 78-year-old woman living alone has unintentionally lost 8 lb over six months. Her appetite has declined and food no longer tastes the same. She takes lisinopril, metformin, sertraline, and omeprazole; BMI is 20 kg/m2. Which approach incorporates the nutritional screening and medication review described in Hazzard?
o: Obtain metabolic and thyroid tests in place of assessing weight change and food intake
Perform MNA and review medications affecting taste or appetite
Arrange endoscopy in place of assessing nutritional status and medication effects
Prescribe calorie supplements and postpone nutritional assessment for three months
explanation:
The Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA) identifies older adults at risk of malnutrition by asking about intake and weight change. Her eight-pound loss, poor appetite and altered taste warrant **nutritional screening and a medication review now**.

**A. Metabolic and thyroid tests alone.** These can uncover causes of weight loss but cannot show how much she is eating.
**B. MNA and medication review.** Document her weight trajectory and actual intake. Metformin, for example, can cause a metallic taste, so ask whether symptoms coincided with starting it.
**C. Endoscopy first.** Dysphagia or gastrointestinal bleeding would direct investigation toward endoscopy. It cannot assess her overall nutritional risk.
**D. Supplements with delayed assessment.** Supplements may help meet calorie needs. Waiting three months could miss an ongoing drug effect or another treatable cause.

q: An inactive 82-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, and osteoarthritis spends most of the day watching television. He asks whether joint pain, fear of falling, and his age make it too late to start exercising. Which counseling statement is supported by Hazzard?
o: Joint pain generally makes prolonged reduction of daily activity preferable
Starting at an advanced age generally offers little prospect of benefit
Benefits generally outweigh risks, with guidance tailored to his limitations
Fall risk generally makes rest preferable until baseline risk has fallen
explanation:
Physical activity helps preserve strength, mobility and independence even when started late in life. For this sedentary 82-year-old, **the benefits generally outweigh the risks when activity is adapted to his joint pain and balance**.

**A. Rest painful joints long term.** Prolonged inactivity can weaken the muscles that support arthritic joints. Low-impact movement can be adjusted to his symptoms.
**B. Too late to start.** Previously inactive older adults can still improve strength and walking ability with training.
**C. Tailor the exercise plan.** Begin with a tolerable activity, such as a short walk on a level surface, and increase it gradually as pain and stamina allow.
**D. Wait for fall risk to decline.** Balance and strength training address contributors to falls. Supervision can help him start safely.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 166.

q: A 69-year-old woman at high cardiovascular risk wants to improve a diet rich in processed foods. Which change fits the Mediterranean-style pattern described in Hazzard?
o: Favor processed meats and hydrogenated fats over fish and nuts
Favor olive oil, nuts, and fish while reducing processed meat
Favor animal fats while reducing oils derived from plant sources
Favor foods containing trans fats while reducing olive oil and fish
explanation:
A Mediterranean eating pattern emphasizes plant foods and unsaturated fats and includes fish. **Replace processed meat with fish, nuts and olive oil** to improve the composition of this woman's diet.

**A. Processed meats and hydrogenated fats.** This substitution reduces foods rich in unsaturated fats while increasing foods the pattern limits.
**B. Olive oil, nuts and fish.** These provide unsaturated fats and can replace less favorable sources of fat and protein.
**C. Animal fats in place of plant oils.** The substitution reverses the emphasis on olive oil and other plant-derived fats.
**D. Trans fats in place of olive oil and fish.** Trans fats are discouraged for cardiovascular health.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 416.

q: A 75-year-old man reports altered food taste, reduced appetite, and weight loss beginning after changes to several medications. His mood is stable, he eats with family, and oral examination reveals no problem. Which area of evaluation most directly addresses the timing and taste change?
o: Evaluate depression and its effects on appetite and food intake
Evaluate medication effects on food taste and appetite
Evaluate chewing difficulty and its effects on food intake
Evaluate mealtime isolation and its effects on food intake
explanation:
Medications can alter taste or suppress appetite enough to reduce food intake. His weight loss and change in flavor perception began after several prescriptions changed. **Review which drugs were started or adjusted and when the symptoms appeared.**

**A. Depression.** Depression can reduce interest in food. His stable mood makes it a less direct explanation for a new taste disturbance.
**B. Medication effects.** A close match between a dose change and symptom onset can identify a drug to reassess while monitoring intake and weight.
**C. Chewing difficulty.** Dental or denture problems tend to make specific textures hard to eat. He describes altered flavor and has a normal oral examination.
**D. Mealtime isolation.** Eating alone can diminish appetite. He shares meals with family, making isolation a poor explanation for this change.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 166.

q: An 85-year-old woman attends with her daughter, who reports increasing social isolation since the patient's husband died six months ago. The patient rarely leaves home and mainly eats frozen meals by herself in front of the television. She has lost interest in cooking and preparing meals. Her weight is stable, but the quality of her diet appears poor. Which intervention addresses the social contribution to her eating difficulties?
o: Arrange private meals in a quiet room and defer her return to eating with company.
Wait for documented weight loss before arranging social meals and offering additional dietary support.
Address social isolation and encourage community meal participation to provide company while she eats.
Use a restricted uniform menu to simplify food selection while keeping meals separate from social activities.
explanation:
Bereavement and eating alone can reduce interest in cooking and diminish diet quality before weight falls. **Arrange opportunities to eat with others**, such as a community meal program, to address the social cause.

**A. Private quiet meals.** Quiet may help some diners, but further isolation perpetuates her particular difficulty.
**B. Wait for weight loss.** The diet has already deteriorated. Stable weight does not exclude inadequate nutrient intake.
**C. Community meals.** Companionship restores the social part of eating and can encourage better intake.
**D. Restricted uniform menu.** Simplifying choices does nothing to restore company or interest in meals.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 296, 409–410.

q: A 71-year-old man with well-controlled heart failure, diabetes, and hypertension follows a longstanding diet restricting salt, fat, and sugar. He says the food tastes like cardboard, eats very little, and is losing weight. Which dietary approach is consistent with the source’s strategies to improve oral intake?
o: Tighten the dietary restrictions and continue foods he finds unappealing
Relax unnecessary restrictions and offer foods matching his preferences
Reduce meal frequency and retain the same restrictive diet
Remove preferred foods and encourage adaptation to the restricted menu
explanation:
A diet can meet disease-specific targets on paper yet lead to undernutrition if the patient eats very little of it. **Relax unnecessary restrictions and offer foods he enjoys**, balancing them with his heart failure and diabetes needs.

**A. Tighten restrictions.** More unpalatable food is likely to worsen the intake deficit.
**B. Liberalize selectively.** A dietitian can retain essential restrictions and restore acceptable foods in adequate amounts.
**C. Reduce meal frequency.** Small, frequent meals offer more opportunities to meet energy needs.
**D. Remove preferred foods.** Taste and acceptability are already the barriers. Removing preferred foods reinforces them.

q: A 67-year-old woman at her annual visit reports being sedentary during office work and television viewing. She feels overwhelmed about starting exercise. She asks whether she could accumulate activity in short bouts instead of one longer continuous session. Assuming similar total energy expenditure, what does Hazzard report about coronary heart disease risk reduction?
o: Short bouts provide less coronary protection than continuous sessions despite similar total energy expenditure.
Short bouts provide greater coronary protection than continuous sessions despite similar total energy expenditure.
Short bouts provide equivalent coronary protection to continuous sessions with similar total energy expenditure.
Short bouts require vigorous intensity to provide coronary protection despite similar total energy expenditure.
explanation:
Physical activity can reduce coronary heart disease risk whether it is accumulated during the day or completed in one session. **Several short walks can offer comparable protection to one longer walk when total energy expenditure is similar.**

**A. Less protection from short bouts.** Each bout contributes to the day's activity. A continuous session has no demonstrated advantage for coronary risk at the same expenditure.
**B. Greater protection from short bouts.** Dividing activity may make it easier to maintain, but session count alone confers no extra coronary protection.
**C. Equivalent protection.** Three ten-minute walks at the same pace as one thirty-minute walk illustrate how she can accumulate a comparable amount of activity.
**D. Vigorous intensity required.** Moderate activity such as brisk walking can lower cardiovascular risk, including when it is broken into manageable bouts.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 807.

q: A 73-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and hearing loss lives alone. His neighbor reports that he appears lonely and isolated. He wants more social contact but does not know how to connect with others, and hearing loss makes group activities difficult. Which initial plan follows the social-connection guidance in Hazzard?
o: Refer to intensive group activities and defer addressing hearing difficulties until he adjusts.
Recommend solitary activities at home and track how frequently he pursues his hobbies.
Address barriers such as hearing loss and connect him with suitable community programs.
Arrange contact according to neighbor availability and let staff choose his social activities.
explanation:
Loneliness reflects a gap between the social contact a person wants and the contact they experience. He wants company, and hearing loss interferes with conversation. **Ask what contact he prefers, address his hearing and connect him with a suitable community program.**

**A. Intensive groups immediately.** Background noise and overlapping voices can make group conversation difficult while his hearing needs remain unaddressed.
**B. Solitary hobbies.** These can be enjoyable, but tracking them gives little information about whether he has the companionship he wants.
**C. Hearing support and community referral.** A hearing assessment and a quiet small group or one-to-one activity could make conversation easier.
**D. Staff-selected activities.** The neighbor can help arrange introductions. Ask the patient directly about his interests when choosing activities, even with mild cognitive impairment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 166, Table 11-3.

q: An 80-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and early dementia eats poorly despite having a caregiver at home. Recent tests show low protein and zinc levels. Her son asks about nutritional screening. Which approach follows Hazzard?
o: Use albumin and prealbumin results in place of a dietary and weight history
Use a tool such as MNA or MST alongside body weight and weight-change assessment
Use zinc and protein results in place of assessing intake and weight change
Use current BMI and outward appearance in place of weight history and intake questions
explanation:
Nutritional screening looks for inadequate intake and unintentional weight loss. In early dementia, a caregiver can help describe how much the patient actually eats. **Measure weight, compare it with prior weights and use the Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA) or the Malnutrition Screening Tool (MST).**

**A. Albumin and prealbumin alone.** Inflammation can lower both values independently of food intake, making them poor stand-alone screening tests.
**B. MNA or MST with weight assessment.** Either tool can flag nutritional risk and prompt a closer look at what limits her meals.
**C. Zinc and protein levels alone.** Abnormal results warrant attention, but they cannot quantify her calorie intake or tell how much weight she has lost.
**D. BMI and appearance alone.** Substantial weight loss can occur while BMI remains in the normal range.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 120, 166. ASPEN, Visceral Proteins as Nutrition Markers.

q: A 76-year-old woman with osteoarthritis and stable heart failure starts rehabilitation. She needs greater strength for rising from a chair and better endurance for walking. Which pair of training components targets these goals?
o: Flexibility exercises and relaxation training
Balance exercises and relaxation training
Resistance exercises and aerobic training
Range-of-motion exercises and breathing practice
explanation:
Rising from a chair requires enough leg force to lift body weight. Repeated walking draws on aerobic capacity, which determines how long a person can sustain a submaximal effort.

**Pair progressive resistance exercise for chair-rise strength with aerobic training for walking endurance. Tailor both to her joint symptoms and cardiac stability.**

**A. Flexibility and relaxation.** Flexibility can improve available joint motion, but this combination gives neither a progressive strength load nor sustained aerobic work.
**B. Balance and relaxation.** Balance practice can improve steadiness during a transfer. It does not build the leg force and cardiovascular endurance asked about.
**C. Resistance and aerobic exercise.** Loaded leg exercises train force production, while repeated walking or cycling increases endurance.
**D. Range of motion and breathing practice.** These may prepare her to exercise, but neither substitutes for progressive loading or sustained whole-body activity.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 824.

q: An older man taking temazepam for sleep has recurrent falls. According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which statement about benzodiazepines supports reviewing this treatment?
o: They increase the risks of falls and cognitive impairment
They reduce the risks of falls and cognitive impairment
They increase the metabolic clearance of long-acting benzodiazepine agents
They reduce the risks of delirium and physical dependence
explanation:
Benzodiazepines impair alertness, cognition and psychomotor function, particularly in older adults. **Temazepam can increase both falls and cognitive impairment**, so reassess its need in this man with recurrent falls.

**A. Increased falls and cognitive risk.** These are class effects, including with benzodiazepines used for sleep.
**B. Reduced falls and cognitive risk.** Sedation and impaired coordination can make nighttime walking less safe.
**C. Faster clearance of long-acting drugs.** Metabolism of long-acting benzodiazepines is often slower with age.
**D. Less delirium and dependence.** Benzodiazepines can increase delirium risk, and continued use can lead to physical dependence.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 2, p. 2060.

q: למטופלת עם מחלה נוירולוגית הופעל ייפוי כוח מתמשך בזמן שלא יכלה להחליט. לאחר שיפור במצבה נדרשת החלטה טיפולית חדשה. מה צריך מיופה הכוח לבדוק לפני שיחליט בשמה?
o: האם אחד הילדים מעדיף לקבל את ההחלטה
האם ההחלטה תואמת את העדפותיו האישיות
האם היא מסוגלת להחליט בעצמה עם סיוע
האם רוב בני המשפחה מסכימים להצעתו
explanation:
**שימור עצמאות בקבלת החלטות** נדרש גם לאחר הפעלת ייפוי כוח מתמשך. המדריך מחייב לבדוק בכל שלב אם האדם יכול להחליט בעצמו או לבצע את הפעולה בסיוע, כדי לאפשר ביטוי לרצונו ולבקשותיו (עמ׳ 17).
"בכל שלב בו הינך יכול לקבל החלטות בעצמך או לבצע עבור עצמך פעולות, הוא צריך לבדוק אם אתה יכול לקבל את ההחלטה או לבצע את הפעולה בעצמך" (עמ׳ 17).

**א. האם אחד הילדים מעדיף לקבל את ההחלטה.** שגויה, העדפת ילד אינה מחליפה בדיקה אם המטופלת יכולה להחליט בעצמה (עמ׳ 17).
**ב. האם ההחלטה תואמת את העדפותיו האישיות.** שגויה, מיופה הכוח נדרש לשמור על רצונה ורצונותיה של הממנה, ולא להחליפם בהעדפותיו (עמ׳ 17).
**ג. האם היא מסוגלת להחליט בעצמה עם סיוע.** נכונה, הבדיקה נדרשת בכל שלב, ולכן השיפור במצב מצריך בחינת יכולתה הנוכחית (עמ׳ 17).
**ד. האם רוב בני המשפחה מסכימים להצעתו.** שגויה, הסכמת רוב המשפחה אינה הבדיקה שהמדריך דורש לפני פעולה בשמה (עמ׳ 17).

q: An older man with gout and a creatinine clearance of 22 mL/min needs treatment. How does the renal-adjustment table in the 2023 Beers Criteria distinguish colchicine from NSAIDs?
o: Use the usual colchicine dose with monitoring, and reduce the NSAID dose
Reduce the colchicine dose with monitoring, and use the usual NSAID dose
Avoid colchicine, and reduce the NSAID dose with monitoring
Reduce the colchicine dose with monitoring, and avoid NSAIDs
explanation:
In **renal impairment**, the Beers table differentiates dose reduction from avoidance. Below a creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min, it recommends reducing colchicine and monitoring for toxicity, while avoiding NSAIDs because of kidney-injury and further kidney-function risks (p. 2073). "Colchicine <30 GI, neuromuscular, and bone marrow toxicity Reduce dose; monitor for adverse effects." (p. 2073).

**A. Use the usual colchicine dose with monitoring, and reduce the NSAID dose.** Wrong, the colchicine recommendation is dose reduction with monitoring, and the NSAID recommendation is avoidance rather than reduced-dose use (p. 2073).
**B. Reduce the colchicine dose with monitoring, and use the usual NSAID dose.** Wrong, the colchicine advice fits, but the NSAID advice contradicts the avoidance recommendation at this clearance (p. 2073).
**C. Avoid colchicine, and reduce the NSAID dose with monitoring.** Wrong, the table specifies reduced-dose colchicine with monitoring rather than avoidance, and recommends avoiding NSAIDs rather than reducing them (p. 2073).
**D. Reduce the colchicine dose with monitoring, and avoid NSAIDs.** Correct, both parts follow the table's recommendations for a clearance below the stated threshold (p. 2073).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2073.

q: An 81-year-old woman with difficulty managing medications takes diphenhydramine nightly for sleep. Which consideration supports reviewing this medication under Beers 2023?
o: Cholinergic activity with a risk of confusion and constipation
Anticholinergic activity with a risk of confusion and constipation
Anticholinergic activity with a reduction in delirium risk
Cholinergic activity with a reduction in falling risk
explanation:
Diphenhydramine is a first-generation antihistamine that also blocks muscarinic receptors. Regular use for sleep exposes older adults to effects in the brain and gut.

**Anticholinergic activity can cause confusion and constipation.** Both are reasons to reconsider nightly use.

**A. Cholinergic activity with confusion and constipation.** These symptoms fit blockade of muscarinic signaling, whereas cholinergic stimulation is the opposite mechanism.
**B. Anticholinergic activity with confusion and constipation.** Central anticholinergic effects can impair thinking, and reduced bowel motility can cause constipation.
**C. Anticholinergic activity with less delirium.** Greater anticholinergic exposure increases susceptibility to delirium.
**D. Cholinergic activity with fewer falls.** Diphenhydramine has anticholinergic activity, and cumulative exposure is associated with more falls.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2057.

q: A 77-year-old man with moderate frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 6) presents after a mechanical fall. He lives alone, uses a walker, and receives home aide assistance three times weekly. He has lost 8 kg in 12 months. Grip strength is 18 kg, gait speed is 0.5 m/s, and albumin is 2.8 g/dL. His family asks how to help him regain strength. Which intervention has compelling evidence for improving skeletal muscle function in sarcopenia?
o: A daily aerobic walking program replacing the structured resistance exercise program
Regular growth hormone treatment intended to increase muscle mass and limb strength
A progressive resistance exercise program targeting muscle strength in the limbs
Nutritional supplementation replacing the structured exercise program while reducing physical activity
explanation:
Resistance training challenges muscle to generate progressively more force. For this frail man after a fall, **a progressive, individually adapted limb-strengthening program** addresses weakness without assuming that workload is the same for every patient.

**A. Replace resistance work with walking.** Walking trains endurance. It need not strengthen the muscle groups that limit transfers or recovery from a stumble.
**B. Growth hormone.** More lean mass from a drug is not equivalent to better limb strength or daily function.
**C. Progressive resistance exercise.** Select safe loads, supervise initially and increase the load as he gains strength.
**D. Supplements and less activity.** Nutrition can support training. Reducing activity risks further deconditioning.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 737.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA

q: חולה עם דמנציה הוגדרה בישראל כחולה הנוטה למות שאינה בעלת כשרות. לפני הכרעה לגבי רצונה בהארכת חיים, איזה מידע יש לברר לפי סעיף 5(ב)?
o: את רצון הבת שהביעה העדפה לטיפול המרחיב ביותר
את רצון הבן שהביע העדפה לטיפול המצמצם ביותר
הנחיות תקפות, החלטת מיופה כוח או החלטת ועדה
את העדפת הצוות במשמרת שהכיר אותה לאחרונה
explanation:
בירור **רצון חולה שאינה בעלת כשרות** נעשה במסלולים שהחוק מונה. הנחיות מקדימות תקפות, החלטת מיופה כוח לפי תנאי החוק או החלטת ועדה הם מסלולי הבירור בסעיף, ולא העדפת קרוב או איש צוות כשלעצמה (עמ׳ 5, סעיף 5(ב)).
"הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות שנתן שמתקיימות בהן הוראות סעיפים 33 ו-34(א);" (עמ׳ 5).
"החלטה של מיופה כוחו שניתנה לפי ייפוי כוח שמתקיימות בו הוראות סעיפים 38 ו-39(א);" (עמ׳ 5).

**א. את רצון הבת שהביעה העדפה לטיפול המרחיב ביותר.** שגויה, העדפת הבת כשלעצמה אינה אחד המסלולים; יש לברר סמכות ומידע בדבר רצון החולה (עמ׳ 5).
**ב. את רצון הבן שהביע העדפה לטיפול המצמצם ביותר.** שגויה, העדפת הבן כשלעצמה אינה מספיקה גם כשהוא מבקש טיפול מצומצם (עמ׳ 5).
**ג. הנחיות תקפות, החלטת מיופה כוח או החלטת ועדה.** נכונה, אלה המסלולים המפורטים בחוק ויש לבדוק את תוקפם ואת תנאיהם (עמ׳ 5).
**ד. את העדפת הצוות במשמרת שהכיר אותה לאחרונה.** שגויה, העדפה של הצוות אינה מחליפה את בירור הרצון במנגנונים שבסעיף (עמ׳ 5).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס_ו-2005.pdf, עמ׳ 5.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A 76-year-old woman taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation (INR 2.8) develops acute confusion, picks at her clothes, and sees small children in her room. Ciprofloxacin was started three days ago for a UTI. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, pulse 84, blood pressure 142/78 mm Hg, and urine microscopy now shows 0-2 WBC/hpf. Which approach to the new confusion is supported?
o: Attribute the confusion to persistent infection and defer medication review
Evaluate delirium precipitants and review the newly started ciprofloxacin
Attribute the confusion to anticoagulation and defer the broader assessment
Attribute the confusion to dementia and arrange routine cognitive follow-up
explanation:
A newly introduced drug is one potential precipitant of delirium. The timeline matters, particularly when the medication was started for an illness that can also contribute.
**Review the new ciprofloxacin and the infection alongside other causes of the acute change.**

**A. Attribute the confusion to persistent infection and defer medication review.** An infection may still matter, but the temporal relationship to a new drug deserves assessment now.
**B. Evaluate delirium precipitants and review the newly started ciprofloxacin.** The timing makes medication review necessary without proving a single cause.
**C. Attribute the confusion to anticoagulation and defer the broader assessment.** Anticoagulation may affect the assessment if bleeding or trauma is suspected. Its presence alone does not explain the confusion.
**D. Attribute the confusion to dementia and arrange routine cognitive follow-up.** New hallucinations and fluctuating behavior over days require acute evaluation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 885, 887

q: An 80-year-old man with mild dementia develops functional decline and confusion over two weeks after starting tolterodine. Which assessment should precede attribution to dementia progression?
o: Establish progression from the previous dementia diagnosis
Review medication adverse effects and acute medical contributors
Establish a new degenerative disorder from urinary incontinence
Establish chronic deterioration from a lower cognitive test score
explanation:
Neurodegenerative dementia usually changes over months or years. A two-week change after starting tolterodine raises concern for delirium or a medication effect because this bladder drug blocks muscarinic receptors.

**Review medications and acute medical contributors before labeling progression.** The timing supplies a potentially reversible explanation for the confusion.

**A. Progression from known dementia.** Baseline dementia increases vulnerability to delirium. It does not account for the sudden acceleration by itself.
**B. Medication and illness review.** Check when tolterodine was started, other anticholinergic exposure and acute problems such as infection, pain or dehydration.
**C. New disorder from incontinence.** A urinary symptom alone cannot identify a second neurodegenerative disease.
**D. Chronic decline from a test score.** Acute inattention can lower the score. Reassess cognition after treating contributing factors.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 901–905.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: A 73-year-old woman with diabetes is taking metformin and is hospitalized with a major acute illness that may reduce tissue perfusion. Which drug-related concern justifies avoiding metformin in this situation?
o: Development of hypoglycemia through stimulation of insulin secretion.
Development of lactic acidosis in the setting of impaired perfusion.
Development of hyperglycemia through increased hepatic glucose production.
Development of weight gain through an acute increase in appetite.
explanation:
Metformin lowers glucose chiefly by suppressing hepatic glucose production. An acute illness with poor tissue perfusion increases lactate production, and impaired renal clearance can increase metformin exposure.

**The concern is lactic acidosis during hypoperfusion.** Avoid metformin during hospitalization for major illness that can reduce perfusion.

**A. Stimulated insulin secretion.** Metformin does not directly stimulate beta cells and rarely produces hypoglycemia by itself.
**B. Lactic acidosis.** A low-perfusion illness changes the usual safety profile, particularly when kidney function also deteriorates.
**C. Increased hepatic glucose output.** Metformin lowers hepatic output, which is central to its glucose-lowering action.
**D. Acute appetite-related weight gain.** Gastrointestinal discomfort or reduced appetite can occur. Weight gain is not the reason to withhold it here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1576–1577.

q: An 82-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoarthritis has increased evening confusion and fell a week ago. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and amitriptyline 50 mg nightly for chronic pain. Which action directly addresses a strongly anticholinergic medication exposure?
o: Move donepezil administration from evening to morning
Review discontinuation of amitriptyline used for pain
Reduce memantine to 5 mg twice daily
Add a low dose of quetiapine at dinner
explanation:
Amitriptyline is a sedating tricyclic antidepressant with strong anticholinergic effects, even when prescribed for pain.

**Review stopping amitriptyline.** It can worsen confusion and contribute to falls in a man with Alzheimer disease.

**A. Move donepezil to the morning.** Changing when a cholinesterase inhibitor is taken leaves the nightly anticholinergic exposure in place.
**B. Review amitriptyline.** Reassessing this pain treatment addresses both central anticholinergic effects and sedation.
**C. Reduce memantine.** Adjusting a dementia medicine does not remove the strongly anticholinergic pain treatment.
**D. Add quetiapine.** Adding an antipsychotic leaves the possible contributor in place and brings stroke and mortality risks in dementia.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2059, 2066.

q: A 78-year-old woman hospitalized with a COPD exacerbation is to receive antibiotics. She has comorbidities and recent antibiotic exposure. Which principle should guide antibiotic selection according to Hazzard?
o: Treat sputum culture as a reliable way to distinguish colonization from infection
Use sputum volume as sufficient information for choosing the antibiotic spectrum
Consider disease severity, comorbidities, interactions, and local resistance patterns
Treat prior facility exposure and severe obstruction as evidence of lower resistance risk
explanation:
**Antibiotic selection in COPD exacerbations** incorporates patient history and local resistance patterns. Sputum culture is unreliable for guiding the decision, and facility exposure or severe airflow obstruction increases concern for resistant colonizing organisms (p. 1261).
"Choice of antibiotic is driven by a number of factors (history, tolerance, disease severity, comorbidities, medication interactions, prior treatment failure, local patterns of resistance)" (p. 1261).
"sputum culture data is unreliable in guiding decisions." (p. 1261).

**A. Treat sputum culture as a reliable way to distinguish colonization from infection.** Wrong, culture data are described as unreliable for guiding antibiotic decisions, so they do not provide the proposed certainty (p. 1261).
**B. Use sputum volume as sufficient information for choosing the antibiotic spectrum.** Wrong, the selection factors include history, severity, comorbidities, interactions, and resistance; sputum volume does not replace that assessment (p. 1261).
**C. Consider disease severity, comorbidities, interactions, and local resistance patterns.** Correct, these are explicitly listed factors for selecting empiric treatment (p. 1261).
**D. Treat prior facility exposure and severe obstruction as evidence of lower resistance risk.** Wrong, these exposures are associated with a greater likelihood of resistant colonization, not a lower likelihood (p. 1261).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1261.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

q: גבר בן 86 עם מחלת ריאות חסימתית ודמנציה קלה מאושפז בשל דלקת ריאות ונעזר ב־BiPAP. לאחר התייצבות נשימתית הוא מסוגל להשתתף בשיחה. בנו מספר שאביו אמר בעבר שאינו רוצה מכונות שיאריכו את חייו. הצוות טרם בירר את הבנתו ואת רצונו ביחס לטיפול הנוכחי. השאלה מתייחסת לשיחה מתוכננת, ולא להחלטה דחופה במצב חירום. איזה אופן מסירת מידע תואם את דרישות ההסכמה מדעת בחוק זכויות החולה?
o: לתעד את העדפתו בנוגע למכשירים, לקבל החלטה, ואז לפרט את הסיכונים והחלופות
לפרט את האבחנה והתועלת הצפויה, ולהשאיר את הסיכונים לשיחה לאחר החלטתו
לפרט את התועלת, הסיכונים והחלופות, ולוודא שהמידע מאפשר לו בחירה מרצון
לפרט את התועלת והסיכונים של התמיכה, ולהשאיר את היעדר הטיפול מחוץ לדיון
explanation:
**הסכמה מדעת** מחייבת מידע על הטיפול, תועלתו, סיכוניו והחלופות, לרבות היעדר טיפול. מטרת מסירת המידע היא לאפשר למטופל להבין ולבחור מרצונו, ולכן יש למסרו בשלב מוקדם ככל האפשר, ולא לאחר קבלת ההחלטה. הדרישה כאן עוסקת ב**הבנת המידע ובחירה מרצון**, ואינה מכריעה מראש אם להמשיך את התמיכה הנשימתית או להפסיקה (סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8).
"ובאופן שיאפשר למטופל מידה מרבית של הבנת המידע לשם קבלת החלטה בדרך של בחירה מרצון ואי תלות." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. לתעד את העדפתו בנוגע למכשירים, לקבל החלטה, ואז לפרט את הסיכונים והחלופות.** שגויה, העדפה קודמת אינה מחליפה את מסירת המידע הנדרש לצורך ההחלטה הנוכחית. מסירת הסיכונים והחלופות לאחר ההחלטה אינה מאפשרת להם לשמש בסיס לבחירה. זהו יישום של סעיף 13(ב) ושל דרישת מסירת המידע מוקדם ככל האפשר בסעיף 13(ג), עמ׳ 8.
**ב. לפרט את האבחנה והתועלת הצפויה, ולהשאיר את הסיכונים לשיחה לאחר החלטתו.** שגויה, סיכוני הטיפול הם חלק מהמידע הנדרש לקבלת ההסכמה. דיון בהם לאחר ההחלטה משאיר את ההחלטה ללא רכיב מידע שהחוק דורש למסור למטופל (סעיפים 13(ב)(3) ו־13(ג), עמ׳ 8).
**ג. לפרט את התועלת, הסיכונים והחלופות, ולוודא שהמידע מאפשר לו בחירה מרצון.** נכונה, ההסבר כולל רכיבים נדרשים לצורך הבחירה ומכוון להבנתם. החוק דורש מידע על התועלת, הסיכונים והחלופות באופן שמאפשר החלטה מרצון; זהו הבסיס לשיחה המתוארת (סעיפים 13(ב) ו־13(ג), עמ׳ 8).
**ד. לפרט את התועלת והסיכונים של התמיכה, ולהשאיר את היעדר הטיפול מחוץ לדיון.** שגויה, החוק כולל במפורש גם סיכויים וסיכונים של היעדר טיפול. השמטתם מותירה את המטופל ללא מידע נדרש להשוואה בין המשך הטיפול לבין הימנעות ממנו (סעיף 13(ב)(4), עמ׳ 8).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A 75-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment and recurrent falls develops acute agitation on the second day after hip-fracture repair. She pulls at her Foley catheter and has a positive CAM. Assessment finds no continuing need for the catheter and no immediate threat to safety or essential treatment. Which initial step best follows nonpharmacologic delirium care?
o: Begin scheduled haloperidol as initial treatment to suppress agitation
Begin scheduled lorazepam to suppress the agitation
Remove the unnecessary Foley catheter and reorient her
Increase scheduled oxycodone without reassessing pain
explanation:
Catheters can cause discomfort and restrict mobility, both important during postoperative delirium. Remove unnecessary equipment and use familiar cues.
**Remove the Foley because its indication has ended, then reorient and supervise her.**

**A. Begin scheduled haloperidol as initial treatment to suppress agitation.** Scheduled haloperidol offers risks without a persisting safety threat or failed supportive care.
**B. Begin scheduled lorazepam to suppress the agitation.** Lorazepam can suppress alertness and worsen confusion in the absence of withdrawal.
**C. Remove the unnecessary Foley catheter and reorient her.** Removing the object she is pulling at addresses a contributor while permitting movement.
**D. Increase scheduled oxycodone without reassessing pain.** An opioid increase without assessing pain and prior doses can compound confusion.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 887–888, Table 58-5

q: A 77-year-old man takes hydrochlorothiazide, but his blood pressure remains uncontrolled. A switch to chlorthalidone is being considered. Which difference does Hazzard identify?
o: Chlorthalidone has greater potency and a longer half-life
Chlorthalidone has greater potency and a shorter half-life
Chlorthalidone has lower potency and a longer half-life
Chlorthalidone has lower potency and a shorter half-life
explanation:
Chlorthalidone and hydrochlorothiazide are related antihypertensive diuretics with different pharmacokinetics. **Chlorthalidone is more potent and has a longer half-life**.

**A. More potent and longer acting.** It can provide more sustained blood-pressure lowering at a lower milligram dose.
**B. More potent but shorter acting.** The duration is longer, not shorter.
**C. Less potent but longer acting.** The duration fits, but milligram-for-milligram potency is greater.
**D. Less potent and shorter acting.** Both proposed differences are reversed.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1225.

q: An older woman taking sertraline needs analgesia after a fracture, and tramadol is being considered. Which pharmacologic consideration explains particular caution with this combination?
o: Tramadol's serotonergic action favors combining it with an antidepressant for protection
Tramadol's serotonergic action counteracts the effect of the patient's sertraline
Tramadol's serotonergic action is a reason to avoid the combination
Tramadol's serotonergic action favors increasing the doses of both medicines
explanation:
Tramadol provides opioid analgesia and inhibits serotonin reuptake. **Avoid combining it with sertraline when a suitable alternative exists** because the serotonergic effects can add.

**A. Protective combination.** Adding serotonergic exposure increases toxicity risk.
**B. Counteracts sertraline.** Tramadol increases rather than neutralizes serotonergic activity.
**C. Avoid the combination.** Excess serotonin can cause agitation, autonomic instability and neuromuscular abnormalities.
**D. Increase both doses.** Greater exposure increases the risk without improving safety.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1061, 929.

q: An 84-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment, MMSE 23, and heart failure attends after his wife’s sudden death from stroke. He says he does not want to end up connected to machines. His daughter interrupts and says he does not know what he is saying and should receive every treatment. He has no written advance directive and his creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which step is appropriate before transferring decisions to his daughter or writing a treatment-limitation order?
o: Use the family’s preferred plan before assessing his decision-making ability
Assess his capacity for the specific decisions being discussed
Transfer the decisions to his daughter based on the MMSE score
Record a DNR order from the general statement about machines
explanation:
Capacity is specific to the treatment decision. A global cognitive score and a general statement of values cannot determine consent to a particular intervention. **Assess his capacity for the decisions being discussed** and clarify what he means by machines.

**A. Follow the family plan first.** His daughter's preference becomes relevant as a surrogate only if he lacks capacity for the decision.
**B. Assess decision-specific capacity.** Explore what he understands, what he expects to happen to him, how he weighs his options and what he chooses.
**C. Transfer decisions on the MMSE alone.** Cognitive screening cannot decide capacity for a specific treatment.
**D. Write a DNR order immediately.** A statement about machines does not tell you whether he wishes to decline CPR in the circumstances at hand.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 153.
ref: Hazzard Ch 10 — ASSESSMENT OF DECISIONAL CAPACITY AND COMPETENCIES
chapterTitle: Assessment of Decisional Capacity and Competencies

q: אישה כתבה הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות. כעת היא סובלת מקושי בבליעה, אך לא נקבע שהיא חולה הנוטה למות או שאינה בעלת כשרות. מה יש לברר לפני החלת ההנחיות כמסלול ההחלטה לפי חוק זה?
o: האם בני המשפחה מעדיפים את הטיפול המוצע כעת
האם מתקיימים תנאי תחולת החוק וההנחיות
האם עצם קושי הבליעה מספיק להפעלת ההנחיות
האם אבחנת דמנציה מחליפה קביעת מצב וכשרות
explanation:
**הנחיות מקדימות** לפי חוק זה נועדו למצב שבו נקבע שהאדם חולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות. לכן קושי בבליעה או אבחנה קוגניטיבית אינם ממלאים כשלעצמם את התנאים; יש לברר את תחולת המסגרת לפני יישום ההנחיות (עמ׳ 16, סעיפים 30–31; המשפט השני הוא הסקה יישומית).
"אם יהיה חולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות, במתן הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות, בייפוי כוח, או בשילוב ביניהם," (עמ׳ 16).
"אדם בעל כשרות רשאי לתת הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות שבהן יפרט את רצונו לגבי טיפול רפואי עתידי בו אם ייקבע לגביו כי הוא חולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות," (עמ׳ 16).

**א. האם בני המשפחה מעדיפים את הטיפול המוצע כעת.** שגויה, העדפת המשפחה אינה מחליפה את תנאי התחולה שבהם האדם הביע את רצונו מראש (עמ׳ 16).
**ב. האם מתקיימים תנאי תחולת החוק וההנחיות.** נכונה, זהו הבירור הנדרש כדי להתאים את המסמך למצב שבו החוק מייעד את הפעלתו (עמ׳ 16).
**ג. האם עצם קושי הבליעה מספיק להפעלת ההנחיות.** שגויה, סעיף 31 דורש קביעה של מצב חולה נוטה למות ואי כשרות, ולא תסמין בודד (עמ׳ 16).
**ד. האם אבחנת דמנציה מחליפה קביעת מצב וכשרות.** שגויה, דמנציה כשלעצמה אינה שתי הקביעות הנדרשות בסעיף (עמ׳ 16).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס_ו-2005.pdf, עמ׳ 16.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: חולה בגיר בישראל הוגדר כדין כחולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות. קיימות הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות תקפות שנתן, המבקשות טיפול חריג להארכת חיים בתנאים הנדונים. לא מונה מיופה כוח ואין החלטת ועדה; אשתו ובתו חלוקות בדעתן. על מה יש לבסס את קביעת רצונו לפי סעיף 14 לחוק החולה הנוטה למות?
o: על עמדת אשתו ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול
על עמדת בתו ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול
על הנחיותיו המקדימות ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול
על הערכת הצוות ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול
explanation:
לעניין קבלת **טיפול חריג להארכת חיים**, סעיף 14 מפרט כיצד נקבע רצונו של חולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות. אחת הדרכים היא: "על פי הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות שנתן שמתקיימות בהן הוראות סעיפים 33 ו-34(א);" (עמוד 9, סעיף 14(ב)(1)). בשאלה נקבע שההנחיות תקפות ומתייחסות לנסיבות הנדונות; הצהרת אדם קרוב נזכרת בסעיף 14(ג) כאשר אין הנחיות או החלטות מן הסוגים המפורטים בסעיף 14(ב), ולכן מחלוקת המשפחה אינה מחליפה כאן את ההנחיות.

**א. על עמדת אשתו ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול.** שגויה, ההנחיות התקפות כבר מבטאות את רצונו בנסיבות המתוארות. המסלול של הצהרת אדם קרוב חל בהיעדר ההנחיות או ההחלטות המנויות, ולא במקום ההנחיות הקיימות (עמוד 9, סעיף 14(ב) ו־14(ג)).
**ב. על עמדת בתו ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול.** שגויה, עמדת הבת אינה מקבלת קדימות על פני ההנחיות התקפות מחמת המחלוקת המשפחתית; תנאי הפנייה למסלול אדם קרוב אינו מתקיים בשאלה (עמוד 9, סעיף 14(ג)).
**ג. על הנחיותיו המקדימות ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול.** נכונה, החוק מונה את ההנחיות העומדות בדרישותיו כבסיס לקביעת הרצון, והשאלה קובעת שהן תקפות ומתאימות למצב הנדון (עמוד 9, סעיף 14(ב)(1)).
**ד. על הערכת הצוות ביחס לרצונו לקבל את הטיפול.** שגויה, הערכת הצוות לגבי רצונותיו אינה תחליף למקור המפורש שהחוק קובע כאשר קיימות הנחיות תקפות הרלוונטיות למצב זה (עמוד 9, סעיף 14(ב)(1)).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, התשס״ו־2005, סעיף 14, עמוד 9 בעותק המקומי.
