q: גבר בן 79 עם דמנציה וסקולרית וסוכרת מאובחן כקורבן לניצול כלכלי על ידי נכדו, שגנב ממנו 50,000 דולר במשך 6 חודשים. למטופל אין capacity לקבלת החלטות פיננסיות, אך הוא מסרב לתבוע, באומרו 'הוא משפחה.' בתו רוצה להגיש תלונה פלילית ולהעביר אותו למתקן memory care. הנכד הוא המטפל העיקרי שלו והם חיים יחד שנים. מה הפעולה המתאימה ביותר של העובד הסוציאלי?
o: לתמוך בתוכנית הבת להגשת תלונה ולהעברה למתקן
לדווח ל-APS ולאפשר להם לחקור תוך שמירה על מסגרת המגורים הנוכחית
לארגן גישור משפחתי לטיפול בניצול הכלכלי
להסדיר representative payee עבור Social Security בלבד
explanation:
התשובה הנכונה היא דיווח ל-APS תוך שמירה על מסגרת המגורים הנוכחית במהלך החקירה. עובדים סוציאליים הם mandated reporters לניצול כלכלי. APS יכול לחקור, לפעול לשחזור הכספים, ולהטמיע אמצעי הגנה מבלי לפגוע בקשרי הטיפול הקיימים.

אופציה A (תלונה פלילית והעברה למתקן) היא המלכודת הקלאסית — משפחות לעיתים קרובות רוצות פעולה דרמטית מיידית, אך הסרת מטפל ותיק עלולה לפגוע במטופל יותר מהנזק הכלכלי עצמו. הגשת תלונה פלילית מצריכה שיתוף פעולה של הקורבן, שאינו קיים כאן.

אופציה C (גישור משפחתי) אינה מתאימה לניצול ברמת פשע חמור (felony). היא ממזערת את החומרה ומפרה את חובת הדיווח החובה.

אופציה D (representative payee) מגנה על הכנסת Social Security בלבד, ולא על שאר הנכסים. היא אינה מספיקה מבלי לטפל בדפוס הניצול הרחב יותר.

נקודה קלינית: ניצול כלכלי על ידי בני משפחה מהווה כ-60% ממקרי התעללות בקשישים. קורבנות לעיתים קרובות מסרבים לתבוע בשל נאמנות, תלות, או פחד. APS יכול להטמיע הסדרים הגנתיים (trusts, guardianships מוגבלים) ללא הליך פלילי, תוך שמירה על הקשרים ומניעת ניצול נוסף.
retiredReason: US health-system policy (Medicare, Medicaid, PACE, US federal law or agency); not part of the Israeli exam.

q: An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, and mild cognitive impairment attends routine follow-up. His daughter reports two falls during the past month, both at night while getting up to use the toilet. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, zolpidem 10 mg at bedtime, and aspirin 81 mg daily. Blood pressure is 138/82 sitting and 118/70 after three minutes standing. Which interpretation of zolpidem is consistent with Beers 2023?
o: Its association with falls supports planning discontinuation during medication review
Its nonbenzodiazepine structure supports retaining treatment despite recurrent falls
Its substantial improvement in sleep duration supports retaining treatment for insomnia
Its protection against delirium supports retaining treatment despite cognitive impairment
explanation:
Zolpidem is a nighttime sedative with modest sleep benefit and a risk of falls, delirium, and fractures in older adults.

**Plan discontinuation during medication review.** He may still be sedated when he gets up at night to use the toilet. His postural pressure drop warrants separate attention.

**A. Review for discontinuation.** Removing a bedtime sedative addresses one potentially reversible contributor to nocturnal falls.
**B. Retain because it is not a benzodiazepine.** Zolpidem can produce similar adverse effects on alertness and balance despite its different chemical structure.
**C. Retain for substantial sleep benefit.** The average improvement in sleep duration or latency is small.
**D. Retain for delirium prevention.** Zolpidem can precipitate or worsen delirium, especially in a vulnerable older adult.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2060.

q: The organism in a urine culture from a woman with pyelonephritis is susceptible to nitrofurantoin. Why does this susceptibility result not make nitrofurantoin appropriate for this infection?
o: Its activity is directed toward renal tissue more than toward the urine
Its effectiveness for bladder infection also supports its use for renal infection
Its renal penetration is inadequate for treating this complicated urinary infection
Its limitation reflects bacterial resistance rather than inadequate delivery into renal tissue
explanation:
Pyelonephritis is infection of kidney tissue. An antibiotic must be active against the organism and reach that tissue. **Nitrofurantoin concentrates in urine but has inadequate renal tissue penetration**.

**A. Greater kidney tissue than urine activity.** This reverses its useful distribution.
**B. Bladder efficacy predicts kidney efficacy.** Cystitis exposes bacteria to urinary drug levels. Kidney infection requires adequate tissue levels.
**C. Poor renal tissue penetration.** A susceptible laboratory result cannot compensate for inadequate drug delivery at the infected site.
**D. Resistance is the explanation.** The organism is susceptible in this vignette. The limitation is pharmacologic.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1709, 1711.

q: An 88-year-old man with mild dementia, BPH, osteoarthritis, and insomnia has become increasingly confused over three days and no longer recognizes family. One week ago he started diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily. Vital signs are stable and CAM screening is positive. Which medication plan applies Beers 2023 guidance to minimize his anticholinergic burden?
o: Discontinue both diphenhydramine and oxybutynin, then reassess symptoms.
Replace diphenhydramine with oral doxylamine and continue oxybutynin.
Replace oxybutynin with oral tolterodine and continue diphenhydramine.
Continue both diphenhydramine and oxybutynin while monitoring symptoms.
explanation:
Starting two strong anticholinergics together can increase confusion and fall risk. Both new drugs belong in the immediate review of this man’s delirium.

**Stop diphenhydramine and oxybutynin and reassess.** Removing both exposures gives his cognition a chance to improve while other causes are investigated.

**A. Stop both.** This removes the new antihistamine and bladder antimuscarinic that together increased his burden.
**B. Use doxylamine and retain oxybutynin.** Doxylamine is another strongly anticholinergic antihistamine, so the combination persists.
**C. Use tolterodine and retain diphenhydramine.** Tolterodine is also a bladder antimuscarinic, so two anticholinergic drugs remain.
**D. Monitor both.** Observation while continuing both drugs leaves the potentially reversible burden unchanged.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2066, 2070, 2074.
label: Source: AGS Beers 2023 · pp. 2066, 2070, 2074; Tables 3, 5, 7

q: A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?
o: Metformin is the higher-risk drug because its main effect is to stimulate insulin secretion.
Glyburide is the higher-risk drug because its long half-life increases hypoglycemia risk in older patients.
Metformin and glyburide have similarly low hypoglycemia risk when used as single agents.
Glyburide is the lower-risk drug because its long half-life reduces hypoglycemia risk in older patients.
explanation:
Glyburide drives beta-cell insulin release for a relatively long time. Metformin chiefly reduces hepatic glucose output and carries low hypoglycemia risk on its own.

**Glyburide is the higher-risk drug.** Medication errors, cognitive impairment and impaired renal function make prolonged hypoglycemia especially consequential here.

**A. Metformin stimulates insulin secretion.** This describes a sulfonylurea rather than the main action of metformin.
**B. Glyburide has a long half-life.** An extra dose or a missed meal can leave insulin action exceeding available glucose for hours.
**C. Both drugs have low risk alone.** The sulfonylurea adds substantial hypoglycemia risk even without another glucose-lowering drug.
**D. Longer action makes glyburide safer.** Longer action makes a low harder to reverse durably.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1576–1577, 1579.

q: An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, depression, and chronic pain from spinal stenosis attends a medication review. His wife reports increasing daytime sedation and two near-falls. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, tramadol 50 mg four times daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. He also takes oral diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Which characteristic of diphenhydramine explains the Beers recommendation to avoid this use?
o: Accelerated clearance in advanced age, requiring higher doses to sustain a hypnotic effect.
Reduced likelihood of confusion with regular use, despite development of tolerance during treatment.
Strong anticholinergic effects and confusion risk, with cumulative exposure associated with increased falls.
Progressively enhanced hypnotic efficacy with repeated use, supporting dose reduction during continued treatment.
explanation:
Diphenhydramine can sedate through histamine blockade and impair thinking through anticholinergic effects. Tolerance to its sleep effect can develop even as adverse effects remain.

**Strong anticholinergic activity raises confusion risk, and cumulative exposure is associated with falls.** Nightly use is particularly relevant in a man with sedation and near-falls.

**A. Faster clearance calls for more drug.** Clearance tends to fall with age, so increasing the dose to sustain sleep risks greater exposure.
**B. Less confusion with regular use.** Tolerance to the sleep effect provides no protection from anticholinergic confusion.
**C. Anticholinergic burden and falls.** Muscarinic blockade can impair thinking, and repeated exposure adds to the medication-related fall risk.
**D. Progressively better sleep effect.** Repeated use can produce tolerance, diminishing the hypnotic benefit.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2057.

q: A 75-year-old woman with mild dementia, hypertension, and osteoporosis has attended the emergency department three times in two months for nonspecific discomfort, with normal investigations. She takes 12 medications prescribed by four physicians, and her daughter reports increasing forgetfulness with medication-taking. Vital signs and laboratory results are normal. Which initial approach supports medication optimization?
o: Select medications to discontinue by pill count before establishing their indications
Arrange a comprehensive medication review with the patient and a pharmacist
Change dosing schedules before establishing which medications are actually taken
Add a cognitive medication before reviewing the current treatment indications
explanation:
A medication review connects every drug a patient actually takes to its indication, benefit, and potential harm. With four prescribers and forgetfulness, each list may tell only part of the story.

**Review the whole regimen with the patient and a pharmacist.** Clarifying actual use can uncover discrepancies, adverse effects, and opportunities to simplify dosing.

**A. Stop by pill count.** The number of pills signals burden but cannot identify which drug can be safely withdrawn.
**B. Patient and pharmacist review.** Discuss how she takes medicines and compare accounts across prescribers before deciding what to change.
**C. Change schedules immediately.** A new schedule based on an inaccurate list may preserve duplicates or omit an indicated drug.
**D. Add a cognitive medicine.** Adding treatment before reviewing causes of forgetfulness and discomfort risks increasing the existing burden.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 311, 313.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with dementia and chronic kidney disease was hospitalized for suspected digoxin toxicity, and digoxin was withheld. After treatment of the acute event and stabilization, her medicines are reviewed before discharge. Digoxin was prescribed years ago for a poorly documented indication. Current echocardiography shows preserved systolic function and the ECG shows sinus rhythm, but previous cardiac records have not yet been reviewed. What should guide the long-term digoxin decision?
o: Use the duration of the previous prescription as the basis for restarting treatment given for years
Use her tolerability before hospitalization as the basis for restarting treatment she previously tolerated
Use the current sinus rhythm as the basis for stopping treatment prescribed before this examination
Use the current indication and balance of benefits and harms in an updated medication review
explanation:
Digoxin has a narrow margin between benefit and toxicity, particularly when renal clearance falls. A hospitalization for suspected toxicity is a reason to revisit why the drug was prescribed.

**Base the decision on the current indication and balance of benefits and harms.** Review prior cardiac records, present systolic function and rhythm, and the risk of another toxic episode.

**A. Restart because it was prescribed for years.** Duration documents past use but supplies no evidence of continuing benefit.
**B. Restart because she tolerated it before.** Previous tolerance cannot predict safety after an episode of suspected toxicity in chronic kidney disease.
**C. Stop on today’s sinus rhythm alone.** A single ECG cannot reconstruct the prior arrhythmia, its course, or the original treatment goal.
**D. Review the indication and net benefit.** Previous records and current cardiac and renal status inform whether continued exposure is justified.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 312.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 78-year-old woman with chronic constipation is starting senna. Which instruction about taking the medication is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Take it on waking because evacuation follows immediately after swallowing
Take it after each meal because its effect depends on food volume
Take it at bedtime because evacuation follows several hours after dosing
Take it at the urge to defecate because it acts locally in the rectum
explanation:
Senna stimulates colonic motility after a delay of about 8 to 12 hours. **Bedtime dosing** commonly produces a bowel movement the next morning.

**A. Take for an immediate morning effect.** Oral senna takes hours to work.
**B. Take after every meal.** Its onset depends on colonic processing and action, not the volume of the preceding meal.
**C. Take at bedtime.** The delayed onset aligns the response with the following morning.
**D. Wait for an urge.** Oral senna does not act immediately as a local rectal rescue.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1372.

q: An 85-year-old man develops sleepiness and falls after starting temazepam for insomnia. Medication review leads to a decision to stop benzodiazepine treatment for sleep. Which plan implements that decision?
o: Arrange supervised tapering and discontinuation of temazepam
Arrange replacement of temazepam with nighttime lorazepam treatment
Arrange replacement of temazepam with nighttime flurazepam treatment
Arrange replacement of temazepam with nighttime quazepam treatment
explanation:
**Benzodiazepine hypnotics** can cause confusion, falls, and withdrawal symptoms when discontinued. A discontinuation plan should account for withdrawal risk; replacing temazepam with another benzodiazepine does not implement the decision to stop the class (pp. 659, 885).
"The side effects associated with this class of medications include confusion, falls, rebound insomnia, tolerance, and withdrawal symptoms on discontinuation." (p. 659).
"Medications with potential for withdrawal should be tapered carefully." (p. 885).

**A. Arrange supervised tapering and discontinuation of temazepam.** Correct, it implements the decision while allowing careful tapering of a medication with withdrawal potential (pp. 659, 885).
**B. Arrange replacement of temazepam with nighttime lorazepam treatment.** Wrong, lorazepam is another benzodiazepine used for insomnia, so substitution continues the class that the team decided to stop (p. 659).
**C. Arrange replacement of temazepam with nighttime flurazepam treatment.** Wrong, flurazepam is a longer-acting benzodiazepine discouraged in older adults because of next-day effects (p. 659).
**D. Arrange replacement of temazepam with nighttime quazepam treatment.** Wrong, quazepam is also a longer-acting benzodiazepine discouraged because of next-day effects, and substitution continues benzodiazepine exposure (p. 659).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 659, 885.

q: An older woman takes warfarin together with an SSRI. If the combination is needed, which risk and monitoring recommendation matches Beers 2023?
o: Reduced bleeding risk and less frequent INR monitoring
Increased bleeding risk and close INR monitoring
Reduced bleeding risk and close INR monitoring
Increased bleeding risk and less frequent INR monitoring
explanation:
Warfarin lowers vitamin K-dependent clotting activity, while SSRIs reduce uptake of serotonin into platelets and can impair serotonin-dependent platelet aggregation. **When both drugs are needed, anticipate more bleeding, monitor INR closely and assess clinically for bleeding.** A therapeutic INR cannot exclude the platelet effect.

**A. Less bleeding and fewer INR checks.** The drugs act on different parts of hemostasis, so their combination can add risk rather than reduce it.
**B. More bleeding and close INR monitoring.** Review INR after medication changes, and ask about bruising, nosebleeds, melena or other bleeding even when INR is in range.
**C. Less bleeding with close INR checks.** Close INR monitoring is appropriate, but it does not cancel impaired platelet aggregation.
**D. More bleeding with fewer checks.** Infrequent INR review could miss excess warfarin effect. Clinical surveillance is needed in addition.

Reference · AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Table 5, p. 2071.

q: An 80-year-old man with moderate dementia, diabetes, and hypertension is found on the floor, confused and sweating, with glucose 42 mg/dL. He lives alone with weekly family visits. He takes glimepiride 4 mg twice daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily; his recent HbA1c is 6.8%. After treatment with dextrose, which change removes the long-acting sulfonylurea exposure highlighted by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Continue glimepiride at a lower dose and reassess glucose readings.
Stop glimepiride and reassess the remaining diabetes regimen.
Stop metformin and retain glimepiride as the diabetes treatment.
Add glucose monitoring and retain the current glimepiride dose.
explanation:
Glimepiride stimulates insulin release and can cause prolonged hypoglycemia. Living alone with dementia makes recurrent low glucose especially dangerous.

**Stop glimepiride and reassess the remaining regimen.** Dextrose treats the immediate glucose of 42 mg/dL, while removing the long-acting drug addresses recurrence.

**A. Lower the dose.** A smaller dose still leaves exposure to a long-acting secretagogue after severe hypoglycemia.
**B. Stop glimepiride.** This removes the agent most directly implicated and allows the glycemic goal and other drugs to be reconsidered.
**C. Stop metformin instead.** Keeping glimepiride preserves the prolonged insulin-secretagogue effect.
**D. Monitor without reducing exposure.** Monitoring may detect another low but cannot prevent the unchanged dose from causing one.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2061.

q: A 77-year-old woman with symptomatic heart failure takes naproxen for chronic pain. What concern about this treatment follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Continue treatment because it reduces fluid retention
Avoid treatment because of fluid-retention risk
Continue treatment because it protects against worsening heart failure
Avoid treatment because it promotes excessive fluid removal
explanation:
NSAIDs such as naproxen can promote sodium and water retention. In symptomatic heart failure, retained fluid can aggravate congestion.

**Avoid naproxen because of fluid-retention risk.** Another analgesic strategy is preferable when heart failure is symptomatic.

**A. Continue for less retention.** NSAID exposure can increase retention.
**B. Avoid because of retention.** Worsening fluid overload is the relevant drug–disease interaction.
**C. Continue for heart failure protection.** Naproxen offers no protection against decompensation and can worsen symptoms.
**D. Avoid because it removes too much fluid.** The concern is sodium and water retained in the body, the opposite of excessive diuresis.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2065.

q: An 83-year-old woman with recurrent urinary tract infections has stopped long-term nitrofurantoin prophylaxis after medical review. She has no active infection and no history of estrogen-dependent cancer. Which nonantibiotic option does Hazzard recommend considering to prevent recurrences?
o: Consider an oral cranberry product as part of prevention.
Consider vaginal estrogen as part of prevention.
Consider an oral vitamin C supplement as part of prevention.
Consider methenamine as part of prevention.
explanation:
**Vaginal estrogen** addresses the decline in vaginal lactobacilli associated with lower estrogen levels in older women. Hazzard describes it as potentially effective for prevention and distinguishes it from agents for which evidence is insufficient to make a recommendation (pp. 1713–1714). "Topical estrogen appears to be a safe and potentially effective method for prevention of UTI in postmenopausal women." (p. 1713).

**A. Consider an oral cranberry product as part of prevention.** Wrong, cranberry evidence is inconsistent; the review cited on the following page found insufficient evidence to recommend for or against it (pp. 1713–1714).
**B. Consider vaginal estrogen as part of prevention.** Correct, this is the option recommended for consideration in older women with recurrent UTI (p. 1713).
**C. Consider an oral vitamin C supplement as part of prevention.** Wrong, ascorbic acid is among the agents for which the review found insufficient evidence to recommend for or against use (p. 1714).
**D. Consider methenamine as part of prevention.** Wrong, methenamine hippurate is also in that insufficient-evidence group in this source; the question asks for Hazzard's recommendation (p. 1714).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1713, 1714.

q: A 79-year-old man with Parkinson disease develops visual hallucinations during dopaminergic treatment. Acute contributors have been assessed, and the team suspects a medication contribution. Which medication-review approach does Hazzard describe?
o: Consider increasing dopaminergic treatment to reduce the hallucinations
Consider reducing dopaminergic treatment as tolerated and reviewing other medications
Consider abruptly stopping levodopa to assess a rapid change in hallucinations
Consider adding hallucination treatment in place of reviewing the existing medications
explanation:
Visual hallucinations can emerge when dopaminergic treatment that helps movement also affects perception. Their timing relative to medication changes helps identify an exposure that can be adjusted.

**Reduce dopaminergic treatment as tolerated and review the other medicines.** An anticholinergic, opioid or benzodiazepine can contribute to confusion alongside the Parkinson drugs.

**A. Increase dopaminergic treatment.** Escalating exposure can intensify medication-related hallucinations.
**B. Reduce and review.** Adjust gradually, watching whether the hallucinations abate and whether rigidity or immobility returns.
**C. Stop levodopa abruptly.** Sudden withdrawal risks a severe rigidity-and-fever syndrome.
**D. Add a treatment without reviewing medicines.** An antipsychotic may help persistent, distressing symptoms. It leaves a potentially reversible drug effect unaddressed if used alone.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 946.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS

q: An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with severe dementia, dysphagia, and pressure ulcers has lost 15% of her weight in six months despite speech therapy and nutritional supplements. Her family asks about tube feeding during a goals-of-care review. Her medications include donepezil, memantine, mirtazapine for appetite, and megestrol. Which prescribing approach best follows Hazzard's general principles?
o: Continue the existing regimen because the drugs were previously indicated
Stop the cognitive drugs by class while leaving appetite drugs unreviewed
Stop the appetite drugs by class while leaving cognitive drugs unreviewed
Review the full regimen and deprescribe drugs lacking current benefit
explanation:
Deprescribing asks whether each treatment still offers a benefit the patient values. Advanced dementia, dysphagia, and continued weight loss can change the balance since medicines were started.

**Review all four drugs and deprescribe those lacking current benefit.** Discuss cognitive symptoms, appetite, comfort, swallowing burden, and treatment goals with the family.

**A. Continue every previous indication.** Prior appropriateness cannot substitute for evidence of current benefit or tolerability.
**B. Stop only cognitive drugs.** Class-wide withdrawal overlooks individual response and leaves the appetite drugs unassessed.
**C. Stop only appetite drugs.** This approach omits the benefits and burdens of the dementia medicines.
**D. Review the entire regimen.** A decision about each drug can follow its present purpose, observed effect, and consistency with goals of care.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 314–315.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue and difficulty shopping after amitriptyline was added for neuropathic pain. Her blood pressure falls on standing. Her other medications include metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin, and aspirin. Which change removes the newly introduced drug identified by Beers as strongly anticholinergic, sedating, and liable to cause orthostatic hypotension?
o: Discontinue amitriptyline as the newly added medication
Replace glyburide with insulin while continuing the amitriptyline
Reduce lisinopril dosage while continuing the amitriptyline
Add donepezil for cognition while continuing the amitriptyline
explanation:
Amitriptyline can cause sedation, anticholinergic symptoms, and orthostatic hypotension. The onset of fatigue and impaired shopping after it was added makes a medication effect plausible.

**Discontinue the newly added amitriptyline.** This removes a drug that can worsen standing symptoms and daily function.

**A. Stop amitriptyline.** Withdrawal addresses the exposure that preceded the new problems.
**B. Replace glyburide with insulin.** Diabetes treatment merits its own assessment, but this change would leave the new tricyclic in place.
**C. Reduce lisinopril.** A blood-pressure review may be relevant, but it does not remove amitriptyline’s sedation or anticholinergic effects.
**D. Add donepezil.** Treating cognition while retaining a potentially impairing drug adds burden and misses the temporal clue.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2059.

q: An 84-year-old man is admitted from assisted living with three days of confusion, agitation, daytime somnolence, and nighttime restlessness. He has benign prostatic hyperplasia, osteoarthritis, and mild Alzheimer dementia. He takes tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly started one week ago for insomnia. Temperature is 37.1°C, blood pressure 142/84, pulse 78, and oxygen saturation 96%. He is inattentive and disoriented; urinalysis and chest radiography are normal. Which change removes the recently introduced strongly anticholinergic exposure during evaluation?
o: Start quetiapine while continuing the existing medication regimen
Stop diphenhydramine while reviewing the remaining medication regimen
Add melatonin while continuing the existing medication regimen
Increase memantine while continuing the existing medication regimen
explanation:
New inattention, disorientation, and disturbed sleep over days suggest delirium. Diphenhydramine was recently added and has strong anticholinergic effects.

**Stop diphenhydramine while reviewing the full regimen and other delirium triggers.** The timing identifies a reversible contributor without proving a single cause.

**A. Add quetiapine.** An antipsychotic would target behavior while leaving the recent anticholinergic exposure in place.
**B. Stop diphenhydramine.** Removing the new nightly antihistamine directly lowers anticholinergic burden during evaluation.
**C. Add melatonin.** This might change sleep management, but continuing diphenhydramine preserves the suspected contributor.
**D. Increase memantine.** Escalating dementia treatment does not address a new drug associated with acute confusion.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2066, 2074.

q: A 79-year-old woman with diabetes takes metformin. Her eGFR has fallen to 28 mL/min/1.73 m². Considering the renal appropriateness of metformin separately from treatment of congestion, which action follows Hazzard?
o: Stop metformin because the renal contraindication is present
Continue metformin because its hypoglycemia risk is low
Increase metformin because appetite and weight have declined
Switch to extended-release metformin and continue treatment
explanation:
Metformin is eliminated by the kidney. Its usual glucose-lowering benefits need to be weighed against accumulation in advanced renal impairment.

**Stop metformin at eGFR 28 mL/min/1.73 m².** This is below the 30 threshold, independently of whether congestion is the patient's immediate symptom.

**A. Stop for the renal contraindication.** The measured filtration rate crosses the threshold for discontinuation.
**B. Continue because it rarely causes hypoglycemia.** Low hypoglycemia risk does not protect against accumulation and lactic acidosis.
**C. Increase for weight or appetite loss.** These findings do not justify a higher dose and poor intake adds further concern.
**D. Switch to extended release.** The formulation changes gastrointestinal tolerability, not renal clearance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1576–1577, Table 99-11.

q: An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, BPH, and insomnia reports dizziness on standing and three falls in the past month. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, terazosin 5 mg at bedtime, zolpidem 10 mg nightly, and recently added oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily. Blood pressure falls from 145/85 supine to 118/70 standing with dizziness. Which pair combines a nonselective peripheral alpha-1 blocker with a strongly anticholinergic drug in Beers 2023?
o: Terazosin and carbidopa/levodopa.
Zolpidem and carbidopa/levodopa.
Zolpidem and oxybutynin.
Terazosin and oxybutynin.
explanation:
Terazosin blocks peripheral alpha-1 receptors and can lower standing blood pressure. Oxybutynin blocks muscarinic receptors and adds a separate cognitive and fall concern.

**Terazosin and oxybutynin are the requested pair.** The measured pressure drop makes the alpha blocker particularly relevant.

**A. Terazosin and carbidopa/levodopa.** Terazosin fits the first class, but the dopaminergic Parkinson treatment is not a bladder antimuscarinic.
**B. Zolpidem and carbidopa/levodopa.** These are a hypnotic and a Parkinson treatment. Neither supplies the alpha-blocker–anticholinergic pairing.
**C. Zolpidem and oxybutynin.** Oxybutynin supplies strong anticholinergic activity, but zolpidem is a sedative hypnotic.
**D. Terazosin and oxybutynin.** The first can cause orthostasis through alpha blockade, and the second contributes strong anticholinergic exposure.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, pp. 2058, 2060, 2074.

q: A 77-year-old care-home resident has become restless over the past two days, without clear-cut delirium. She has no fever, instability, or new urinary symptoms. Staff ask whether to start antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. What is appropriate initially?
o: Start oral antibiotics and assess her subsequent response
Review hydration, medications, and other causes, with follow-up
Transfer her for intravenous antibiotics because of the behavioral change
Obtain a routine urine culture and base treatment on its result
explanation:
Restlessness is nonspecific and can arise from pain, dehydration, medications or the care environment. In a stable resident without new urinary symptoms, **assess those causes and arrange follow-up**.

**A. Start antibiotics as a diagnostic trial.** Improvement or fluctuation would not prove a urinary cause.
**B. Review hydration and medicines.** This looks for reversible explanations while monitoring for emerging illness.
**C. Transfer for IV antibiotics.** Behavioral change alone does not indicate severe bacterial infection.
**D. Culture routinely and treat the result.** A positive culture can detect colonization rather than explain the behavior.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1704.

q: An 83-year-old man with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation weighs 68 kg and has serum creatinine of 1.9 mg/dL. Clinical assessment has found him suitable for apixaban. According to the Hazzard dosing table, which pair of his findings meets two dose-reduction criteria?
o: His age and his recorded body weight
His age and his serum creatinine level
His body weight and his atrial-fibrillation type
His body weight and his serum creatinine level
explanation:
**Apixaban dose reduction** in the cited table requires at least two listed criteria (p. 1205). The table specifies “Age ≥ 80”, “Body weight < 60 kg”, and “Serum creatinine ≥ 1.5 mg/dL” (p. 1205). This patient meets the age and creatinine criteria but not the weight criterion.

**A. His age and his recorded body weight.** Wrong, his age qualifies, but 68 kg is not below the table’s 60 kg weight threshold (p. 1205).
**B. His age and his serum creatinine level.** Correct, age 83 and creatinine 1.9 mg/dL each satisfy a listed criterion (p. 1205).
**C. His body weight and his atrial-fibrillation type.** Wrong, his weight does not qualify, and atrial-fibrillation type is not one of the three listed reduction criteria (p. 1205).
**D. His body weight and his serum creatinine level.** Wrong, creatinine qualifies but weight does not, so this pair does not supply two criteria (p. 1205).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1205.

q: A 79-year-old woman has a TSH of 8.2 mIU/L and a normal free T4 on initial testing. There is no acute illness requiring immediate intervention. What is needed before diagnosing persistent subclinical hypothyroidism?
o: Repeat thyroid tests to check whether the abnormality persists.
Attribute her symptoms to thyroid disease and begin long-term replacement.
Diagnose overt hypothyroidism from the initial elevated TSH result.
Diagnose dementia progression from the initial elevated TSH result.
explanation:
A TSH of 8.2 with normal free T4 suggests a subclinical pattern, but mild elevations can fluctuate. **Repeat thyroid tests to confirm persistence** before deciding on treatment.

**A. Repeat TSH and free T4.** Repeat testing distinguishes a persistent abnormality from a transient TSH elevation.
**B. Attribute symptoms and start replacement.** Common nonspecific symptoms can have other causes and this is a first measurement.
**C. Diagnose overt hypothyroidism.** Overt primary hypothyroidism ordinarily requires low free T4.
**D. Diagnose dementia progression.** A thyroid test cannot establish a trajectory of cognitive decline.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1553.

q: An older patient develops muscle pain while taking a statin. The CK level is 12 times the upper limit of normal. Which action concerning the statin is supported by Hazzard?
o: Continue the current statin dose while monitoring the muscle pain
Increase the current statin dose to improve cardiovascular protection
Discontinue the statin because of the degree of CK elevation
Continue the current statin dose and add an exercise program
explanation:
Creatine kinase (CK) rises when muscle fibers are injured. In a symptomatic statin user, a CK level more than ten times the upper limit of normal warrants **discontinuing the statin** and evaluating the muscle injury.

**A. Continue and monitor pain.** With a twelvefold elevation, symptom observation alone leaves the suspected cause in place.
**B. Increase the statin.** Further exposure can aggravate muscle injury.
**C. Discontinue the statin.** The CK elevation crosses the threshold for stopping therapy and assessing complications.
**D. Continue and add exercise.** Exercise does not remove the suspected drug cause and can itself elevate CK.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1598.
ref: Hazzard Ch 100 — MYOPATHIES, POLYMYALGIA RHEUMATICA, AND GIANT CELL ARTERITIS
chapterTitle: Myopathies, Polymyalgia Rheumatica, and Giant Cell Arteritis

q: An older woman takes gabapentin and has a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min. Which adjustment follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Increase the dose to compensate for reduced kidney function
Reduce the dose because of central nervous system adverse effects
Maintain the dose and substitute liver tests for renal adjustment
Maintain the dose and substitute blood counts for renal adjustment
explanation:
Gabapentin depends on the kidneys for clearance. Accumulation can produce central nervous system effects such as drowsiness or confusion.

**Reduce gabapentin at a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min.** The renal adjustment threshold is below 60 mL/min.

**A. Increase the dose.** Less efficient elimination increases exposure to a given dose, making escalation hazardous.
**B. Reduce the dose.** A lower dose limits accumulation and central adverse effects.
**C. Monitor liver tests instead.** Hepatic monitoring cannot compensate for reduced renal elimination.
**D. Monitor blood counts instead.** A blood count neither measures gabapentin clearance nor prevents dose-related CNS effects.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2073.

q: בישראל, מטופלת נקבעה כחולה הנוטה למות שאינה בעלת כשרות. אין לצוות מסמך זמין המתעד את רצונה. איזה צעד מחייב החוק לצורך בירור הרצון?
o: להסיק את רצונה מתוך הערכת חומרת הדמנציה הנוכחית
להסיק את רצונה מתוך מדיניות הטיפול הנהוגה במחלקה
לאסוף מידע רלוונטי במאמץ סביר לבירור רצונה
להסיק את רצונה מתוך העדפת הצוות לגבי תוכנית הטיפול
explanation:
**בירור רצון החולה** דורש מאמץ לאסוף את הנתונים והמסמכים הנוגעים בדבר. חומרת המחלה או העדפת הצוות אינן תחליף לבירור שהחוק מטיל על הרופא האחראי או מי שהוסמך לכך (סעיף 9, עמ׳ 7).
"יעשה מאמץ סביר כדי לקבל את כל הנתונים והמסמכים הנוגעים בדבר, לצורך בירור רצונו של החולה הנוטה למות" (עמ׳ 7).

**א. להסיק את רצונה מתוך הערכת חומרת הדמנציה הנוכחית.** שגויה, חומרת הדמנציה אינה מחליפה איסוף מידע על רצון המטופלת (עמ׳ 7).
**ב. להסיק את רצונה מתוך מדיניות הטיפול הנהוגה במחלקה.** שגויה, מדיניות כללית אינה ממלאת את החובה לברר את רצון החולה המסוימת (עמ׳ 7).
**ג. לאסוף מידע רלוונטי במאמץ סביר לבירור רצונה.** נכונה, זהו הצעד שהחוק מחייב כאשר החולה נוטה למות ואינה בעלת כשרות (עמ׳ 7).
**ד. להסיק את רצונה מתוך העדפת הצוות לגבי תוכנית הטיפול.** שגויה, העדפת הצוות אינה הנתונים שעליו לאסוף על רצון החולה (עמ׳ 7).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 7.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: An older adult with chronic pain, cognitive impairment, and sedating medications asks about adding cannabis. Which safety consideration does Hazzard emphasize?
o: Cannabis may offset memory impairment caused by other medications
Cannabis may reduce the effects of concurrently used sedating substances
Cannabis may worsen memory impairment and contribute to medication interactions
Cannabis may reduce the adverse effects of the existing medication combination
explanation:
Cannabis can impair short-term memory and add to the effects of sedating drugs. In an older adult already experiencing cognitive impairment, **worsening recall and medication interactions** both matter when considering cannabis for pain.

**A. Improve memory.** Cannabis can make it harder to learn and recall new information, compounding existing forgetfulness.
**B. Counteract sedation.** Drowsiness may increase when cannabis is combined with other centrally acting sedatives.
**C. Worsen memory and interact.** Poorer recall can lead to missed or duplicate doses. Concurrent sedatives can further impair alertness.
**D. Reduce existing adverse effects.** Adding another psychoactive substance can compound dizziness and unsteadiness, increasing fall risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 321.
ref: Hazzard Ch 23 — SUBSTANCE USE AND DISORDERS

q: An 80-year-old woman is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. Evaluation and treatment of the causes are ongoing. Despite nonpharmacologic measures, her behavior threatens her safety and interrupts essential treatment. Which prescribing principle applies?
o: Start at a full dose to obtain a rapid, predictable response
Plan prolonged treatment to prevent later recurrence of confusion
Use the lowest starting dose for the shortest necessary duration
Treat improved agitation as evidence that the causes have resolved
explanation:
Drug treatment for agitation has a safety goal and a limited duration. An older person with pneumonia can be particularly vulnerable to sedation.
**Start at the lowest effective dose, reassess the patient and discontinue as soon as the safety indication has resolved.**

**A. Start at a full dose to obtain a rapid, predictable response.** Full initial doses risk oversedation and may obscure deterioration.
**B. Plan prolonged treatment to prevent later recurrence of confusion.** There is no indication to continue an antipsychotic for prevention once the acute threat resolves.
**C. Use the lowest starting dose for the shortest necessary duration.** Short, cautious treatment preserves the ability to follow cognition and clinical status.
**D. Treat improved agitation as evidence that the causes have resolved.** Improved behavior does not show that infection or other contributors have resolved.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 888–889

q: A 77-year-old man with chronic kidney disease and asymptomatic, non-life-threatening hyperkalemia is assessed in an outpatient clinic. Which approach addresses reversible contributors as described in Hazzard?
o: Shift potassium into cells while deferring review of contributing medications
Review contributing medications, hydration status, and reversible kidney dysfunction
Give intravenous calcium to remove the excess potassium from the body
Give sodium bicarbonate while deferring assessment of acid-base status
explanation:
Stable, non-life-threatening hyperkalemia in chronic kidney disease often has a reversible contributor. **Review medications, hydration and any recent fall in renal function** to identify why potassium clearance has declined.

**A. Shift potassium first.** Redistribution can lower serum potassium temporarily while the precipitating medication continues to act.
**B. Review reversible factors.** Stopping a contributing drug or correcting volume depletion addresses the mechanism of potassium retention.
**C. IV calcium for removal.** Calcium protects the myocardium without lowering serum or total-body potassium.
**D. Bicarbonate without acid-base assessment.** Accompanying metabolic acidosis is a reason to consider bicarbonate, so acid-base status matters.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1271.
ref: Hazzard Ch 82 — AGING OF THE KIDNEY

q: A woman with dementia takes a sedating medication that was not prescribed for her and develops acute confusion. Evaluation identifies the drug as a harmful contributor. She poses no immediate danger to herself or staff. Which approach follows the delirium management flowchart?
o: Add a regular sedative while maintaining the harmful exposure
Increase the harmful medication while monitoring cognitive status
Remove the harmful exposure while monitoring cognitive status
Observe the cognitive changes while maintaining the harmful exposure
explanation:
Drug exposure can cause delirium even at a customary dose in an older adult. Ask about borrowed and nonprescription drugs as well as prescribed treatment.
**Remove the identified harmful sedative and observe cognition while investigating other contributors.**

**A. Add a regular sedative while maintaining the harmful exposure.** Adding a sedative leaves the harmful exposure in place and can magnify its effects.
**B. Increase the harmful medication while monitoring cognitive status.** A larger dose may deepen sedation or confusion.
**C. Remove the harmful exposure while monitoring cognitive status.** Removing this dispensable drug directly addresses a treatable contributor.
**D. Observe the cognitive changes while maintaining the harmful exposure.** Observation alone unnecessarily prolongs a known harmful exposure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 885, 887, Figure 58-2

q: מטופל בן 84, המסוגל לקבל החלטות, מבקש מידע על הפרוגנוזה לפני החלטה על טיפול. בנו מבקש להסתיר מידע שלילי כדי לשמור על תקווה. לפי סעיף 13(ד) לחוק זכויות החולה, איזו קביעה מאפשרת למטפל להימנע ממסירת מידע רפואי מסוים במסגרת החריג?
o: הבן קבע שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל
הרופא קבע שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל
ועדת האתיקה אישרה שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל
הצוות הסיעודי קבע שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל
explanation:
החוק מחייב למסור למטופל **מידע הדרוש להסכמה מדעת**, לרבות האבחנה והפרוגנוזה, באופן שמאפשר הבנה ובחירה. החריג בסעיף 13(ד) דורש **אישור ועדת אתיקה** לכך שמסירת מידע מסוים עלולה לגרום נזק חמור לבריאותו הגופנית או הנפשית. בקשת הבן לשמור על תקווה אינה כשלעצמה אישור כזה (עמ׳ 8).
"אם אישרה ועדת אתיקה כי מסירתו עלולה לגרום נזק חמור לבריאותו הגופנית או הנפשית של המטופל." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. הבן קבע שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל.** שגויה, העדפת בן המשפחה אינה אישור ועדת אתיקה. כשמטופל מבקש מידע לצורך החלטה, בקשת הבן אינה מקיימת את תנאי החריג (עמ׳ 8).
**ב. הרופא קבע שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל.** שגויה, לפי החריג שנשאל, הערכת הרופא בדבר נזק חמור זקוקה לאישור ועדת אתיקה. קביעתו לבדה אינה האישור שהסעיף דורש (עמ׳ 8).
**ג. ועדת האתיקה אישרה שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל.** נכונה, זהו הגורם והסיכון שהסעיף מגדיר: אישור ועדת אתיקה לכך שהמסירה עלולה להזיק באופן חמור לבריאותו הגופנית או הנפשית של המטופל (עמ׳ 8).
**ד. הצוות הסיעודי קבע שהמידע עלול לגרום נזק חמור לבריאות המטופל.** שגויה, הערכת הצוות הסיעודי אינה מחליפה את אישור ועדת האתיקה. הסעיף נותן למטפל אפשרות להימנע ממסירה רק בתנאי החריג המוגדר (עמ׳ 8).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו־1996, סעיף 13(ב), 13(ג), 13(ד), עמ׳ PDF 8.
ref: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · §13, PDF p. 8

q: An 86-year-old man with severe COPD, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease has recurrent falls, difficulty preparing meals, and missed medications. Which assessment addresses the combined physical, functional, psychological, and social dimensions of his care?
o: A diabetes-focused review of glycemic measurements and glucose-lowering doses
A pulmonary-focused review of spirometry measurements and inhaler technique
A comprehensive geriatric assessment by a team of health professionals
A kidney-focused review of filtration estimates and renal drug dosing
explanation:
**Comprehensive geriatric assessment** evaluates frail older people across several dimensions to uncover treatable problems. It includes physical health, functional status, psychological health, and socioenvironmental factors, rather than organizing the assessment around a single disease (p. 128).
"CGA is a systematic evaluation of frail older persons by a team of health professionals that may uncover treatable health problems and lead to better health outcomes." (p. 128).
"This evaluation typically includes four dimensions: physical health; functional status; psychological health, including cognitive and affective status; and socioenvironmental factors." (p. 128).

**A. A diabetes-focused review of glycemic measurements and glucose-lowering doses.** Wrong, this addresses diabetes management but omits the other dimensions explicitly included in CGA, including function and the social environment (p. 128).
**B. A pulmonary-focused review of spirometry measurements and inhaler technique.** Wrong, a pulmonary review addresses one disease domain, whereas this question requires assessment of function, psychological health, and the social environment as well (p. 128).
**C. A comprehensive geriatric assessment by a team of health professionals.** Correct, the multidisciplinary assessment covers the dimensions relevant to the several difficulties stated in the question (p. 128).
**D. A kidney-focused review of filtration estimates and renal drug dosing.** Wrong, a renal review addresses kidney disease and drug dosing but does not constitute the multidimensional evaluation described (p. 128).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 128.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A 79-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), mild cognitive impairment, and knee osteoarthritis is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone and is independent in four of six activities of daily living. Her discharge medications include furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily for knee pain. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m². Which change to analgesic treatment follows Hazzard's approach to limiting NSAID harm?
o: Replace naproxen with acetaminophen because its adverse-event profile favors initial use for osteoarthritis.
Continue naproxen because concomitant ACE inhibition protects renal perfusion during NSAID treatment.
Increase naproxen because impaired renal function favors NSAIDs over alternative osteoarthritis analgesics.
Add acetaminophen while retaining naproxen because combining analgesics avoids NSAID renal toxicity.
explanation:
Oral NSAIDs can impair renal perfusion and promote fluid retention. Those effects matter in a woman recently hospitalized with heart failure whose eGFR is 28.

**Replace naproxen with a trial of acetaminophen for knee pain.** This reduces NSAID exposure while still treating a symptom that affects function.

**A. Replace naproxen.** Acetaminophen offers an initial pharmacologic option with a more favorable adverse-effect profile for this patient.
**B. Continue because of lisinopril.** An ACE inhibitor does not protect the kidney from NSAID effects. The combination deserves particular caution in impaired renal function.
**C. Increase naproxen.** Greater NSAID exposure can aggravate kidney injury and fluid retention.
**D. Add acetaminophen but keep naproxen.** A second analgesic does not remove the renal and cardiac risks of ongoing naproxen.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 312, 1280.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: גבר בן 84 עם דמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר מתונה, סוכרת, ו-hip fracture לאחרונה מועבר מהשיקום לחדר המיון עם confusion ואגיטציה. אשתו מדווחת שהוא חסר מנוחה בלילות במשך 3 ימים. תרופות כוללות donepezil 10 mg, metformin 500 mg BID, ו-oxycodone 5 mg q6h PRN. חום 37.2°C, HR 92, BP 156/88. בבדיקת שתן: 50-100 WBC, nitrites חיוביים. איזו תרופה תרשום ראשונה?
o: לא להתחיל טיפול אנטיביוטי; לחפש סיבה אחרת לבלבול
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tab BID
Nitrofurantoin 100 mg PO BID
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily
explanation:
התשובה היא **לא להתחיל טיפול אנטיביוטי; לחפש סיבה אחרת לבלבול**. בתרחיש אין תסמינים ממקמים לדרכי השתן או חום, ולכן אין לייחס את הבלבול ל־UTI על סמך ממצאי השתן בלבד. יש להעריך דליריום וסיבות חלופיות, תוך הערכה חוזרת אם מופיעים סימני זיהום נוספים או אי־יציבות (עמ׳ 1703).
"unless more specific localizing signs and symptoms for UTI are present, clinicians should NOT initiate UTI treatment for these symptoms." (עמ׳ 1703).

**א. לא להתחיל טיפול אנטיביוטי; לחפש סיבה אחרת לבלבול.** נכונה, הספר מורה שלא להתחיל טיפול ל־UTI בשל תסמינים לא ספציפיים ללא סימנים ממקמים, ומדגיש בירור סיבות לא זיהומיות לבלבול (עמ׳ 1703).
**ב. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tab BID.** שגויה, היעדר תסמינים ממקמים אינו מספק בסיס להתחלת TMP-SMX. השאלה היא אם קיימת התוויה לאנטיביוטיקה, ולא איזו אנטיביוטיקה לבחור (עמ׳ 1703).
**ג. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg PO BID.** שגויה, גם ניטרופורנטואין אינו מוצדק על סמך בלבול וממצאי שתן בלבד. הספר ממליץ להימנע מטיפול אנטימיקרוביאלי בבקטריוריה ללא תסמיני דרכי שתן ספציפיים (עמ׳ 1703, טבלה 106-2).
**ד. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily.** שגויה, מתן צפטריאקסון אינו מחליף ביסוס של זיהום סימפטומטי. יש לברר סיבות חלופיות לדליריום לפני ייחוסו ל־UTI, במיוחד בהיעדר סימנים נוספים (עמ׳ 1703).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 1703, לרבות טבלה 106-2.

q: An older woman with recurrent falls asks for a sleeping medication. Which statement about centrally acting medications is appropriate in this context?
o: They reduce fall risk by improving continuity of sleep
They increase fall risk and warrant considering alternatives
They are preferred to nonpharmacologic insomnia management
They are recommended for fall prevention when treatment begins
explanation:
Centrally acting hypnotics can impair alertness, balance and coordination. In a woman with recurrent falls, **review the risk and consider nonpharmacologic insomnia treatment** before prescribing one.

**A. Reduce falls through better sleep.** Improving sleep continuity does not offset or eliminate drug-related unsteadiness.
**B. Increase fall risk.** Assess the cause of insomnia and consider behavioral treatment that avoids additional sedation.
**C. Preferred over behavioral care.** Nonpharmacologic approaches avoid sedative adverse effects and merit priority here.
**D. Start for prevention.** A sedative is not a fall-prevention treatment and may add a new risk factor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 639.

q: Apixaban has been selected for an 81-year-old man with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. He weighs 72 kg and has a serum creatinine of 1.9 mg/dL, with no additional dose-modifying factor. According to the Hazzard dosing table, which adjustment is appropriate?
o: Continue 5 mg twice daily because weight above 60 kg prevents dose reduction
Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily because age and creatinine meet the criteria
Continue 5 mg twice daily because dose reduction requires all three criteria
Reduce to 2.5 mg once daily because age and creatinine require a longer interval
explanation:
**Apixaban dose reduction** in the cited table requires at least two criteria, not all three. The reduced regimen is "2.5 mg twice daily (for at least two criteria)"; age of at least 80 and serum creatinine of at least 1.5 mg/dL satisfy two criteria in this case (p. 1205). His weight does not cancel the two fulfilled conditions.

**A. Continue 5 mg twice daily because weight above 60 kg prevents dose reduction.** Wrong, a weight above the low-weight criterion does not negate the two qualifying age and creatinine criteria (p. 1205; application).
**B. Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily because age and creatinine meet the criteria.** Correct, he meets two criteria, and the table specifies the reduced twice-daily regimen for that situation (p. 1205).
**C. Continue 5 mg twice daily because dose reduction requires all three criteria.** Wrong, requiring all three conditions is inconsistent with the table’s requirement for at least two (p. 1205).
**D. Reduce to 2.5 mg once daily because age and creatinine require a longer interval.** Wrong, the table reduces the dose while retaining twice-daily administration; it does not specify once-daily dosing (p. 1205).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1205.

q: A patient receiving morphine develops acute kidney injury and somnolence. Which combination explains the relationship between morphine-6-glucuronide elimination and toxicity risk?
o: Reduced metabolite elimination and increased toxicity risk.
Reduced metabolite elimination and decreased toxicity risk.
Increased metabolite elimination and increased toxicity risk.
Increased metabolite elimination and decreased toxicity risk.
explanation:
The liver converts morphine to morphine-6-glucuronide, an active opioid metabolite cleared by the kidneys. Acute kidney injury slows its elimination, so the same morphine dose can produce prolonged sedation and respiratory depression.

**A. Reduced elimination and increased toxicity.** Accumulated metabolite continues to stimulate opioid receptors between doses. New somnolence is a reason to assess ventilation promptly.
**B. Reduced elimination and decreased toxicity.** Retaining an active metabolite prolongs opioid exposure and can deepen sedation.
**C. Increased elimination and increased toxicity.** The somnolence fits toxicity. Kidney injury impairs excretion of the metabolite, allowing its concentration to rise.
**D. Increased elimination and decreased toxicity.** Efficient clearance would limit accumulation. This patient's declining renal function predicts the opposite pattern.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 386, 1060.

q: An 82-year-old man with Parkinson disease, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and mild cognitive impairment has three days of agitation and visual hallucinations. Oxybutynin for urinary urgency was added yesterday to carbidopa/levodopa, tamsulosin, and donepezil. Vital signs are normal and the CAM is positive. Which statement should guide review of the new oxybutynin prescription under the Beers Criteria?
o: Review stopping oxybutynin because its anticholinergic effects can worsen delirium
Continue oxybutynin because bladder antimuscarinics lack adverse cognitive effects
Increase oxybutynin because its anticholinergic effects can improve delirium
Continue oxybutynin because cognitive impairment reduces its central adverse effects
explanation:
Oxybutynin is a bladder antimuscarinic with strong anticholinergic activity. Its adverse cognitive effects are particularly relevant in an older person with delirium.
**Review stopping oxybutynin. Agitation predates its first dose, but the new drug could worsen the episode.**

**A. Review stopping oxybutynin because its anticholinergic effects can worsen delirium.** Removing it can reduce further anticholinergic exposure without attributing the original onset to it.
**B. Continue oxybutynin because bladder antimuscarinics lack adverse cognitive effects.** Bladder antimuscarinics can have central cognitive effects, especially oxybutynin.
**C. Increase oxybutynin because its anticholinergic effects can improve delirium.** Increasing muscarinic blockade is more likely to aggravate confusion than to restore attention.
**D. Continue oxybutynin because cognitive impairment reduces its central adverse effects.** Preexisting cognitive impairment increases vulnerability to central adverse effects.

Reference · AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Tables 3 and 7, pp. 2066, 2074

q: במטופלת עם קיהיון שהוגדרה כנוטה למות ויש לה קושי באכילה נערכת הערכה לקראת החלטה על דרך ההזנה. לפי המלצות הוועדה הלאומית, על מה צריכה להתבסס ההחלטה על צורת מתן המזון והנוזלים?
o: על השלב הקוגניטיבי כתחליף להערכת מצב רפואי ותזונתי
על מצבה וצרכיה ובהתייעצות עם צוות רב מקצועי
על העדפת המשפחה כתחליף לבדיקת אפשרויות ההזנה
על זמינות הזונדה כתחליף לבחינת דרך הפה
explanation:
**דרך ההזנה** צריכה להיבחר בהחלטה רפואית אישית לפי מצב המטופלת, צרכיה ויכולותיה. ההמלצות דורשות שיתוף צוות רב מקצועי ומעדיפות דרך הפה תוך הערכה מקצועית והתאמה, כך שההחלטה אינה נגזרת מנתון יחיד (עמ׳ 5).
"ההחלטה בדבר צורת מתן המזון והנוזלים צריכה להיות רפואית אינדיבידואלית בהתאם למצבו של החולה עם קיהיון, למקום שהייתו, לצרכיו, וליכולותיו" (עמ׳ 5).
"ההחלטה הרפואית צריכה להתקבל בשיתוף פעולה מלא של צוות רב מקצועי" (עמ׳ 5).

**א. על השלב הקוגניטיבי כתחליף להערכת מצב רפואי ותזונתי.** שגויה, המסמך דורש החלטה אישית המביאה בחשבון מצב רפואי, צרכים ויכולות; שלב קוגניטיבי אינו מחליף את ההערכה הזו (עמ׳ 5).
**ב. על מצבה וצרכיה ובהתייעצות עם צוות רב מקצועי.** נכונה, ההחלטה האישית ושיתוף הצוות הרב מקצועי מופיעים במפורש בהמלצות (עמ׳ 5).
**ג. על העדפת המשפחה כתחליף לבדיקת אפשרויות ההזנה.** שגויה, המסמך דורש הערכה מקצועית של צרכים, דרכי מתן ויכולת האכלה; העדפת המשפחה אינה תחליף לה (עמ׳ 5).
**ד. על זמינות הזונדה כתחליף לבחינת דרך הפה.** שגויה, המסמך מעדיף דרך הפה ומחייב לבחון אותה ולהתאים את ההזנה; זמינות אמצעי אינה ממלאת דרישה זו (עמ׳ 5).

מקור: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות, עמ׳ 5.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: Duloxetine is being considered for a 76-year-old man with neuropathic pain and a calculated creatinine clearance of 24 mL/min. Which approach follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Start the usual dose and monitor kidney function during treatment
Start a low dose and increase it gradually during treatment
Avoid duloxetine in the range of kidney function described
Give duloxetine intermittently while retaining the usual dose per administration
explanation:
For **duloxetine**, Beers recommends avoidance when creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min. The table gives the rationale "Increased GI adverse effects (nausea, diarrhea)" and the recommendation "Avoid" (Table 6, p. 2073).

**A. Start the usual dose and monitor kidney function during treatment.** Wrong, at this creatinine clearance, the recommendation is avoidance; renal monitoring does not substitute for that recommendation (p. 2073).
**B. Start a low dose and increase it gradually during treatment.** Wrong, the table specifies avoidance rather than initiation at a reduced dose with subsequent escalation (p. 2073).
**C. Avoid duloxetine in the range of kidney function described.** Correct, the patient’s creatinine clearance is below the stated threshold, where increased gastrointestinal adverse effects support avoidance (p. 2073).
**D. Give duloxetine intermittently while retaining the usual dose per administration.** Wrong, intermittent administration is not the listed renal adjustment; the recommendation at this clearance is avoidance (p. 2073).

Source: AGS Beers 2023, pp. 2073.

q: An older woman taking a thiazide develops hyponatremia and is hypovolemic on examination. Which fluid-management approach matches the principle described in Hazzard?
o: Give isotonic saline and monitor serum sodium
Restrict water intake and monitor body weight
Give a loop diuretic and restrict water intake
Increase free-water intake and monitor body weight
explanation:
Thiazides can cause sodium loss, and hypovolemia encourages retention of water. **Give isotonic saline to restore volume and follow sodium during correction**, while addressing the diuretic.

**A. Isotonic saline with monitoring.** This replaces extracellular volume and allows the rate of sodium correction to be observed.
**B. Restrict water only.** It does not replace the volume that has been lost.
**C. Loop diuresis with restriction.** Further salt and water loss could worsen a depleted circulation.
**D. Increase free water.** Extra water can lower serum sodium further without adequately correcting sodium depletion.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 83-year-old man with heart failure has an inadequate response to furosemide and is about to start metolazone. Which monitoring approach is appropriate during this change?
o: Check electrolytes closely while adjusting the diuretic regimen
Defer electrolyte checks until prolonged clinical stability is achieved
Follow edema clinically in place of electrolyte checks after addition
Reduce electrolyte checks when the urine output starts to increase
explanation:
**Metolazone** can produce a brisk diuretic response and life-threatening hyponatremia and hypokalemia even after short-term use. This risk explains the recommendation for **close electrolyte monitoring** while diuretic therapy is adjusted (p. 1182). "For this reason, electrolytes should be monitored closely when diuretic therapy is being adjusted." (p. 1182).

**A. Check electrolytes closely while adjusting the diuretic regimen.** Correct, monitoring during adjustment addresses the electrolyte complications described with metolazone (p. 1182).
**B. Defer electrolyte checks until prolonged clinical stability is achieved.** Wrong, serious electrolyte abnormalities can develop after relatively short-term use, so prolonged stability is not the point at which monitoring should begin (p. 1182).
**C. Follow edema clinically in place of electrolyte checks after addition.** Wrong, observation of edema leaves the specified electrolyte monitoring undone during a period when severe abnormalities can occur (p. 1182).
**D. Reduce electrolyte checks when the urine output starts to increase.** Wrong, a brisk diuretic response is described alongside the risk of dangerous sodium and potassium disturbances; it is not a reason to reduce monitoring (p. 1182).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1182.

q: How do the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria distinguish the safety of low-dose doxepin for sleep from the warning applied to higher doses?
o: Low-dose doxepin falls under the same anticholinergic warning as higher doses
Low-dose doxepin has greater cognitive risk than higher doses
Low-dose doxepin has a safety profile comparable to placebo
Low-dose doxepin causes orthostatic hypotension more often than higher doses
explanation:
**Low-dose doxepin** is explicitly distinguished from the higher-dose anticholinergic warning. Beers applies that warning above 6 mg/day and describes the safety profile at 6 mg/day or less as comparable to placebo (p. 2059). The deciding statement is "the safety profile of low-dose doxepin (≤6 mg/day) is comparable to that of placebo." (p. 2059).

**A. Low-dose doxepin falls under the same anticholinergic warning as higher doses.** Wrong, the warning lists doxepin above 6 mg/day and explicitly distinguishes the lower-dose safety profile (p. 2059).
**B. Low-dose doxepin has greater cognitive risk than higher doses.** Wrong, the low-dose statement is a placebo-comparable safety profile, not a greater cognitive risk than the higher-dose category (p. 2059).
**C. Low-dose doxepin has a safety profile comparable to placebo.** Correct, this matches the explicit description of doxepin at 6 mg/day or less (p. 2059).
**D. Low-dose doxepin causes orthostatic hypotension more often than higher doses.** Wrong, orthostatic hypotension is part of the higher-dose warning; the low-dose statement describes placebo-comparable safety, not greater hypotension than higher doses (p. 2059).

Source: AGS Beers 2023, pp. 2059.

q: An 81-year-old man with heart failure, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and mild dementia is hospitalized for the fourth time this year. His wife is exhausted by managing 12 medications, multiple specialist visits, and daily glucose checks. She asks whether care can be simplified. What should guide review of this treatment burden?
o: Arrange home assistance while retaining the existing treatment priorities.
Ask each specialist to simplify care around individual disease priorities.
Discuss patient priorities to guide a shared care plan.
Teach medication organization while retaining the existing treatment priorities.
explanation:
Multimorbidity can make disease-by-disease regimens overwhelming for patients and caregivers. **Agree on the patient's priorities with him and his wife**, then align medications, monitoring and visits across clinicians.

**A. Add home help alone.** Help can ease task delivery without resolving whether each task still serves his goals.
**B. Ask specialists separately.** Individual disease targets may compete and increase total workload.
**C. Shared priorities and plan.** Determine which outcomes matter most and which tasks can be simplified without sacrificing them.
**D. Teach organization alone.** An organized regimen can remain unnecessarily burdensome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 613.
ref: Hazzard Ch 41 — MANAGING THE CARE OF PATIENTS WITH MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS
chapterTitle: Managing the Care of Patients with Multiple Chronic Conditions

q: An older woman with recurrent falls takes alprazolam. Which consideration in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria challenges the assumption that changing to diazepam would resolve the fall risk associated with benzodiazepines?
o: Increased metabolism of long-acting agents in older adults
Decreased metabolism of long-acting agents in older adults
Decreased sensitivity to benzodiazepines in older adults
Protection against falls and fractures from benzodiazepines
explanation:
Older adults are more sensitive to benzodiazepines and may clear long-acting agents more slowly. **Reduced metabolism of long-acting diazepam** can prolong sedation, so switching from alprazolam cannot be assumed to resolve fall risk.

**A. Increased metabolism.** The direction is reversed for long-acting agents in later life.
**B. Decreased metabolism.** Longer exposure can leave residual psychomotor impairment after the intended effect.
**C. Decreased sensitivity.** Older adults generally have greater sensitivity at a given exposure.
**D. Protection from falls and fractures.** Benzodiazepines increase the risks of both, regardless of the reason for use.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 2, p. 2060.

q: An older adult with iron-deficiency anemia is clinically stable, tolerates oral iron, and has no known problem with absorption. Which statement about iron replacement agrees with Hazzard?
o: Prefer daily oral iron, since dosing lowers hepcidin and improves absorption on the following day.
Prefer repeated daily iron, since recent dosing increases absorption of iron from the next dose.
Prefer alternate-day oral iron, since dosing increases hepcidin and reduces absorption on the following day.
Prefer intravenous iron initially, since oral replacement is inadequate in most patients with iron-deficiency anemia.
explanation:
For a stable patient who tolerates and absorbs oral iron, **alternate-day oral dosing** allows the transient hepcidin rise after a dose to wear off. This can improve fractional absorption of the next dose.

**A. Daily because hepcidin falls.** Oral iron initially raises hepcidin and restricts iron transfer into blood.
**B. Repeated daily doses improve uptake.** Recent dosing blunts next-day absorption.
**C. Alternate-day oral treatment.** The interval accommodates hepcidin-mediated inhibition and is suitable in the absence of urgent or absorption concerns.
**D. Routine IV first.** IV replacement is useful for intolerance or failure, but oral treatment is sufficient in many patients.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.
ref: Hazzard Ch 94 — AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA
chapterTitle: AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA

q: בהכנת תעודת רופא לצורך בקשה למינוי אפוטרופוס למטופל עם דמנציה ושינוי קוגניטיבי חריף, איזה תוכן נדרש בחוזר מעבר לתיאור מחלות הרקע?
o: העדפת המשפחה למוסד ומידת זמינותו לקליטה
הערכת קוגניציה ותובנה ומשך מינוי
עלות השהייה במוסד ומקור המימון האפשרי
ציון גיל המטופל ומספר האבחנות שברשימתו
explanation:
**הערכה לצורך אפוטרופסות** דורשת תיאור של יכולת המטופל ומצבו, ולא הסקה ממחלה או מסירוב בלבד. החוזר דורש התייחסות למצב הקוגניטיבי וההתנהגותי, לתובנה, לדחיפות ולהמלצה על תקופת המינוי; לכן שינוי חריף מחייב תיעוד ולא קביעה אוטומטית של צורך קבוע (עמ׳ 4, 5; המשפט האחרון הוא הסקה).
"התייחסות למצב הקוגניטיבי וההתנהגותי (ריכוז, התמצאות בזמן, ובמקום)." (עמ׳ 5).
"מידת התובנה של הנבדק ביחס למצבו." (עמ׳ 5).

**א. העדפת המשפחה למוסד ומידת זמינותו לקליטה.** שגויה, העדפת מיקום וזמינות מוסד אינן מחליפות את תיאור המצב הקוגניטיבי והתובנה בתעודה הרפואית (עמ׳ 5).
**ב. הערכת קוגניציה ותובנה ומשך מינוי.** נכונה, אלו רכיבים שהחוזר דורש לכלול בהערכת המטופל ובנימוק להליך ולמשכו (עמ׳ 5).
**ג. עלות השהייה במוסד ומקור המימון האפשרי.** שגויה, מידע כלכלי אינו מחליף את הערכת היכולת והמצב הרפואי הנדרשת בתעודה (עמ׳ 5).
**ד. ציון גיל המטופל ומספר האבחנות שברשימתו.** שגויה, גיל ורשימת אבחנות אינם מספקים את התיאור התפקודי והקוגניטיבי שהחוזר דורש (עמ׳ 4, 5).

מקור: חוזר מינוי אפוטרופוס באשפוז ממושך, סעיף 9.3.2, עמ׳ 5.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר מנהל רפואה 10/2006: מינוי אפוטרופוס על גופו של אדם ו/או רכושו במסגרת אשפוז ממושך

q: אישה בישראל, המבינה את משמעות החלטתה, מבקשת לבטל ייפוי כוח מתמשך שבו מינתה את בנה. היא לא הגבילה במסמך את אפשרותה לבטלו. לפי מדריך משרד המשפטים, איזה צעד נדרש במסלול הביטול הרגיל?
o: מסירת הודעה בכתב לבן ולאפוטרופוס הכללי
מסירת הודעה בעל פה לבן ולאפוטרופוס הכללי
קבלת הסכמה מהבן ואישור מהרופא המטפל
קבלת החלטת בית משפט ואישור מהרופא המטפל
explanation:
**ביטול ייפוי כוח מתמשך** אפשרי לבקשת הממנה בתנאים המתוארים במדריך. במסלול הרגיל הביטול נעשה בהודעה בכתב למיופה הכוח ובדיווח בכתב לאפוטרופוס הכללי; מסלול המחייב החלטת בית משפט נוגע בין השאר למי שהגביל במסמך את אפשרות הביטול שלו (עמ׳ 20).
"הביטול מתבצע בהודעה בכתב שלך למיופה הכוח" (עמ׳ 20).
"אתה נדרש למסור לאפוטרופוס הכללי הודעה בכתב על ביטול ייפוי הכוח" (עמ׳ 20).
"ביטול ייפוי הכוח אפשרי גם במקרה שבחרת להגביל את האפשרות שלך לבטל את ייפוי הכוח, אך הוא דורש במקרה זה החלטת בית משפט." (עמ׳ 20).

**א. מסירת הודעה בכתב לבן ולאפוטרופוס הכללי.** נכונה, אלה שתי ההודעות בכתב הנדרשות במדריך, ובשאלה אין הגבלה עצמית שמחייבת פנייה לבית משפט (עמ׳ 20).
**ב. מסירת הודעה בעל פה לבן ולאפוטרופוס הכללי.** שגויה, הודעה בעל פה אינה ממלאת את דרישת ההודעה בכתב למיופה הכוח והדיווח בכתב לאפוטרופוס הכללי (עמ׳ 20).
**ג. קבלת הסכמה מהבן ואישור מהרופא המטפל.** שגויה, המדריך מתאר ביטול בהודעת הממנה; הוא אינו מתנה את המסלול הרגיל בהסכמת מיופה הכוח או באישור רופא (עמ׳ 20).
**ד. קבלת החלטת בית משפט ואישור מהרופא המטפל.** שגויה, המדריך מאפשר את מסלול ההודעות כאשר לא נקבעה הגבלה עצמית; מסלול בית המשפט אינו דרישת הביטול הרגיל בנסיבות אלו (עמ׳ 20).

מקור: משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך, עמ׳ 20.
ref: משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך

q: דיירת בישראל עם דמנציה שמונה לה אפוטרופוס זקוקה להחלטה רפואית. היא אינה מסוגלת להבין את משמעות ההחלטה, אין הנחיות מקדימות, וגם לאחר בירור לא ניתן לעמוד על רצונה הקודם. לפי סעיף 67ו(ב)(3), מה ינחה את ההחלטה?
o: העדפת הבת לגבי סוג הטיפול שנראה לה ראוי
טובת המטופלת מתוך התחשבות ברצונה הנוכחי
ההעדפה המשוערת של אדם מבוגר בעל אבחנה דומה
העדפת האפוטרופוס לגבי טיפול שהיה בוחר לעצמו
explanation:
כאשר לא ניתן לברר רצון קודם והאדם אינו מסוגל להבין את ההחלטה, החוק מפנה ל**טובתו** תוך התחשבות **ברצונו הנוכחי**. זהו מצב מוגדר, ולא מסקנה הנובעת מעצם היעדרו של מסמך הנחיות מקדימות (סעיף 67ו(ב)(3), עמ׳ 67).
"בהתאם לטובתו, מתוך התחשבות ברצונו הנוכחי" (עמ׳ 67).

**א. העדפת הבת לגבי סוג הטיפול שנראה לה ראוי.** שגויה, העדפת הבת עשויה להיות חלק מהשיח, אך אינה אמת המידה שהסעיף קובע (עמ׳ 67).
**ב. טובת המטופלת מתוך התחשבות ברצונה הנוכחי.** נכונה, התיאור ממלא את התנאים להפעלת אמת המידה הזו בחוק (עמ׳ 67).
**ג. ההעדפה המשוערת של אדם מבוגר בעל אבחנה דומה.** שגויה, הסעיף עוסק בטובתה של המטופלת המסוימת ובהבעת רצונה כעת, ולא ברוב מדומיין (עמ׳ 67).
**ד. העדפת האפוטרופוס לגבי טיפול שהיה בוחר לעצמו.** שגויה, החלטת האפוטרופוס צריכה להתייחס למטופלת, לא לבחירה שהיה עושה עבור עצמו (עמ׳ 67).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיפים 67ו ו־68, עמ׳ 67.
