q: A 78-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment is brought by her family for weight loss. She has lost 8 kg in six months and has a Mini Nutritional Assessment score of 19, indicating nutritional risk. She lives alone and says she forgets to eat. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, and zolpidem 10 mg at night. Laboratory results show albumin 3.4 g/dL and vitamin B12 280 pg/mL. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for addressing contributors to poor nutritional intake?
o: Use megestrol for weight gain because it improves function and survival in older adults
Give oral supplements with meals to minimize compensatory reductions in food intake
Review sedative treatment and arrange practical assistance with meals and eating
Use cyproheptadine for weight gain because its benefits are established in older adults
explanation:
**Contributors to poor intake** should be identified and addressed, including medication effects and assistance needs. Hazzard supports help with eating and medication review; sedative-hypnotics can cause cognitive slowing. This supports reviewing zolpidem and arranging meal assistance, without establishing that this combination has the greatest nutritional benefit for this patient (pp. 427, 659; inference).
"underlying causative or contributing condition(s) to PEM should be sought, identified, and addressed." (p. 427).
"providing company at meals and feeding assistance as needed, and minimizing dietary restrictions." (p. 427).

**A. Use megestrol for weight gain because it improves function and survival in older adults.** Wrong, appetite stimulants have not established these benefits in older adults; observed weight gain has not been associated with improved function or reduced mortality (p. 428).
**B. Give oral supplements with meals to minimize compensatory reductions in food intake.** Wrong, supplements are recommended between meals to reduce compensatory decreases in mealtime intake, not with meals for that purpose (p. 428).
**C. Review sedative treatment and arrange practical assistance with meals and eating.** Correct, it addresses an assistance need in the stem and a medication class with cognitive adverse effects; benefit magnitude is not predicted (pp. 427, 659; inference).
**D. Use cyproheptadine for weight gain because its benefits are established in older adults.** Wrong, cyproheptadine is among the agents not shown effective in older adults and capable of serious adverse effects (p. 428).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 427, 428, 659.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: An 81-year-old man with COPD on home oxygen has lost about 7 kg in three months. His BMI is 20.1 kg/m². He reports early satiety and breathlessness while eating. He takes tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, and furosemide 40 mg daily. Albumin is 3.1 g/dL, BNP is 890 pg/mL, and echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 35%. Oral nutritional supplementation is planned. Which rationale for choosing a formula is supported by Hazzard?
o: A pulmonary formula is preferred because clinical trials establish its superior benefit
A standard formula provides more calories in a smaller volume than concentrated supplements
A concentrated supplement delivers more calories per milliliter and requires less volume
A fiber-enriched formula is preferred because routine fiber supplementation prevents diarrhea
explanation:
The energy density of a supplement determines the volume needed to deliver a given number of calories. With early satiety, dyspnea and heart failure, **a concentrated supplement can deliver more energy in less fluid**.

**A. Pulmonary-specific formula.** Clinical trials have not demonstrated the claimed superiority of disease-specific pulmonary formulas.
**B. Standard formula in less volume.** Standard formulas are less energy-dense. Equal calories generally require more volume.
**C. Concentrated supplement.** A smaller serving can provide the same energy and may be easier for him to finish.
**D. Routine fiber against diarrhea.** Fiber enrichment is not a proven general way to prevent diarrhea during enteral feeding.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 428, 430.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: חולה עם דמנציה הוגדרה כדין כחולה הנוטה למות. לאחר הערכת בליעה ותזונה נמצא שאפשר לספק לה דרך הפה את כמות המזון והנוזלים הנדרשת, באופן מותאם ובטוח. איזו דרך הזנה מועדפת לפי המלצות הוועדה הארצית של משרד הבריאות בנושא הזנה בחולה עם דמנציה הנוטה למות?
o: הזנה דרך גסטרוסטום עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים
הזנה דרך הפה עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים
הזנה דרך זונדה עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים
הזנה דרך הווריד עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים
explanation:
**האכלה דרך הפה** היא הדרך המועדפת כאשר היא מספקת את הצרכים לאחר הערכה והתאמה לחולה. המלצות הוועדה קובעות: "הדרך המועדפת למתן המזון והנוזלים היא דרך הפה." (עמוד 5, החלטה ו). באותה החלטה נדרשים הערכת כמות המזון והנוזלים והתייעצות בנושא הבליעה כדי להתאים את ההאכלה; השאלה קובעת שבירור זה נעשה ונמצא שאפשר לתת את הנדרש דרך הפה.

**א. הזנה דרך גסטרוסטום עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים.** שגויה, התאמת המזון אינה משנה את העדפת הדרך הפומית כאשר ניתן לספק בה את הצרכים. ההמלצה על דרך חלופית מופיעה כאשר אי אפשר להאכיל ולהשקות דרך הפה במידה הראויה, בניגוד לנתון בשאלה (עמוד 5, החלטה ו; עמוד 6, החלטה ח).
**ב. הזנה דרך הפה עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים.** נכונה, זו הדרך המועדפת בהמלצות, והנתונים בשאלה קובעים שנבדקה ונמצאה מתאימה לסיפוק צרכיה של החולה (עמוד 5, החלטה ו).
**ג. הזנה דרך זונדה עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים.** שגויה, זונדה נכללת בדרכי ההזנה החלופיות כאשר ההאכלה דרך הפה אינה מספקת; בשאלה נקבע שהדרך הפומית מספקת ומתאימה ולכן היא המועדפת (עמוד 5, החלטה ו; עמוד 6, החלטה ח).
**ד. הזנה דרך הווריד עם התאמת הרכב המזון לצרכיה האישיים.** שגויה, עירוי נזכר בין הדרכים החלופיות במצב שבו אי אפשר לספק מזון ונוזלים דרך הפה במידה הראויה. זה אינו המצב המתואר בשאלה, ולכן אין להעדיפו על פני ההאכלה הפומית (עמוד 5, החלטה ו; עמוד 6, החלטה ח).

מקור: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות בנושא הזנה בחולה עם קיהיון הנוטה למות, עמודים 5 ו־6, החלטות ו ו־ח.

sourceChecked.source: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית בנושא הזנה בחולה עם קיהיון הנוטה למות

q: A severely malnourished older man starts tube feeding after hip-fracture surgery. Which set of electrolytes should be specifically monitored for refeeding syndrome during the initial feeding period?
o: Phosphate, magnesium, and calcium
Phosphate, magnesium, and potassium
Phosphate, sodium, and potassium
Calcium, magnesium, and potassium
explanation:
For **refeeding syndrome** during enteral nutrition, Hazzard specifies monitoring phosphate, magnesium, and potassium. Inference: the monitoring plan for this patient should include the complete set rather than substitute a different electrolyte for one of its components. The table states: "Monitor phosphate, magnesium, potassium" (Table 30-12, p. 431).

**A. Phosphate, magnesium, and calcium.** Wrong, this leaves potassium out of the monitoring set specified for refeeding syndrome; calcium does not replace it in that recommendation (p. 431).
**B. Phosphate, magnesium, and potassium.** Correct, this contains all three electrolytes in the refeeding-syndrome monitoring recommendation (p. 431).
**C. Phosphate, sodium, and potassium.** Wrong, this omits magnesium, which remains part of the specified monitoring set (p. 431).
**D. Calcium, magnesium, and potassium.** Wrong, this omits phosphate, which remains part of the specified monitoring set (p. 431).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 431.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A 76-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. She has lost 6 kg in two months because of dysphagia. A video swallow study shows aspiration of thin liquids but safe swallowing of nectar-thick liquids. Her family requests a feeding tube. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, pramipexole, and quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime; MoCA during admission is 18/30. Which principle supports considering speech-therapy-guided, supervised thickened liquids?
o: Feeding tubes improve pressure-ulcer healing and should guide the choice of feeding route.
Thickened liquids are an effective compensatory option in patients with Parkinson disease.
Nasogastric tubes reduce agitation and should guide the choice of feeding route.
Swallow-study findings take priority over autonomy and quality of life in choosing the route.
explanation:
Thickened liquid can slow a bolus enough to improve airway protection in some patients with Parkinson disease. **A speech-therapy-guided, supervised trial of nectar-thick liquids is reasonable because she swallowed this consistency safely during testing.** Monitor hydration, nutrition and tolerance as delirium resolves.

**A. Feeding tubes improve pressure-ulcer healing.** In nursing-home residents with advanced cognitive impairment, PEG placement was associated with more new ulcers and less healing. Those observations cannot predict this patient's outcome or determine her feeding route.
**B. Thickened liquids can compensate for dysphagia.** Use the consistency that worked for her, with assistance and reassessment. Safe swallows during testing do not guarantee adequate intake or freedom from pneumonia.
**C. Nasogastric feeding reduces agitation.** A nasal tube can be uncomfortable and invite pulling during delirium.
**D. Swallow findings override autonomy.** Discuss the benefits and burdens with her and her family. Capacity is decision-specific, and a cognitive score obtained during delirium is insufficient on its own.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 450–451. Teno et al., feeding tubes and pressure ulcers in advanced cognitive impairment, PMID 22782196.

q: An 82-year-old man with chronic kidney disease receives enteral nutrition after a stroke. His current standard formula meets calorie targets, but assessment identifies a need to restrict electrolyte intake. Which formula category has the role described in Hazzard for this problem?
o: A renal formula with low electrolyte content and high caloric density
A pulmonary formula with high fat content and low carbohydrate content
A hepatic formula enriched in branched-chain rather than aromatic amino acids
A predigested formula containing hydrolyzed protein and less complex carbohydrate
explanation:
**Renal formulas** have a specific role when renal disease creates a need for fluid or electrolyte restriction. Hazzard describes them as "low in electrolytes and dense in calories" (p. 430). This is a selective indication, not a recommendation for routine disease-specific formulas in all patients.

**A. A renal formula with low electrolyte content and high caloric density.** Correct, its low electrolyte content directly matches the restriction identified in the stem (p. 430).
**B. A pulmonary formula with high fat content and low carbohydrate content.** Wrong, the pulmonary formulation changes fat and carbohydrate composition; it does not address the electrolyte-restriction indication specified for renal formulas (p. 430).
**C. A hepatic formula enriched in branched-chain rather than aromatic amino acids.** Wrong, the hepatic formulation addresses protein delivery limited by hepatic encephalopathy, not the renal electrolyte-restriction problem in the stem (p. 430).
**D. A predigested formula containing hydrolyzed protein and less complex carbohydrate.** Wrong, predigested formulations alter nutrient complexity for impaired digestion; they do not supply the renal electrolyte-restriction rationale (p. 430).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 430.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A 77-year-old woman with undernutrition and muscle weakness is receiving nutritional and rehabilitation care. An oral nutritional supplement is prescribed between meals. What is the purpose of this timing?
o: To increase satiety during the regular meals
To limit compensatory reductions in mealtime food intake
To replace the protein consumed in regular meals
To reduce the total daily intake of calories
explanation:
An oral supplement adds nutrition only to the extent that it does not displace food the patient already eats. **Offer it between meals to limit compensatory reductions in meal intake**.

**A. Increase mealtime satiety.** Feeling fuller at mealtime could reduce food intake and cancel part of the supplement's benefit.
**B. Limit meal displacement.** A separate snack adds a chance to consume energy and protein while preserving appetite for meals.
**C. Replace meal protein.** Regular meals still provide nutrients. The supplement is intended to add to them.
**D. Reduce daily calories.** The treatment of undernutrition aims to increase total energy intake.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 428.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A woman with dementia eats less and shows pain when her denture is inserted. Examination finds an ill-fitting denture and a local lesion at its contact point. Which approach addresses the identified local cause?
o: Increase the intensity of analgesia while continuing the injuring denture
Remove the mechanical source of injury to the oral mucosa
Add sedation while continuing to use the same denture
Change the feeding route while leaving the denture unaltered
explanation:
An ill-fitting denture can injure oral mucosa through repeated pressure or friction. Pain on insertion and a lesion exactly where the denture makes contact explain why eating has become uncomfortable and point to correcting the fit.

**A. Increase analgesia.** Analgesia may ease insertion pain. Continued friction can keep the mucosal lesion from healing.
**B. Relieve mechanical pressure.** Remove the denture to relieve pressure on the lesion and have its fit assessed before she wears it again.
**C. Add sedation.** Sedation can blunt her ability to communicate pain and reduce alertness during meals while the pressure point persists.
**D. Change the feeding route.** Providing calories by another route would leave the painful contact uncorrected whenever she wears the denture.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 459, 461.

q: A patient receiving tube feeding develops diarrhea. According to Table 30-12 in Hazzard, which adjustment is part of the possible management?
o: Increase the feeding rate to replace nutrients lost through diarrhea
Decrease the feeding rate as part of the response to diarrhea
Maintain the feeding rate and reduce fiber to improve tolerability
Increase the feeding rate and reduce fiber to shorten feeding time
explanation:
**Diarrhea during enteral nutrition** is one of the gastrointestinal complications addressed in the management table. The listed measures include decreasing delivery rate, increasing fiber, and antidiarrheals; the rate adjustment therefore goes downward, not upward (p. 431).
"↓Delivery rate, ↑fiber, antidiarrheals" (p. 431).

**A. Increase the feeding rate to replace nutrients lost through diarrhea.** Wrong, the table recommends decreasing delivery rate when managing diarrhea, rather than increasing it to compensate for losses (p. 431).
**B. Decrease the feeding rate as part of the response to diarrhea.** Correct, a lower delivery rate is an explicitly listed measure for diarrhea (p. 431).
**C. Maintain the feeding rate and reduce fiber to improve tolerability.** Wrong, the table lists increased fiber along with reduced delivery rate, rather than reducing fiber while preserving the rate (p. 431).
**D. Increase the feeding rate and reduce fiber to shorten feeding time.** Wrong, both proposed adjustments conflict with the diarrhea row, which calls for a lower rate and increased fiber (p. 431).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 431.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A woman recovering from bowel surgery cannot meet nutritional requirements orally. Her gastrointestinal tract has been assessed as functional, and enteral feeding has no contraindication, but it cannot yet meet her full requirements. Which nutrition strategy follows Hazzard?
o: Continue parenteral nutrition while withholding enteral nutrition
Combine enteral nutrition with supplemental parenteral nutrition
Withhold enteral nutrition until it can meet the full requirement
Replace central parenteral nutrition with peripheral parenteral nutrition
explanation:
Enteral nutrition uses the gastrointestinal tract. When the gut functions but cannot yet supply all requirements, **use enteral feeding and supplement the remaining deficit parenterally when indicated**.

**A. Parenteral feeding alone.** It bypasses a usable gut and omits the benefits of tolerated enteral intake.
**B. Combine the routes.** Provide the amount tolerated through the gut and tailor intravenous nutrition to the clinically important shortfall.
**C. Wait for full enteral tolerance.** Partial enteral feeding can start before it supplies the entire requirement.
**D. Switch to peripheral venous access.** Changing the catheter site does not address the opportunity to use the functioning gut.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 429.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: According to Hazzard, which enteral-feeding approach is appropriate for most patients with diabetes who need tube feeding?
o: Use a diabetes-specific formula routinely because it costs less
Use a standard formula and adjust the glucose-control regimen
Use a pulmonary formula to reduce carbon dioxide production
Use a glutamine-enriched formula for its established outcome benefit
explanation:
Tube feeding provides a predictable carbohydrate load, allowing glucose therapy to be matched to delivery. **A standard enteral formula with adjustment of the glucose-control regimen** is adequate for most patients with diabetes.

**A. Routine diabetes-specific formula because it is cheaper.** Standard formulas generally cost less. Diabetes alone does not require a specialized product.
**B. Standard formula plus glucose adjustment.** Monitor glucose and coordinate treatment with the amount and timing of feeding.
**C. Pulmonary formula.** A product marketed for respiratory disease does not address the patient's glucose management needs.
**D. Glutamine-enriched formula.** Trials have not demonstrated the asserted general improvement in clinical outcomes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 430.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: An 83-year-old woman with advanced COPD and cachexia has lost weight and eats poorly because of dyspnea. She uses continuous home oxygen, declines tube feeding, and agrees to oral nutritional supplements. Which supplement strategy follows Hazzard’s nutritional guidance?
o: Use standard-density supplements with meals to increase the volume consumed
Use higher-calorie supplements between meals to limit displacement of meal intake
Use higher-calorie supplements with meals to promote compensatory reduction in food intake
Use standard-density supplements between meals to deliver more calories per milliliter
explanation:
Breathlessness and early satiety can limit how much a person with severe COPD can eat. **Offer calorie-dense supplements between meals** to add energy in a small volume while preserving ordinary food intake.

**A. Standard-density supplement with meals.** Extra volume at mealtime can fill the patient before she eats enough food.
**B. Higher-calorie supplement between meals.** The smaller volume per calorie and separate timing both suit her intake barrier.
**C. Higher-calorie supplement with meals.** Its density is helpful, but deliberate displacement of regular food works against the goal.
**D. Standard-density supplement between meals.** The timing is appropriate. A standard formula does not supply more calories per milliliter than a concentrated one.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 428.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A woman receiving tube feeding after a stroke develops abdominal distension and pain with a gastric residual volume of 320 mL. There is no obstruction. What should be done before attributing this to failure of a prokinetic drug?
o: Change the prokinetic drug on the basis of the treatment duration
Evaluate remediable factors such as medications and feeding formula
Stop feeding for a prolonged period on the basis of the residual volume
Continue the feeding plan and reassess tolerability at the next routine review
explanation:
A gastric residual is a clue to feeding tolerance and must be interpreted alongside symptoms. With pain, distension and a residual of 320 mL, **evaluate reversible medication and formula factors promptly**.

**A. Change the prokinetic by duration.** Time already spent on a drug does not identify why gastric emptying is impaired.
**B. Look for reversible factors.** Review drugs that slow motility and how the formula is being delivered before calling the prokinetic ineffective.
**C. Hold feeds for a prolonged period.** This volume warrants assessment. By itself it is insufficient to dictate a prolonged interruption.
**D. Wait for routine review.** Pain and distension require timely reassessment of tolerance and the feeding plan.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 431.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: חולה עם דמנציה שהוגדר נוטה למות סובל מקושי חדש באכילה בזמן מחלה חריפה. לא ידועה התנגדות קודמת להזנה, ורצונו לקבלה הובהר. לפי המלצות משרד הבריאות, מה מתאים לדיון ב-PEG בשלב החריף?
o: להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה בעקבות הקושי
להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה לפי דרישת המשפחה
לראות במצב החריף עילה להקדמת התקנת PEG
לדחות התקנת PEG ולברר את המצב הרפואי
explanation:
**החלטה על PEG** בחולה עם דמנציה הנוטה למות היא רפואית ואישית. ההמלצות שוללות התקנה בזמן מחלה חריפה ומאפשרות לדחות את ההחלטה תוך בירור המצב ובחינת דרכי הזנה אחרות לפי הצורך; אין כאן הרשאה להתעלם מרצון המטופל (עמ׳ 6).
"בכל מקרה אין להתקין PEG בחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות כשהוא במצב של מחלה חריפה" (עמ׳ 6).

**א. להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה בעקבות הקושי.** שגויה, ההמלצה מפורשת שאין להתקין PEG במצב החריף המתואר (עמ׳ 6).
**ב. להתקין PEG במהלך המחלה החריפה לפי דרישת המשפחה.** שגויה, דרישת משפחה אינה מבטלת את ההמלצה הרפואית לגבי מחלה חריפה (עמ׳ 6).
**ג. לראות במצב החריף עילה להקדמת התקנת PEG.** שגויה, המצב החריף מצדיק דחייה והערכה, ולא הקדמת ההתקנה (עמ׳ 6).
**ד. לדחות התקנת PEG ולברר את המצב הרפואי.** נכונה, זו הגישה התואמת את ההמלצה בזמן הבירור של המצב החריף (עמ׳ 6).

מקור: המלצות הוועדה הארצית: PEG בחולה עם קיהיון הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 6.

q: An 84-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease develops progressive dysphagia over three weeks. Meals take 30 minutes, and he has lost 4 kg. He takes levodopa/carbidopa, rasagiline, amantadine, and quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime for hallucinations. Examination shows masked facies, resting tremor, and saliva pooling. A modified barium swallow shows delayed pharyngeal transit with residue; creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which statement explains why increasing dopaminergic medication need not improve his swallowing?
o: Axial swallowing symptoms often improve more than distal limb bradykinesia
Arm and leg rigidity often responds less than axial swallowing dysfunction
Axial swallowing symptoms often remain refractory despite improvement in limb rigidity
Axial swallowing symptoms often reflect isolated nigrostriatal dopaminergic denervation
explanation:
Levodopa often improves the speed and range of limb movements. Swallowing depends on axial motor control and other neural pathways that can deteriorate as Parkinson disease advances.

**Dysphagia can persist despite improved limb rigidity.** His pharyngeal delay, residue and weight loss warrant attention even if hand or leg movement improves after a dose.

**A. Swallowing improves more than hand slowness.** Fine distal movements are among the symptoms most likely to improve with levodopa.
**B. Limb rigidity responds less well.** Arm and leg rigidity generally responds better than axial swallowing dysfunction.
**C. Swallowing can remain refractory.** The same patient can have a clear limb response and persistent dysphagia because the affected pathways differ.
**D. Isolated dopamine loss explains dysphagia.** Nondopaminergic changes can contribute to axial dysfunction, limiting what a dose increase can achieve.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 939, 950.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS

q: אישה בת 79 במוסד סיעודי מפתחת דלקת ריאות אספירטיבית חוזרת. יש לה דמנציה וסקולרית בינונית (MMSE 18/30), סוכרת, ו-CKD שלב 3 (eGFR 45). התרופות הנוכחיות כוללות metformin 500 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg ליום, ו-sertraline 50 mg ליום. בדיקת בליעה בווידאופלואורוסקופיה מראה אספירציה שקטה של נוזלים דקים. קלינאית התקשורת ממליצה על נוזלים מסומכים, אך המטופלת מסרבת. לבתה יש ייפוי כוח מתמשך. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?
o: הנחת PEG tube לכל התזונה
דחיית סירוב המטופלת ואכיפת נוזלים מסומכים
דיון במטרות טיפול ובעדיפויות איכות החיים
הפסקת כל צריכה אורלית באופן מיידי
explanation:
**הזנה בדמנציה** מחייבת החלטה פרטנית על דרך מתן המזון והנוזלים, תוך הערכת בליעה וצרכים תזונתיים. ההמלצות הישראליות מעדיפות הזנה דרך הפה, וחוק זכויות החולה מחייב מידע על התועלת, הסיכון והחלופות לצורך הסכמה. לכן בירור **מטרות הטיפול ואיכות החיים** הוא הסקה יישומית המתאימה לסירוב המתואר, לפני בחירה חד צדדית בדרך הזנה (המלצות הוועדה, עמ׳ 5; סעיף 13).
"הדרך המועדפת למתן המזון והנוזלים היא דרך הפה." (המלצות הוועדה, עמ׳ 5)

**א. הנחת PEG tube לכל התזונה.** שגויה, מעבר אוטומטי להזנה דרך צינור אינו ההחלטה הפרטנית שההמלצות דורשות. יש לשקול דרך הזנה בהתאם למצב, לצרכים ולהערכת הבליעה, ולא להסיק אותה מעצם הסירוב להסמכה (עמ׳ 5; סעיף 13).
**ב. דחיית סירוב המטופלת ואכיפת נוזלים מסומכים.** שגויה, ההצעה עוקפת את בירור הסירוב וההסכמה. עצם קיומו של ייפוי כוח בשאלה אינו מתאר החלטה מוסכמת על כפיית נוזלים מסומכים; יש לברר הבנה ורצון לפני פעולה (יישום סעיף 13).
**ג. דיון ב-goals of care ובעדיפויות איכות החיים.** נכונה, דיון כזה מאפשר להבין את הסירוב ולשקול את בטיחות הבליעה מול מטרות המטופלת והחלופות. הוא מקדם החלטה פרטנית על ההזנה ומידע הנדרש להסכמה (הסקה מעמ׳ 5 וסעיף 13).
**ד. הפסקת כל צריכה אורלית באופן מיידי.** שגויה, הפסקת כל צריכה פומית אינה מסקנה אוטומטית מן הממצא לגבי נוזלים דקים. המקור דורש הערכה מקצועית והתאמה פרטנית של מתן מזון ונוזלים, ולא החלטה גורפת ללא בירור נוסף (עמ׳ 5).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8 בקובץ המקומי. המלצות הוועדה להזנה בחולים עם קיהיון, עמ׳ 5.

q: An 88-year-old man with erosive reflux esophagitis needs medication to heal the esophagitis. Which comparison is supported by Hazzard?
o: A proton pump inhibitor is more effective than an H2-blocker for healing esophagitis
An H2-blocker is more effective than a proton pump inhibitor for healing esophagitis
A prokinetic is more effective than a proton pump inhibitor for healing esophagitis
An H2-blocker plus a prokinetic is more effective than a proton pump inhibitor for healing esophagitis
explanation:
Healing erosive reflux esophagitis requires sustained acid suppression. **A proton pump inhibitor heals erosions more effectively than an H₂ blocker**.

**A. PPI preferred.** Inhibiting the final step of gastric acid secretion provides stronger suppression and improves mucosal healing.
**B. H₂ blocker preferred.** These agents reduce acid but achieve lower healing rates than PPIs.
**C. Prokinetic preferred.** Improving motility does not provide equivalent acid suppression or healing.
**D. H₂ blocker and prokinetic preferred.** Adding a motility agent does not give this combination a healing advantage over a PPI.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1319.

q: An older woman is about to start oral alendronate after assessment of its suitability. Which administration instruction is consistent with Hazzard's precautions against esophageal injury?
o: Take the medicine lying down with a full glass of water
Take the medicine upright with a small sip of water
Take the medicine upright with a full glass of water
Take the medicine lying down with a small sip of water
explanation:
Oral alendronate can irritate the esophagus if the tablet lodges or refluxes. **Take it on arising while sitting or standing, with a full glass of plain water. Stay upright for at least 30 minutes and until after the first food of the day.**

**A. Lying down with a full glass.** Water helps transit, but lying down increases the chance of prolonged esophageal contact.
**B. Upright with a small sip.** Posture is appropriate. A sip may not clear the tablet reliably.
**C. Upright with a full glass.** Gravity and approximately 180 to 240 mL of plain water facilitate transit. Wait at least 30 minutes before food, other beverages or medicines.
**D. Lying down with a sip.** Both aspects promote prolonged contact with the esophageal lining.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1316, 1318. FDA Fosamax prescribing information, administration instructions.

q: An 82-year-old man in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a recent left middle cerebral artery stroke with residual hemiparesis develops acute confusion and agitation during dinner. Staff observed food pocketing and failure to swallow before he became aggressive when they tried to help. He has diabetes and hypertension and takes aspirin, lisinopril, metformin, and mirtazapine 15 mg at bedtime. Oxygen saturation falls to 88%, and chest radiography shows a right lower-lobe infiltrate. Which source-described relationship makes a swallowing-related pulmonary complication relevant?
o: Dysphagia increases aspiration-pneumonia risk even when aspiration is silent.
Dysphagia-related aspiration is confined to material above the true vocal folds.
Dysphagia-related aspiration is identified by the presence of coughing with each event.
Dysphagia protects against pulmonary complications when food remains in the mouth.
explanation:
Poststroke dysphagia can allow food or saliva to pass below the true vocal folds without triggering a cough. Food pocketing followed by hypoxemia and a right lower-lobe infiltrate raises concern for aspiration. The abrupt presentation alone cannot distinguish pneumonitis from infectious pneumonia.

**A. Increased pneumonia risk.** Impaired swallowing allows bacteria-laden secretions to reach the lungs, even during clinically silent aspiration.
**B. Material above the vocal folds.** Material that enters the laryngeal vestibule and stays above the folds is called penetration. Aspiration crosses below them.
**C. Cough with every event.** A blunted protective response can leave airway entry unnoticed.
**D. Protection from food pocketing.** Retained food signals poor bolus clearance and can spill into the pharynx after the attempted swallow.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 438.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.438

q: אישה בת 91 עם דמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר מתקדמת (תלויה בכל ADLs) מובאת לחדר מיון ממוסד סיעודי בשל ירידה בצריכה אוראלית במשך שבועיים. היא ירדה 8% ממשקל גופה ב-3 חודשים. הצוות מדווח שהיא מסובבת את ראשה מהאוכל ומהדקת את פיה. סימנים חיוניים יציבים. בדיקות מראות albumin 2.8 g/dL, BUN 38 mg/dL, Cr 1.1 mg/dL. בתה שואלת לגבי הנחת feeding tube. לפי הספרות הנוכחית, מה יש לייעץ לה?
o: הזנה באמצעות PEG משפרת הישרדות אצל חולים בדמנציה מתקדמת
הזנה באמצעות PEG מונעת דלקת ריאות משאיפה בדמנציה מתקדמת
הזנה באמצעות PEG אינה משפרת הישרדות ואינה מונעת אספירציה
הזנה באמצעות זונדה עדיפה על PEG בחולים בדמנציה מתקדמת
explanation:
**הזנה בצינור בדמנציה מתקדמת** אינה מספקת יתרון מוכח בהישרדות או במניעת אספירציות לעומת האכלה דרך הפה; מסמך הוועדה מתאר היעדר הבדל בתוצאות אלו (עמ׳ 3, 4). לכן אין להבטיח לבת שהנחת צינור תשיג מטרות אלה. ההחלטה על דרך ההזנה דורשת הערכה רפואית אישית, והמסמך מעדיף הזנה דרך הפה כאשר היא מתאימה למצב החולה (עמ׳ 5).
"כמו כן הוכיחו מחקרים שונים שאין הבדל בין שתי שיטות ההאכלה הללו ביחס לסיבוכים שונים, כולל אספירציות." (עמ׳ 4).

**א. הזנה באמצעות PEG משפרת הישרדות אצל חולים בדמנציה מתקדמת.** שגויה, לא הודגם יתרון בתוחלת החיים בהזנה מלאכותית לעומת האכלה דרך הפה, ולכן אין בסיס להבטיח הארכת חיים מהנחת PEG במקרה המתואר (עמ׳ 3, סעיף ב.7).
**ב. הזנה באמצעות PEG מונעת דלקת ריאות משאיפה בדמנציה מתקדמת.** שגויה, המסמך מציין היעדר הבדל באספירציות בין דרכי ההאכלה; צינור אינו מספק את ההגנה המובטחת באפשרות זו (עמ׳ 4).
**ג. הזנה באמצעות PEG אינה משפרת הישרדות ואינה מונעת אספירציה.** נכונה, זו האפשרות התואמת את היעדר היתרון המתואר בהישרדות ובאספירציות. אין פירוש הדבר שמוותרים על טיפול תזונתי, אלא שמתכננים אותו לפי מצבה האישי של החולה (עמ׳ 3 עד 5).
**ד. הזנה באמצעות זונדה עדיפה על PEG בחולים בדמנציה מתקדמת.** שגויה, המסמך אינו מראה יתרון בתוחלת החיים לזונדה לעומת PEG; בחירת דרך ההזנה אישית, ולא מבוססת על עדיפות גורפת של זונדה (עמ׳ 4, 5).

מקור: הוועדה הארצית לגריאטריה, המלצות בנושא הזנה בחולי קיהיון, 4Recommendations.pdf; עמ׳ 3, 4, 4, 5.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות

q: גבר בן 77 מגיע עם 4 חודשים של dysphagia פרוגרסיבי לסולידים ונוזלים, ירידה של 7 ק"ג במשקל, ושיעול לילי. יש לו סוכרת, CAD, ו-CKD stage 3b (eGFR 32). התרופות כוללות metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol, ו-lisinopril. Barium swallow מראה התכווצויות טרציאריות ושט מורחב עם היצרות 'bird's beak' בצומת GE. Manometry מאשר achalasia. הוא מסרב ל-surgical myotomy. איזו טיפול תרופתי מתאים ביותר בהתחשב בתפקוד הכלייתי שלו?
o: Nifedipine 10 mg sublingual לפני ארוחות
Sildenafil 50 mg daily
הזרקת botulinum toxin
Isosorbide dinitrate 5 mg sublingual לפני ארוחות
explanation:
**התשובה הנכונה היא הזרקת botulinum toxin**.

**א. Nifedipine 10 mg sublingual לפני ארוחות.** שגויה, האפשרות ״nifedipine״ יכולה להפחית במידה מסוימת את לחץ ה-LES, אך היא מלכודת — calcium channel blockers עלולים להחמיר orthostatic hypotension בקשישים, במיוחד בשילוב עם beta blockers. מתן sublingual גורם לספיגה לא צפויה.
**ב. Sildenafil 50 mg daily.** שגויה, האפשרות ״sildenafil״ הינה contraindicated עם nitrates (שמטופלי CAD רבים נוטלים PRN) ועלולה לגרום לhypotension מסוכן בשילוב עם beta blockers. עם eGFR 32, יידרש dose adjustment.
**ג. הזרקת botulinum toxin.** נכונה, עבור מטופלים קשישים עם achalasia שמסרבים או אינם מועמדים לטיפול דפיניטיבי (myotomy), botulinum toxin מספק הקלה סימפטומטית ל-3-6 חודשים עם אפקטים סיסטמיים מינימליים. הוא מתאים במיוחד למטופלים עם פגיעה כלייתית כיוון שאין לו renal clearance. בחולים קשישים עם achalasia, ל-pneumatic dilation יש סיכון גבוה יותר ל-perforation בהשוואה לצעירים. Botulinum toxin הוא הבטוח ביותר אך מצריך הזרקות חוזרות. יש תמיד לשלול pseudoachalasia ממסה בצומת GE בקשישים עם onset מהיר של תסמינים.
**ד. Isosorbide dinitrate 5 mg sublingual לפני ארוחות.** שגויה, האפשרות ״isosorbide״ יכולה להפחית את לחץ ה-LES אך גורמת בשכיחות לכאבי ראש ו-hypotension בקשישים. בשילוב עם metoprolol ושימוש אפשרי ב-nitrates עבור CAD, קיים סיכון ל-hypotension מסוכן.

מקור: Hazzard Ch 31 — DISORDERS OF SWALLOWING · Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss
ref: Hazzard Ch 31 — DISORDERS OF SWALLOWING · Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss

q: An 85-year-old woman has had three episodes of pneumonia in six months. She has mild cognitive impairment, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, and depression. She takes levothyroxine 88 micrograms daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium/vitamin D, and amitriptyline 50 mg nightly. She reports dry mouth and difficulty initiating swallowing; a modified barium swallow shows delayed initiation and reduced pharyngeal contraction. Which medication-related mechanism warrants review?
o: Amitriptyline increases salivary flow through anticholinergic activity.
Amitriptyline reduces salivary flow through cholinergic stimulation.
Amitriptyline reduces salivary flow through anticholinergic activity.
Amitriptyline increases salivary flow through cholinergic stimulation.
explanation:
Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant with strong antimuscarinic effects. Reduced salivation can make a food bolus harder to form and swallow, making the nightly dose worth reviewing in this woman with dry mouth and recurrent pneumonia.

**A. Anticholinergic increase in saliva.** Blocking muscarinic receptors reduces the glands’ response to the nerve signals that normally stimulate secretion.
**B. Cholinergic reduction in saliva.** Cholinergic stimulation promotes salivation, so it would not explain her dry mouth.
**C. Anticholinergic reduction in saliva.** Amitriptyline can reduce lubrication and aggravate dysphagia. Her weak pharyngeal contraction may have additional causes.
**D. Cholinergic increase in saliva.** This describes a salivary stimulant such as pilocarpine. Amitriptyline blocks muscarinic signaling.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 446, 1064.

q: A 73-year-old man with Parkinson disease and diabetes presents with fever and cough. His wife reports three days of increasing confusion and difficulty swallowing tablets. Temperature is 38.4°C, heart rate 102, respiratory rate 24, BP 108/68, and oxygen saturation 91%. Chest radiography shows right-middle-lobe consolidation. WBC is 14,000, glucose 284, and creatinine 1.8 (baseline 1.2); calculated creatinine clearance is 41 mL/min. He grimaces when swallowing water. When reviewing antibiotics for inpatient pneumonia, which pair consists of two agents that Table 105-11 says do not need renal dose reduction at this creatinine clearance?
o: Intravenous moxifloxacin together with intravenous levofloxacin
Intravenous ceftriaxone together with intravenous azithromycin
Intravenous piperacillin–tazobactam together with intravenous tobramycin
Intravenous cefepime together with intravenous ciprofloxacin
explanation:
**Renal dose adjustment** is drug-specific in Table 105-11 (p. 1689). The azithromycin row states "No adjustment required", and the ceftriaxone row states "> 10: not required" (p. 1689). Applied to the stated creatinine clearance, both meet the question’s dosing condition; this is not a claim that every listed pair is an appropriate empiric regimen.

**A. Intravenous moxifloxacin together with intravenous levofloxacin.** Wrong, moxifloxacin needs no adjustment, but levofloxacin has a reduced-dose entry for the range containing this clearance (p. 1689).
**B. Intravenous ceftriaxone together with intravenous azithromycin.** Correct, azithromycin needs no adjustment, and ceftriaxone requires no adjustment above the listed clearance threshold (p. 1689).
**C. Intravenous piperacillin–tazobactam together with intravenous tobramycin.** Wrong, both piperacillin–tazobactam and tobramycin have reduced-dose entries for the renal-function ranges containing this clearance (p. 1689).
**D. Intravenous cefepime together with intravenous ciprofloxacin.** Wrong, ciprofloxacin has a no-adjustment entry for this range, but cefepime has a reduced-frequency entry (p. 1689).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1689.
ref: Hazzard Ch 105 — BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA AND TUBERCULOSIS

q: מטופלת עם דמנציה ודיספגיה מתקשה לאכול את המרקם שניתן לה. לפי המלצות הוועדה הארצית להזנה בדמנציה, מהו העיקרון לבחירת דרך ההזנה?
o: להחיל מרקם אחיד על דיירי המחלקה לפי האבחנה
להתאים את ההזנה אישית עם הערכת בליעה וצוות
להעביר להזנה בצינור בעקבות עצם אבחנת הדמנציה
לבחור מרקם לפי העדפת המשפחה ללא הערכת בליעה
explanation:
בחירת **דרך ההזנה** צריכה להיות רפואית ואישית, בהתאם למצב המטופלת ולצרכיה. ההמלצות מעדיפות הזנה דרך הפה ומדגישות הערכת בליעה, הנחיות מותאמות ועבודת צוות; אין בכך אישור אוטומטי לתזונה רגילה במי שמתקשה בבליעה (עמ׳ 5).
"החלטה בדבר צורת מתן המזון והנוזלים צריכה להיות רפואית אינדיבידואלית" (עמ׳ 5).
"הדרך המועדפת למתן המזון והנוזלים היא דרך הפה." (עמ׳ 5).

**א. להחיל מרקם אחיד על דיירי המחלקה לפי האבחנה.** שגויה, מרקם אחיד לפי אבחנה אינו ממלא את הדרישה להתאמה אישית (עמ׳ 5).
**ב. להתאים את ההזנה אישית עם הערכת בליעה וצוות.** נכונה, האפשרות כוללת את ההערכה המקצועית וההתאמה האישית הנדרשות (עמ׳ 5).
**ג. להעביר להזנה בצינור בעקבות עצם אבחנת הדמנציה.** שגויה, הדרך המועדפת היא הפה; אבחנת דמנציה כשלעצמה אינה מחליפה החלטה רפואית אישית (עמ׳ 5).
**ד. לבחור מרקם לפי העדפת המשפחה ללא הערכת בליעה.** שגויה, העדפה אינה מחליפה את הערכת הבליעה וההנחיות המקצועיות המתוארות (עמ׳ 5).

מקור: המלצות הוועדה הארצית על הזנה בדמנציה, עמ׳ 5.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות

q: A 78-year-old man says that pills stick when he swallows. Medication review has not yet identified a particular causative drug. Which advice is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Review each drug for crushing suitability or a liquid form
Take the pills while lying down to reduce swallowing effort
Reduce the liquid taken with pills to minimize swallowing volume
Group the pills at bedtime and take them while lying in bed
explanation:
For **difficulty swallowing pills**, Hazzard recommends discussing which preparations can be crushed, mixed with food, or given in liquid form. Position and fluid intake also matter: "Pill-induced damage to the esophagus can occur if pills are taken when lying down or with inadequate amounts of liquid." (p. 451).

**A. Review each drug for crushing suitability or a liquid form.** Correct, this checks the suitability of individual medications instead of assuming that every pill can be crushed (p. 451).
**B. Take the pills while lying down to reduce swallowing effort.** Wrong, lying down when taking pills is identified as a circumstance in which esophageal injury can occur (p. 451).
**C. Reduce the liquid taken with pills to minimize swallowing volume.** Wrong, inadequate liquid when taking pills is identified as a circumstance in which esophageal injury can occur (p. 451).
**D. Group the pills at bedtime and take them while lying in bed.** Wrong, taking the pills while lying in bed retains the position associated with pill-induced esophageal injury (p. 451).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 451.

q: An ambulatory acute-rehabilitation patient without cognitive impairment requires thickened liquids because of dysphagia. The swallowing team is considering a free-water protocol. Which description matches the protocols discussed in Hazzard?
o: Thin water during meals and thickened liquids between meals.
Intensive oral care and thin water between meals.
Thin water between meals as a replacement for oral care.
Thin water with each meal after cleaning the mouth.
explanation:
**Free-water protocols** combine intensive oral care with thin liquids between meals while retaining thickened liquids during meals. Initial studies had small samples and restrictive selection criteria, so the description should not be taken as evidence of safety for every patient with dysphagia (p. 450). "These “free water” protocols involve intensive oral care followed by ingestion of thin liquids between meals but thickened liquids during meals." (p. 450).

**A. Thin water during meals and thickened liquids between meals.** Wrong, the timing is incorrect: thickened liquids remain part of meals, while thin liquids are taken between meals (p. 450).
**B. Intensive oral care and thin water between meals.** Correct, this includes both the oral-care requirement and the between-meal timing of thin liquids (p. 450).
**C. Thin water between meals as a replacement for oral care.** Wrong, oral care is part of the protocol and precedes thin-liquid intake; water is not a substitute for it (p. 450).
**D. Thin water with each meal after cleaning the mouth.** Wrong, oral care does not change the protocol's retention of thickened liquids during meals (p. 450).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 450.

q: A 79-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has lost about 7 kg in four months. He takes small bites, chews extensively, reports food going 'the wrong way,' and has a wet, gurgly voice after meals. Medications are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily; creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. Modified barium swallow shows vallecular residue and delayed swallow initiation. Which statement correctly characterizes rehabilitative swallowing therapy considered after this assessment?
o: It uses environmental adaptations to compensate for impaired swallowing mechanics
It changes bolus characteristics to compensate for impaired swallowing mechanics
It exercises swallowing muscles to improve their physiologic function
It uses postural adjustments to compensate for impaired swallowing mechanics
explanation:
**Swallowing rehabilitation** is distinguished from compensatory changes in posture, bolus characteristics, or environment (pp. 449–450). "Rehabilitative interventions have the capacity to directly improve dysphagia at the biological level." (p. 449). They target structures such as muscle or neural circuitry, with exercise approaches applied to swallowing musculature (pp. 449–450); the assessment helps define which physiology needs treatment (p. 448).

**A. It uses environmental adaptations to compensate for impaired swallowing mechanics.** Wrong, environmental adaptation is described as compensation, whereas rehabilitation directly targets biological structures or function (p. 449).
**B. It changes bolus characteristics to compensate for impaired swallowing mechanics.** Wrong, altering the bolus is a compensatory approach, rather than the direct muscle or neural target used to define rehabilitation (p. 449).
**C. It exercises swallowing muscles to improve their physiologic function.** Correct, exercise directed at swallowing musculature matches the rehabilitative approach described (pp. 449–450).
**D. It uses postural adjustments to compensate for impaired swallowing mechanics.** Wrong, postural adjustment is classified among compensatory interventions, not as the defining direct biological action of rehabilitation (p. 449).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 448, 449, 450.

q: An 83-year-old woman with depression has a partial response and adverse effects during antidepressant treatment. After clinical reassessment, she and her clinician agree on a medication change. Which principle should guide dose selection and adjustment?
o: Select a target dose from the usual range despite troublesome adverse effects
Start at the full target dose and escalate rapidly for inadequate response
Adjust the dose to individual response, adverse effects, safety, and drug interactions
Set the effective dose from age and weight before assessing treatment response
explanation:
Effective antidepressant dosing depends on individual tolerability and response. **Adjust the dose to benefit, adverse effects, interactions and safety** when changing treatment.

**A. Usual range despite adverse effects.** A population range cannot override troublesome toxicity.
**B. Full dose and rapid escalation.** Starting lower allows early assessment of tolerability.
**C. Individualized adjustment.** Balance symptom improvement with effects that may impair everyday function.
**D. Age and weight alone.** These cannot predict a person's effective dose without clinical follow-up.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1015.

q: A 90-year-old man receiving palliative care reports oral discomfort. Examination shows soft white plaques that wipe away, exposing red mucosa underneath. Which diagnosis matches this appearance?
o: Hyperplastic candidiasis of the oral mucosa
Pseudomembranous candidiasis of the oral mucosa
Atrophic candidiasis of the oral mucosa
Candidiasis at the lip corners with local inflammation
explanation:
**Pseudomembranous candidiasis** is characterized by removable soft plaques over erythematous mucosa. Hazzard describes "Soft, white or yellow plaques that can be wiped off to expose an underlying erythematous mucosa" (Table 32-3, p. 454). Removal by wiping distinguishes this appearance from the nonremovable lesions described for hyperplastic candidiasis (p. 454).

**A. Hyperplastic candidiasis of the oral mucosa.** Wrong, hyperplastic candidiasis has leukoplakic or keratotic lesions that cannot be removed by scraping, unlike the removable plaques in the stem (p. 454).
**B. Pseudomembranous candidiasis of the oral mucosa.** Correct, the removable soft white plaques and underlying red mucosa match the table’s description (p. 454).
**C. Atrophic candidiasis of the oral mucosa.** Wrong, atrophic candidiasis is described as painful erythematous mucosa with a bald-appearing tongue or denture-area inflammation, rather than removable plaques (p. 454).
**D. Candidiasis at the lip corners with local inflammation.** Wrong, angular cheilitis involves cracked or fissured lesions at the lip commissures, rather than the plaque pattern described (p. 454).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 454.

q: An 84-year-old man has lost weight after developing difficulty chewing solid food. He is hungry and has no signs of depression. Oral examination shows painful carious teeth and poorly fitting dentures. Which intervention targets the identified barrier to intake?
o: Prescribe an appetite stimulant to increase the desire to eat.
Provide dental treatment and adjust the dentures for chewing.
Prescribe an antidepressant to increase the desire to eat.
Restrict food choices to increase adherence to a set menu.
explanation:
A hungry patient who loses weight because chewing hurts has a mechanical barrier to intake. **Treat the caries and refit the dentures** so he can chew comfortably.

**A. Appetite stimulant.** He wants to eat already. Increasing desire does not relieve dental pain.
**B. Dental and denture care.** Treatment addresses both the painful teeth and the poor fit interfering with mastication.
**C. Antidepressant.** The history provides no depression to treat and explains the low intake through oral pain.
**D. Restrict food choices.** A narrower menu cannot correct his dentition and may further limit intake.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 427.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: A 79-year-old woman with dementia and periodontal disease is assessed before dental treatment. After evaluating her oral condition, the team considers the extent of periodontal therapy. What should guide this choice?
o: Her health and functional status after an overall assessment
Her chronological age as a basis for limiting the extent of treatment
An assumption that long-term treatment results are poorer in old age
An assumption that slower healing warrants routine tooth extraction
explanation:
Periodontal therapy aims to control inflammation around the teeth and preserve the tissues that support them. For this woman with dementia, the extent of treatment depends on her oral findings, general health and ability to tolerate treatment and maintain oral hygiene.

**A. Assess health and function.** Consider which teeth can be preserved and whether she can manage daily plaque control independently or with caregiver help.
**B. Limit treatment by age.** At the same chronological age, patients can differ substantially in procedural tolerance and support for mouth care.
**C. Expect poorer long-term results.** Older adults can achieve periodontal outcomes comparable to those in younger adults.
**D. Extract because healing is slower.** Postsurgical healing may take longer. The prognosis of each tooth and the burden of preserving it guide extraction decisions.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 457.

q: A 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease and dysphagia aspirates thin liquids during a swallowing assessment. The team compares honey-thick liquids with chin-down posture. What does Hazzard report for short-term aspiration and pneumonia prevention over three months?
o: Less short-term aspiration and better pneumonia prevention
Less short-term aspiration and similar pneumonia prevention
More short-term aspiration and better pneumonia prevention
More short-term aspiration and similar pneumonia prevention
explanation:
A swallow study shows whether liquid enters the airway during testing. In patients with Parkinson disease who aspirated thin liquids, honey-thick liquid reduced immediate aspiration compared with chin-down posture. Three-month follow-up found no clear pneumonia advantage.

**A. Less aspiration and better pneumonia prevention.** Avoiding aspiration on a test swallow cannot by itself predict fewer infections over subsequent months.
**B. Less aspiration and similar pneumonia rates.** Fewer patients aspirated with honey-thick liquid during testing. Follow-up found no significant difference in pneumonia between chin-down posture and the pooled thickened-liquid groups.
**C. More aspiration and better prevention.** More patients aspirated with chin-down posture, and thickened liquids showed no subsequent advantage against infection.
**D. More aspiration and similar pneumonia rates.** The pneumonia comparison fits, but honey-thick liquid produced less airway entry on fluoroscopy.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 450. Logemann et al., JSLHR 2008, p. 173 and Robbins et al., Ann Intern Med 2008, p. 509.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.450

q: Oral examination reveals soft white plaques that can be wiped away, exposing erythematous mucosa. Which fungal infection pattern matches this appearance in Hazzard?
o: Hyperplastic candidiasis with keratotic mucosal lesions
Pseudomembranous candidiasis of the oral mucosa
Atrophic candidiasis with painful erythematous mucosal lesions
Angular cheilitis with cracked or fissured lip commissures
explanation:
**Pseudomembranous candidiasis** produces removable white or yellow plaques over erythematous mucosa. Hazzard distinguishes it from nonremovable keratotic lesions, painful atrophic erythema, and fissures at the lip corners by their appearance and location (p. 454, Table 32-3).
"Soft, white or yellow plaques that can be wiped off to expose an underlying erythematous mucosa" (p. 454).
"Leukoplakic or keratotic lesions that cannot be removed by scraping" (p. 454).

**A. Hyperplastic candidiasis with keratotic mucosal lesions.** Wrong, hyperplastic lesions are leukoplakic or keratotic and cannot be removed by scraping, unlike the removable plaques described (p. 454).
**B. Pseudomembranous candidiasis of the oral mucosa.** Correct, removable soft plaques exposing underlying erythema match the table's description (p. 454).
**C. Atrophic candidiasis with painful erythematous mucosal lesions.** Wrong, atrophic candidiasis is described as painful erythematous mucosa, with a bald-appearing tongue or denture-area inflammation, rather than removable plaques (p. 454).
**D. Angular cheilitis with cracked or fissured lip commissures.** Wrong, angular cheilitis affects the lip commissures with cracked or fissured lesions, not plaques over the oral mucosa (p. 454).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 454.

q: A 91-year-old man in supported housing with mild dementia (MMSE 22) has lost 3 kg over two months. Staff report that he refuses denture care and eats soft foods. His upper denture fits poorly, with marked ridge resorption and several denture-associated pressure ulcers. His daughter asks about implants. Creatinine clearance is 45 mL/min; medications include donepezil and metoprolol. Which principle should guide initial management of the suspected denture trauma?
o: Retain the poorly fitting denture while adding nutritional supplements.
Retain the poorly fitting denture while changing food texture.
Remove the source of mechanical trauma from the poorly fitting denture.
Retain the poorly fitting denture while observing the ulcers for healing.
explanation:
Ridge resorption can leave a denture pressing unevenly on the tissue beneath it. This man’s ulcers and poor fit make relief of pressure the first step, before considering implants or another long-term prosthesis.

**A. Keep the denture and add supplements.** Supplements may help address weight loss, but the denture can still injure the mucosa when worn.
**B. Keep the denture and soften food.** He already eats soft food. Reducing the effort of chewing leaves the pressure points in contact with the ridge.
**C. Take the ill-fitting denture out.** Relieving pressure allows the ulcers to heal. A dental assessment can determine how to restore a comfortable fit.
**D. Observe during continued use.** Repeated loading can delay healing. Reassess the ulcers after the denture pressure has been relieved.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 459, 461.

q: A 75-year-old woman with Sjögren syndrome reports worsening dry mouth after an anticholinergic medication was added for pain. Which step addresses a possible medication-related cause?
o: Increase the dose of the implicated medication to stimulate saliva
Reduce the dose or substitute the medication causing dry mouth
Attribute the worsening symptoms to normal age-related salivary decline
Maintain the dose and set aside the medication as a cause
explanation:
Xerostomia is the sensation of dry mouth. Sjögren syndrome can reduce salivary reserve, so a new drug that blocks muscarinic signaling can worsen dryness. Reviewing its dose or choosing a less anticholinergic analgesic addresses a potentially reversible contributor.

**A. Increase the dose.** Greater anticholinergic exposure can suppress salivation further.
**B. Reduce the dose or substitute the drug.** Lowering the anticholinergic burden may relieve the added dryness while preserving a plan for pain control.
**C. Attribute symptoms to age.** Healthy aging generally preserves daily salivary output. Worsening dryness warrants assessment for disease and medication effects.
**D. Continue the dose and dismiss a drug effect.** Sjögren syndrome and medication-induced dryness can coexist, and the worsening followed the new prescription.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 457–458.

q: בת 86 עם דמנציה, שהוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות, מאושפזת עם מחלה חריפה וקושי בהאכלה דרך הפה. המשפחה מבקשת להתקין PEG כעת. לפי המלצות המותב הארצי, מהי הגישה המתאימה בשלב החריף?
o: להתקין PEG כעת ולבחון את ההזנה לאחר ההחלמה
לקבוע זונדה קבועה ולבחון את הבליעה לאחר ההחלמה
לדחות PEG כעת ולתכנן הזנה זמנית באופן אישי
להתקין PEG לצד הזנה דרך הפה ולתת נוזלים
explanation:
**מחלה חריפה בחולה הנוטה למות עם דמנציה** היא מצב שבו ההמלצות מורות שלא להתקין PEG, משום שהפעולה מסכנת את חייו. יש לבחור דרך ביניים להזנה ולנוזלים לפי שיקול רפואי אישי ולשמור על הידרציה בזמן בירור המצב (עמ׳ 6).
"בכל מקרה אין להתקין PEG בחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות כשהוא במצב של מחלה חריפה," (עמ׳ 6).
"בתקופת ההמתנה יש להקפיד על מניעת דהידרציה." (עמ׳ 6).

**א. להתקין PEG כעת ולבחון את ההזנה לאחר ההחלמה.** שגויה, המקור קובע שאין להתקין PEG במצב מחלה חריפה קשה בשל הסיכון לחיים (עמ׳ 6).
**ב. לקבוע זונדה קבועה ולבחון את הבליעה לאחר ההחלמה.** שגויה, המקור מתיר שימוש בזונדה באופן זמני וקצר, אך אינו ממליץ עליה כפתרון קבוע (עמ׳ 6).
**ג. לדחות PEG כעת ולתכנן הזנה זמנית באופן אישי.** נכונה, דחיית ההתקנה ותכנון דרך ביניים אישית תואמים את ההמלצות למצב החריף המתואר (עמ׳ 6).
**ד. להתקין PEG לצד הזנה דרך הפה ולתת נוזלים.** שגויה, שילוב עם האכלה דרך הפה ומתן נוזלים אינו מבטל את ההנחיה שלא להתקין PEG בשלב המחלה החריפה במטופלת זו (עמ׳ 6; יישום).

מקור: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות, עמ׳ 6.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An older man has dry mouth after radiation treatment. Examination indicates little or no remaining salivary gland function. Which approach matches this finding?
o: Stimulate salivary secretion by using sugar-free chewing gum
Provide oral moisture using saliva substitute and gel
Stimulate salivary secretion by using oral pilocarpine therapy
Stimulate salivary secretion by using oral cevimeline therapy
explanation:
Treatment of dry mouth after radiation depends on how much saliva the glands can still produce. With little or no residual secretion, a saliva substitute and moisturizing gel can lubricate the mouth directly.

**A. Sugar-free chewing gum.** Chewing triggers a salivary reflex that requires functioning gland tissue to produce moisture.
**B. Saliva substitute and gel.** These coat the mucosa and can relieve dryness during speaking or eating even when the glands barely respond.
**C. Pilocarpine.** This muscarinic agonist stimulates secretion from viable salivary tissue. Extensive gland injury limits the expected response.
**D. Cevimeline.** It also activates muscarinic receptors and is most useful when there is enough residual gland function to increase output.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 458.

q: An 81-year-old woman taking methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis develops cytopenia and oral mucosal ulcerations. Which mechanism is listed for this drug in Hazzard's treatment table?
o: Inhibition of the enzyme dihydrofolic acid reductase
Inhibition of the cellular synthesis of pyrimidines
Neutralization of the cytokine TNF by an antibody
Blockade of the receptor for the cytokine IL-1
explanation:
**Methotrexate** is listed as a potent inhibitor of dihydrofolic acid reductase. The same table lists cytopenia and mucosal ulcerations among its adverse effects, matching the findings that prompted the question (p. 1614).
"Potent inhibitor of dihydrofolic acid reductase" (p. 1614).
"Side effects: cytopenia (anemia), liver toxicity (fibrosis and cirrhosis), hypersensitivity pneumonitis, infections, mucosal ulcerations, alopecia" (p. 1614).

**A. Inhibition of the enzyme dihydrofolic acid reductase.** Correct, the enzyme inhibition matches the methotrexate row, which also lists both adverse findings in this patient (p. 1614).
**B. Inhibition of the cellular synthesis of pyrimidines.** Wrong, pyrimidine synthesis inhibition is assigned to leflunomide; it does not describe the listed action of the patient's methotrexate (p. 1614).
**C. Neutralization of the cytokine TNF by an antibody.** Wrong, the methotrexate row identifies enzyme inhibition, whereas anti-TNF antibodies are listed separately as biologic agents (p. 1614).
**D. Blockade of the receptor for the cytokine IL-1.** Wrong, receptor blockade does not describe the action listed for methotrexate, which is inhibition of dihydrofolic acid reductase (p. 1614).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1614.
ref: Hazzard Ch 101 — RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND OTHER AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES
chapterTitle: Rheumatoid Arthritis and Other Autoimmune Diseases

q: A 78-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment lives alone and has lost 8 kg in four months. His son finds spoiled food and empty pizza boxes at home. Examination shows moderate periodontal disease and halitosis; MMSE is 24/30 with executive dysfunction and BMI is 19.8. Which assessment directly examines his ability to shop for food and prepare meals?
o: Measurement of resting energy expenditure.
Assessment of instrumental activities of daily living.
Measurement of the serum albumin concentration.
Assessment of the percentage of body fat.
explanation:
Instrumental activities of daily living are complex tasks needed to manage an independent household. **Assess IADLs, including shopping and preparing meals**, to understand how executive difficulty may contribute to weight loss.

**A. Resting energy expenditure.** It estimates calorie requirements rather than ability to obtain food.
**B. IADL assessment.** Ask about shopping, food storage, meal planning and cooking, with collateral information if needed.
**C. Serum albumin.** It is influenced by illness and cannot measure independent meal preparation.
**D. Body-fat percentage.** It describes body composition, not household performance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 123.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: An 85-year-old woman develops dry mouth and altered taste after starting a medication with anticholinergic activity. Examination shows reduced saliva without mucosal lesions. Which explanation is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Reduced saliva impairs food dissolution and delivery of tastants to taste buds
Normal aging of the salivary glands routinely reduces total daily salivary output
Reduced saliva strengthens mucosal protection against local microbial infection
Reduced saliva improves food lubrication and preparation for swallowing
explanation:
Taste depends on chemicals from food reaching receptors in solution. The timing of her dry mouth and objectively reduced saliva point to an anticholinergic drug effect that can alter taste even when the mucosa looks healthy.

**A. Impaired delivery to taste buds.** Less fluid is available to dissolve food compounds and carry them to the receptors, so familiar foods can seem bland.
**B. Routine age-related loss of output.** Healthy salivary glands generally maintain total daily secretion with advancing age, although their reserve may decline.
**C. Stronger antimicrobial protection.** Saliva washes oral surfaces and supplies antimicrobial factors. Reduced flow weakens those defenses.
**D. Better lubrication for swallowing.** Dry food is harder to gather into a cohesive bolus and move toward the pharynx.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 457.

q: A woman with dysphagia pockets food in her cheek and chews for prolonged periods. Before selecting swallowing reminders or a texture modification, what should guide the intervention?
o: The swallowing pathophysiology and its effect on bolus flow
The meal duration used as a substitute for swallowing assessment
The dementia diagnosis used as a substitute for swallowing assessment
The body weight used as a substitute for swallowing assessment
explanation:
**Dysphagia intervention** should target the movement disorder responsible for abnormal bolus flow. Hazzard states that "effective dysphagia intervention relies on an accurate diagnosis of the specific pathophysiology" (p. 448); assessment clarifies what must change for safe and efficient bolus flow.

**A. The swallowing pathophysiology and its effect on bolus flow.** Correct, the intervention needs to address the defined swallowing impairment and its effect on movement and clearance of the bolus (p. 448).
**B. The meal duration used as a substitute for swallowing assessment.** Wrong, meal duration does not define the movement disorder and bolus-flow impairment that should guide treatment (p. 448).
**C. The dementia diagnosis used as a substitute for swallowing assessment.** Wrong, a dementia diagnosis does not specify the swallowing sequence that needs modification (p. 448).
**D. The body weight used as a substitute for swallowing assessment.** Wrong, weight does not characterize the movement disorder responsible for impaired bolus flow (p. 448).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 448.

q: After urgent problems have been treated, an older adult with periodontal disease needs a plan for the extent of dental treatment and tooth preservation. What should guide that plan?
o: The patient's chronological age as the basis for treatment
The patient's age group compared with younger adults
The average life expectancy for the patient's age and sex
The patient's health and function after oral and systemic assessment
explanation:
After urgent dental problems are treated, periodontal planning asks which teeth can remain useful and what care they will require. Combine each tooth’s prognosis with the patient’s general health and ability to undergo treatment and maintain the result.

**A. Chronological age.** Two people of the same age can have very different periodontal support and functional capacity.
**B. Comparison with younger adults.** Long-term treatment outcomes can be comparable across age groups, even when postoperative healing is slower.
**C. Average life expectancy.** An age-and-sex estimate cannot tell whether a particular tooth is salvageable or whether the patient can manage its care.
**D. Oral and systemic assessment.** Weigh the benefit of retaining each tooth against the demands of treatment and the assistance the patient needs for daily cleaning.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 457.

q: In the study of patients with Parkinson disease or dementia described in Hazzard, honey-thick liquids were compared with nectar-thick liquids and chin-down posture. Which result distinguishes short-term aspiration from pneumonia during follow-up?
o: Less short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate
More short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate
Less short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate
More short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate
explanation:
In patients with Parkinson disease or dementia, honey-thick liquid most often prevented aspiration during fluoroscopy. Even with that consistency, about half the participants still aspirated, and follow-up showed no clear advantage for preventing pneumonia.

**A. Less aspiration and fewer pneumonias.** The immediate benefit was measurable, but the observed three-month pneumonia rate was numerically higher with honey-thick than with nectar-thick liquids.
**B. More aspiration and fewer pneumonias.** During testing, 53 percent aspirated with honey-thick liquid, compared with 63 percent with nectar-thick liquid and 68 percent with chin-down posture.
**C. Less aspiration and similar pneumonia rates.** Neither the pooled comparison with chin-down posture nor the comparison of the two viscosities showed a clear pneumonia advantage. Clinically important differences remained possible.
**D. More aspiration and similar pneumonia rates.** Similar follow-up rates are compatible with differences during testing, when honey-thick liquid produced the least aspiration.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 450. Logemann et al., JSLHR 2008, pp. 173–183 and Robbins et al., Ann Intern Med 2008, pp. 509–518.

q: A man with Parkinson disease and dysphagia is discussing tube feeding. Which explanation about aspiration pneumonia is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Postpyloric feeding is expected to produce a substantial reduction in pneumonia
Difficulty handling oral or gastric secretions remains an important source of aspiration
Most pneumonias during tube feeding result from aspiration of the feeding formula
Changing to tube feeding is expected to reduce the occurrence of aspiration
explanation:
Tube feeding can deliver nutrients around a swallowing problem, but it cannot prevent aspiration of the patient's own secretions. **Impaired handling of saliva or gastric secretions remains an important cause of pneumonia**.

**A. Large benefit from postpyloric feeding.** Postpyloric placement may produce a small reduction in pneumonia, not reliable large protection.
**B. Endogenous secretions.** Oropharyngeal dysfunction persists in Parkinson disease even when all nutrition is delivered by tube.
**C. Formula causes most pneumonia.** Aspirated endogenous secretions account for much of the risk.
**D. Tube feeding prevents aspiration.** Changing the feeding route does not restore coordinated swallowing or airway protection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 430.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: An 84-year-old man with macular degeneration and visual acuity 20/200 has fallen three times in two months. He lives alone and says he stopped taking medications because he cannot read the labels. His list includes metformin, lisinopril, tamsulosin, and zolpidem 10 mg for sleep. Blood pressure falls from 140/80 supine to 118/70 standing. During medication reconciliation and falls assessment, which paired plan addresses both the listed sedative exposure and the visual barrier to identifying medications?
o: Withdraw zolpidem and provide a medication organizer with usable nonvisual markers
Continue zolpidem and provide a medication organizer with usable nonvisual markers
Withdraw zolpidem and retain the small-print medication labels he cannot read
Continue zolpidem and retain the small-print medication labels he cannot read
explanation:
**Medication safety and visual access** are separate problems in this stem. Hazzard describes falls and confusion concerns with zolpidem-class hypnotics and includes medication organization and nonvisual strategies in low-vision rehabilitation (pp. 478–479, 659). "Concerns remain regarding the risks of falls, confusion, and fracture in older adults, particularly in those with frailty." (p. 659). Applying usable nonvisual markers to medication identification is an inference from those rehabilitation principles (pp. 478–479).

**A. Withdraw zolpidem and provide a medication organizer with usable nonvisual markers.** Correct, this addresses both the sedative exposure and inability to read labels; actual use and suitability of the aid must be established in the stated review (pp. 478–479, 659; application).
**B. Continue zolpidem and provide a medication organizer with usable nonvisual markers.** Wrong, the organizer addresses access, but continuing the listed hypnotic does not address its identified falls-related risk (pp. 478–479, 659).
**C. Withdraw zolpidem and retain the small-print medication labels he cannot read.** Wrong, removing the hypnotic addresses that exposure, but keeping unreadable labels leaves the medication-access problem unresolved (pp. 478–479, 659).
**D. Continue zolpidem and retain the small-print medication labels he cannot read.** Wrong, the plan leaves both the listed sedative exposure and the demonstrated visual barrier unchanged (pp. 478–479, 659).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 659, 478, 479.

q: A 78-year-old woman with diabetic retinopathy and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22) is hospitalized with cellulitis. Her vision has worsened over six months. Her daughter reports a cooking burn and reliance on sandwiches. She takes insulin glargine 20 units, furosemide 40 mg twice daily, and amlodipine 10 mg. Which assessment directly evaluates how vision affects the safety and performance of her daily tasks?
o: Administer a Montreal Cognitive Assessment as the functional vision evaluation.
Observe activities of daily living, including performance of kitchen tasks.
Use an eye-chart acuity measurement as the functional vision evaluation.
Administer a PHQ-9 depression screen as the functional vision evaluation.
explanation:
**Functional visual assessment** includes observing activities of daily living and instrumental activities affected by vision (p. 478). The table specifies: "Observe for ability to perform, ease and speed of performance, comfort and stress level, safety" (p. 478). Direct task observation therefore addresses the cooking difficulty without assuming that one test determines her overall ability to live independently.

**A. Administer a Montreal Cognitive Assessment as the functional vision evaluation.** Wrong, a cognitive score does not provide the task-performance and safety observations specified for this assessment (p. 478).
**B. Observe activities of daily living, including performance of kitchen tasks.** Correct, observed kitchen and other daily activities supply the performance and safety information specified by the table (p. 478).
**C. Use an eye-chart acuity measurement as the functional vision evaluation.** Wrong, an acuity measurement does not supply the separate observation of daily task performance and safety that the table requires (p. 478).
**D. Administer a PHQ-9 depression screen as the functional vision evaluation.** Wrong, a depression score does not provide the specified observations of vision-related task performance and safety (p. 478).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 478.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 478, Table 33-5

q: An 81-year-old man receiving eye care for macular degeneration still struggles to read newspapers and play cards. What should guide his vision rehabilitation plan?
o: His activity goals, supported by device training and environmental adaptations.
His chronological age, used to reduce the activities targeted for rehabilitation.
The purchase of a magnifier, used in place of a training program.
The visual acuity result, used in place of a functional activity assessment.
explanation:
Macular degeneration can compromise central detail while leaving the patient with usable vision. **Build the plan around his newspaper and card-playing goals**, then train him with aids and environmental adaptations.

**A. Activity goals.** Try the chosen devices on actual print and cards, adjusting lighting and contrast as needed.
**B. Chronological age.** Age alone says little about which activities he wants or can regain.
**C. Buy a magnifier.** Magnifier power, working distance and practice determine whether the purchase becomes useful.
**D. Acuity alone.** An acuity score cannot measure success at reading a newspaper or distinguishing cards during play.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 478–479.
ref: Hazzard Ch 33 — LOW VISION: ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION

q: אישה בת 76 עם גלאוקומה ואובדן שמיעה מתון דו-צדדי (עם מכשירי שמיעה) מגיעה לביקורת שגרתית. היא מציינת קושי בהבנת הוראות הרופא לגבי טיפות העיניים החדשות שלה. היא גרה לבדה ופספסה מספר תורים אחרונים. בבדיקה: חדות ראייה 20/40 OU עם פגמים בשדה הראייה. איזו אסטרטגיית תקשורת תשפר בצורה הטובה ביותר את ה-adherence הרפואי שלה?
o: לפנות אליה ישירות, לדבר בבהירות בעוצמת קול רגילה, ולתת הוראות כתובות בכתב גדול
לדבר בקול רם יותר ולאט יותר
לדאוג שהבת תגיע לכל הפגישות כמתרגמת
לעבור לתקשורת דרך אימייל בלבד
explanation:
**לפנות אליה ישירות, לדבר בבהירות בעוצמת קול רגילה, ולתת הוראות כתובות בכתב גדול**.

**א. לפנות אליה ישירות, לדבר בבהירות בעוצמת קול רגילה, ולתת הוראות כתובות בכתב גדול.** נכונה, התשובה הנכונה מתייחסת לפגיעה חושית כפולה (dual sensory impairment) באופן מקיף: פנייה ישירה לחולה מאפשרת קריאת שפתיים, עוצמת קול רגילה מתאימה למכשירי שמיעה (צעקה גורמת עיוות), וכתב גדול מותאם למגבלת הראייה ומספק חומר עזר לעיון בבית. Dual sensory impairment (DSI) משפיע על 20-30% מהמבוגרים מעל גיל 70 ומגביר באופן אקספוננציאלי את הסיכון ל-cognitive decline, דיכאון ו-medical non-adherence. התאמות פשוטות (פנייה ישירה לחולה, תאורה טובה, הוראות כתובות ומילוליות) משפרות משמעותית את ההבנה.
**ב. לדבר בקול רם יותר ולאט יותר.** שגויה, אפשרות של דיבור בקול רם יותר ולאט יותר היא המלכודת הקלאסית — אנשים נוטים אינסטינקטיבית לצעוק למשתמשי מכשירי שמיעה, אך הדבר גורם עיוות ו-feedback. מכשירי השמיעה מגבירים את הצליל; מה שנדרש הוא בהירות, לא עוצמה.
**ג. לדאוג שהבת תגיע לכל הפגישות כמתרגמת.** שגויה, האפשרות של הבת כמתרגמת פוגעת באוטונומיה ואינה פרקטית לניהול תרופות בין ביקורים.
**ד. לעבור לתקשורת דרך אימייל בלבד.** שגויה, האפשרות של אימייל בלבד מתעלמת מכך שפגיעת הראייה מקשה על קריאה במסך, ומסירה רמזי תקשורת non-verbal חשובים.

מקור: Hazzard Ch 34 — HEARING LOSS: ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT
ref: Hazzard Ch 34 — HEARING LOSS: ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT

q: An 85-year-old woman with macular degeneration has difficulty reading and identifying objects in her room. Which pair of low-vision adaptations matches the purposes described in Hazzard?
o: Task lighting for reading and contrasting markings on step edges.
Task lighting for reading and markings that match the step color.
Dim lighting for reading and contrasting markings on step edges.
Dim lighting for reading and markings that match the step color.
explanation:
